TWO HONEST CEILINGS that must be in the step text: integer-millisecond resolution, and the fact that no TEST_ASSERTION_KINDS entry is timing-shaped (roster.py:404-409), so the Test closes on the body_equals half and the measurement rides as the supporting edge. Distinct from the refused single-packet timing attack, which needs packet-level control this contract has none of.  FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. Its differential lives in a request BODY -- both series are login POSTs, and the measurement is over their Receipts. A Test action carries only {ordinal, role, kind, method, url} (roster.py:1184-1197), _Door.send passes only url and method to proxy.spend (replay.py:342-351) although proxy.spend accepts headers and body (proxy.py:4216-4224), and record_test_action compares a Receipt to an action over method, scheme, host, port and path alone (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1386-1391). So neither arm is expressible as a Test action and close_test_replay never sees this pair. close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125) is the ONLY writer of a testing->supported hypothesis_transitions row -- its to_status is v_means.settles from rk2_test_outcome (20260815T000000Z...:113-114) -- and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the Test run being cited (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649). The agent-filed Observation IS a real hypothesis_evidence edge -- rk2_promote_hypotheses writes edges from agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530) -- and that edge is the whole of what this reading produces. REFUTATION IS ONE-SIDED THE SAME WAY: rk2_test_outcome maps 'refutes' to settles='refuted' too, so close_test_replay is also the only writer of testing->refuted, and this reading's refutation is an Observation rather than a settled verdict.  THE CEILING IS PRICED AND OWED, NOT PERMANENT -- see owner_ticket. TICKET 211 ('A Test action carries the header and the body it plans', docs/specs/production-harness-v2/issues/211-a-test-action-carries-the-header-and-the-body-it-plans.md) removes exactly this rule, is Blocked by: nothing, is ready-for-agent, and ticket 101's own Blocked by line already names it. The price is small because the two expensive halves already exist: proxy.spend accepts a header mapping and a body today (proxy.py:4216-4224), and receipts.request_agent_sha already stores the agent-view request message (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:59), so binding a plan to what was sent needs no new column. What is owed is rk2_test_spec_problem's action key set widening from five keys to seven (20260815T000000Z...:377), two keyword arguments in _Door.send (replay.py:342-351), two Arguments in the roster action element (roster.py:1184-1197), the header and body comparison in record_test_action (20260815T000000Z...:1383-1396), and the decision about what a read_only Playbook may put in a body (_body_allowed, execution.py:3646). SO THE PLAYBOOK PROSE MUST NOT BE WRITTEN TWICE: 00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:31-33 records the ordering this repo already chose -- 'This is why the order is harness first. Adding state-of-the-art techniques to steps that cannot be executed would multiply the unrunnable part of the catalogue' -- and 211 says in as many words that writing 'this step stops at an Observation' into a third of the corpus would be 'a catalogue that describes attacks it cannot grade'.  The previous statement of this row was already half-right -- it said the invariance half came from close_test_replay and the timing half from the agent. The first half is now withdrawn: close_test_replay cannot run on two body-carrying login attempts, so BOTH halves are the agent's. Two honest ceilings stay: integer-millisecond resolution, and no Finding.  D3 (operator decision, rewrite/DECISIONS.md): a property class with no emitter is neither a missing execution path nor missing evidence, so capability_state stays 'reachable' and owner_ticket is 101 -- ticket 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs, so the gap closes inside it.

technique: Establish sequentially that a single-use action really is single, by spending it once, reading the target's own counter, sending the identical action again after the first has answered, and reading the counter again.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, json_request, state_changing_method, plus a route that STATES the count afterwards -- a balance, a redemption list, a remaining quota. Without a counter this Playbook has nothing to read and does not apply. One Identity label held through use-identity for every call; two labels would make it a question about two accounts, which is a different class.
baseline: The pristine count, read before anything is sent. bb:baseline is pristine_surface because the whole claim is arithmetic on this number, and a number another Playbook moved in between is one this reading cannot use.
variant: The identical action sent a second time after the first answered, then the counter read again.
control: Two. (a) The first send plus its counter read, which must show the action landed exactly once -- that is the state_change against the pristine count. (b) An action value of the same shape that was never issued, which must be refused; without it a second success is consistent with an endpoint that accepts anything. Where the control shows the action is repeatable by design, stop: there is no invariant, so there is nothing for a concurrent pair to break.
payload_family: one single-use value the Task's Identity legitimately holds, submitted twice in sequence
runtime_writer: promote_proposal -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (the live CREATE OR REPLACE; the INSERT INTO observations with the kind the agent named is at :1116-1123, and the 20260814T070000Z definition 65 ledger rows cited is superseded) -- the agent files state_change (evidential, allowed_provenance {receipt}, src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:229) citing the COUNTER READ's Receipt, which is the later request that sees the side effect, and the edge onto the Hypothesis is rk2_promote_hypotheses -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530 (INSERT INTO hypothesis_evidence from an agent-supplied observation_id, no filter on the cited kind). Whether close_test_replay also has a citation here depends on the carrier: see notes. Where the single-use value rides the request line it is close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125)
supported_evidence: state_change x2, agent-filed, which is this Playbook's own declared bar (bb:evidence names state_change for both the control and the variant). The Receipt each cites is the COUNTER READ, not the action's own Receipt. response_differential closes the Test ONLY where the single-use value rides the request line -- see notes; this Playbook's bb:triggers_all names json_request, so the default carrier is a body and the default answer is that it does not.
refuted_evidence: state_change with refuting polarity: the counter is unmoved between the two reads, which is what a correctly consumed single-use value looks like. response_invariant carries it only under the request-line carrier.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the counter after the second submission, whichever way it moved | 2 course of action: stop at two submissions; do not drain a balance and do not go looking for a third item | 3 scope of halt: the route and the one item spent | 4 resume condition: the Program offers a second unspent item of the same kind for the concurrent reading, and an operator has authorised the spend | 5 who is told: the operator, through the Finding the closed Test opens, and in the report which names the item consumed | 6 what is recorded: the item spent by name, the pristine count, the count after each submission, and where the target offers a restore route, that the count was restored [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
owner_ticket: NEW: pass `headers` and `body` from the Test specification through `_Door.send` (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) to `proxy.spend`, which already accepts both -- roughly four lines and one new replay test, no column and no migration, because the Receipt already hashes the whole message. Until it lands this row is a lead the Test lane cannot grade, not a procedure.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. The differential is a request BODY (the single-use value rides a JSON request body, which is what this Playbook's bb:triggers_all `json_request` declares). `_Door.send` (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else -- no `headers=`, no `body=` -- although `proxy.spend` accepts both, and `record_test_action` (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1386-1391) compares a Receipt to an action over method, scheme, host, port and path alone. The replay lane sends no body at all, so a Test action of this row would reach the target as a bodyless request and would not be this reading. `close_test_replay` (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125) is the only writer of a `testing -> supported` hypothesis transition, and `rk2_finding_refusal` (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-650) will not open a Finding without one joined to the very Test run being cited. The Observation an agent files still lands on the Hypothesis as a real evidence edge -- `rk2_promote_hypotheses` (src/redkraken/migrations/20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) writes `hypothesis_evidence` from an agent-supplied `observation_id` with no filter on the cited kind -- but it cannot carry the claim to `supported`. THE CARRIER IS THE WHOLE QUESTION and the Playbook should say so: where the route accepts the single-use value in the PATH or the QUERY (POST /redeem/<code>, ?code=...), both submissions are Test actions, close_test_replay derives response_differential, and the row reaches a Finding. Where it rides a JSON body -- the shipped trigger -- the replay lane would send a bodyless POST, which is not this reading, so the claim rests on the agent-filed state_change pair and stops at an Observation. Note this is NOT the concurrency wall: the sequential reading executes perfectly through mcp__rk2__http_request either way, and race-conditions is bb:effects mutates_object so _body_allowed is true for it. This is the half of business_logic.replay the harness can actually reach, and the Playbook's step 3 makes it mandatory before anything concurrent. The attached reference names the three things it rules out: the action was never single-use, the second copy was accepted because a session or cart refreshed between them, and the counter does not mean what the report assumed because some counters are eventually consistent. Effects are mutates_object and there is no cleanup -- saying so before execution rather than after is the point. PRICE OF THIS WALL, because a wall written into a card without its price is the decision to keep it, made silently. The egress is NOT the limit: `proxy.spend` (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4227) already accepts `headers=` and `body=`, and `_Door.send` (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) simply does not pass them, from the one call site that exists (`_sent`, src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466), out of a request mapping it already holds verbatim. No column and no migration are needed: `receipts.request_agent_sha` and `request_wire_sha` (src/redkraken/migrations/0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:21-22) have hashed the whole message -- start line, headers and body -- since 005, because `proxy.transcript` (src/redkraken/proxy.py:878-887) builds exactly those bytes, and ticket 96 says so in as many words and refuses a second digest of them (src/redkraken/migrations/20260924T000000Z__a_request_may_carry_a_body.sql:10-17). The body PERMISSION already binds correctly at the door for every non-browser tool including this one (src/redkraken/migrations/20260924T000000Z__a_request_may_carry_a_body.sql:255-262), and the approval question is already answered -- a body-bearing Tool run is `reusable: false`, so one human approval covers one Task (same file, :44-66). A spec action carrying the extra keys is not refused today either: rk2_test_request_problem's own COMMENT says 'Key sets are the caller''s business' (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1430-1433). So the price is roughly four lines in one Python function plus a new replay test -- no test constructs `_Door` today -- and the whole header-borne and body-borne family moves onto the Finding path unchanged. What this does NOT remove, correctly, is the separate `%2e` and dot-segment refusal at src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:222-226, whose reason is that scope is stated over resolved paths.

preconditions: A passed sequential control from the row above, a second unspent item, and a primitive that releases two requests at once. The third does not exist: mcp__rk2__http_request is one call returning one response and there is no batch or parallel argument; mcp__rk2__browse is 1..32 ORDERED steps and no member of its twelve-action enum releases anything concurrently. Role max_concurrent in src/redkraken/roster.py is run scheduling, and it is clamped to free Identity leases on purpose (clamp_to_identity_leases), because two hunters sharing one upstream slot is the session mixing the Identity model exists to prevent -- so two runs cannot even stand in for one slot's concurrent pair.
baseline: Not runnable as written. The sequential submission, which the row above covers.
variant: Not runnable. Two identical copies of the action released simultaneously through the same slot, with the counter read after.
control: Not runnable, and this is the part most reports omit: two simultaneous submissions of DISTINCT valid items, which must legitimately credit twice. Without it a multiplied count does not distinguish a race from correct behaviour.
payload_family: two identical state-changing requests released in one window
runtime_writer: None is reached. Were the primitive to exist the shape is ordinary: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125) for the differential and promote_proposal -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (the live CREATE OR REPLACE; the INSERT INTO observations with the kind the agent named is at :1116-1123, and the 20260814T070000Z definition 65 ledger rows cited is superseded) for the state_change edges.
supported_evidence: response_differential, once a release primitive exists. The evidence shape is fine; the release is what is missing.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, on the same condition -- the count after the pair moves exactly as far as the sequential control's single success, whatever the two responses said.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): a Playbook step asks for two requests in flight at once | 2 course of action: record it blocked and stop at the sequential control, reporting that instead; do not read a passed replay test as a passed race test | 3 scope of halt: every route: this is a property of the tool contracts, not of any target | 4 resume condition: a concurrent-release primitive lands with its own budget and Halt accounting | 5 who is told: whoever re-proposes it, through this ledger row | 6 what is recorded: that the missing capability is a release primitive, and the two preconditions worth carrying to whoever builds it -- a per-session lock serialises same-session requests so a real exploit needs distinct app-level sessions, and the multithreading comes from the web server's workers rather than the language [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
owner_ticket: NEW: a bounded concurrent-release primitive (exactly two requests, one window, one Identity slot) so the shipped race-conditions Playbook's step 4 becomes executable
notes: This is the honest headline for this group: the shipped Playbook's own step 4 is not executable today, and the Playbook does not say so. Two shards found it independently and both were right -- this is NOT one of the corrections, it is a real wall. The reference's own note is worth carrying into the Playbook: failing with two to ten requests does not prove a target is safe, which is exactly why a Playbook must not claim safety from a replay that merely succeeded once.

technique: Read a secret or an account's existence off how long a response takes rather than off what it says.

preconditions: A route whose duration varies with the value under test. The measurement exists: Receipts carry ts_arrival, ts_egress and waited_ms (src/redkraken/migrations/0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:56-58), and timing_differential is evidential with allowed_provenance {receipt} (src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:222-223).
baseline: The route answered for a value certain not to exist, sent repeatedly.
variant: The same route answered for a value certain to exist.
control: The same route answered for a syntactically invalid value, which separates 'unknown' from 'bad input' -- and, because a duration is noisy, the two identical sends of the baseline are what say a difference is not the clock.
payload_family: repeated identical requests differing only in the identifier
runtime_writer: promote_proposal -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (the live CREATE OR REPLACE; the INSERT INTO observations with the kind the agent named is at :1116-1123, and the 20260814T070000Z definition 65 ledger rows cited is superseded) files timing_differential from a Receipt (evidential, allowed_provenance {receipt}, src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:223); the edge onto the Hypothesis is rk2_promote_hypotheses -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530 (INSERT INTO hypothesis_evidence from an agent-supplied observation_id, no filter on the cited kind). No Test-lane writer produces it, because TEST_ASSERTION_KINDS (src/redkraken/roster.py:404, and rk2_test_assertion_kinds at src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:184-186) holds nothing time-shaped.
supported_evidence: Neither. timing_differential carries it, and it is filable -- the mined rows that called it writer-less were reading an earlier card. What it cannot do is CLOSE a Test, because close_test_replay derives only the two response kinds and a Finding needs a closed Test.
refuted_evidence: Neither, for the same reason.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the two identifier classes separate by a margin the repeated baseline sends say is not the clock, or they do not | 2 course of action: stop at detection and file the timing_differential; do not turn a duration into an enumeration run | 3 scope of halt: the route under test | 4 resume condition: a Playbook that owns information_disclosure.identifier_oracle takes the reading, which ticket 101 is what would create | 5 who is told: the operator, in the Task record and the routing note | 6 what is recorded: every Receipt label with its waited_ms, the identifier class each carried, and that no Test closed because no assertion kind is time-shaped [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
owner_ticket: 101 -- ticket 101 is the ticket that edits `bb:outputs`, and the only thing missing is a Playbook permitted to emit information_disclosure.identifier_oracle. Separately and not closed by 101: no assertion kind is time-shaped, so this reading can never close a Test whoever owns it.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the ceiling is timing, which ticket 211 does not touch. The ceiling paragraph below still holds. RE-STATED from out_of_scope to reachable under operator decision D3: a missing EMITTER is neither a missing execution path nor missing evidence the Runtime can write, and ticket 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs, so the gap closes inside this ticket. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION. Not because of a carrier this time but because no assertion kind is time-shaped: rk2_test_assertion_kinds is exactly status_equals, status_differs, body_equals, body_differs (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:184-186), so close_test_replay has nothing to settle a duration with, and `close_test_replay` (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125) is the only writer of a `testing -> supported` hypothesis transition, and `rk2_finding_refusal` (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-650) will not open a Finding without one joined to the very Test run being cited. That wall is NOT priced away by the headers-and-body change the other rows name -- it is a different and larger one, a new assertion kind with its own determinism argument, which is why it keeps its own sentence here. Two things were both wrong in the mining and both matter. First, timing_differential is not writer-less: promote_proposal files it and Receipts carry the measurement (ts_arrival, ts_egress, waited_ms, src/redkraken/migrations/0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:56-58). Second, it is still not race-conditions' own claim -- references/race-conditions-and-timing-attacks.md exists to make exactly that split, and keeping them apart is what step 5 of the Playbook is for. The v1 pack put the race, user enumeration by timing and exfiltration by timing in one folder because a stopwatch is involved in all four, and that is the only thing they have in common.
finding_path_note: the ceiling is timing, which ticket 211 does not touch

technique: Shrink the arrival window to a single scheduling tick by synchronising the last bytes or the last frames of several requests, so a limit check and its commit can be straddled.

control: Not runnable.

runtime_writer: None.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, read_method, url_valued_parameter, and a confirmed sink from the sink-discovery row. The ^https?:// pattern on mcp__rk2__http_request constrains OUR request target, never the string placed in the application's parameter.
baseline: http:// against the controlled host, which works, sent twice unchanged.
variant: ftp:// and then dict:// against the same controlled authority -- one scheme per request, the authority never changing.
control: Two. (a) The two identical baseline sends. (b) rk-probe://<controlled-host>/, a scheme no client library implements, whose failure gives the shape of 'unsupported' so it can be told apart from 'rejected by policy'.
payload_family: one non-http scheme per request, authority fixed to a host the Program controls
runtime_writer: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125); the supporting error_detail edge is written by promote_proposal -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (the live CREATE OR REPLACE; the INSERT INTO observations with the kind the agent named is at :1116-1123, and the 20260814T070000Z definition 65 ledger rows cited is superseded)
supported_evidence: response_differential -- body_differs between the ftp/dict arm and the unimplemented-scheme control, both carried in our query string, so the Test closes on the request line. The library's message naming the scheme is filed alongside as error_detail (evidential, allowed_provenance {receipt,tool_run}, src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:227) and cited as a supporting hypothesis_evidence edge.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every scheme including the invented one produces one answer, so the route validates the scheme before it fetches.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the first scheme the fetcher acts on, or all arms matching the unimplemented-scheme control | 2 course of action: stop at that scheme; do not turn an accepted gopher or dict into a command to whatever is behind it | 3 scope of halt: the route under test | 4 resume condition: an operator authorises a scheme aimed somewhere other than the two declared names | 5 who is told: the operator, through the Finding the closed Test opens | 6 what is recorded: the scheme list actually sent, in order, and the Artifact label for each [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
notes: FINDING PATH: this row IS on it. The whole differential lives in the request line -- which scheme prefixes the controlled authority inside the parameter value -- which is what a Test action carries, so `close_test_replay` derives `response_differential` from the Test's own assertions (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1063-1070) and writes the `testing -> supported` transition `rk2_finding_refusal` requires. Spelling constraint the Test lane imposes: `rk2_test_request_problem` (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:222-226) refuses any specification url that carries a `.` or `..` PATH SEGMENT or the literal `%2e` anywhere at all, so every arm of this row leaves dots unencoded and spells no dot segment. Note the door itself would forward them verbatim (`origin_form()`, src/redkraken/proxy.py:818-828) -- the refusal is the Test lane's, not the egress's. Corrects a mined 'blocked'. pd-web-b3 filed this blocked because error_detail was said to have no runtime writer; it does -- promote_proposal inserts the observations row with the kind the agent named and the element lists are deliberately open (src/redkraken/roster.py:1356-1370). Even without that edge the row closes on the differential alone. The file:// arm is NOT in this row: it names the target's own filesystem, which is a host on the target's side of the boundary, and step 7 refuses it.

preconditions: None that may be met. Needs an authoritative nameserver for a domain we operate, TTL control, and a timing window inside the target's resolver cache.
baseline: Not runnable.
variant: Not runnable.
control: Not runnable, and this is the substantive half of the refusal: a rebinding failure may mean the validator and the fetcher share one resolution or may mean a resolver cached, and a refutation that cannot mean one thing is not a control.
payload_family: a low-TTL A record flipping between a permitted and an internal address
runtime_writer: None.
supported_evidence: None available.
refuted_evidence: None available -- see the control field: the technique's refutation is not interpretable.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the technique is proposed | 2 course of action: record it refused with the reason attached and do not substitute a public rebinding service, which routes the target's DNS through a third party nobody in the engagement chose | 3 scope of halt: every route | 4 resume condition: an operator stands up a zone under the Program's own control and authorises it in writing; that is not something a reading does mid-flight | 5 who is told: whoever re-proposes it, through this ledger row | 6 what is recorded: that the refusal is the authoritative-zone requirement and the race, not the SSRF [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
owner_ticket: NEW: none is planned -- record the refusal permanently rather than opening a ticket for a capability the corpus has decided against
notes: Refused by decision on two counts from the card: registering or claiming a third-party resource, and a technique that needs a machine-in-the-middle-shaped position between two resolutions. references/dns-rebinding.md keeps the idea underneath it, which is this Playbook's whole subject: the check and the fetch are two reads of one URL and a defect exists wherever they disagree. Rebinding makes them disagree about DNS; userinfo and the redirect make them disagree in ways two Program-owned hosts can demonstrate. The reference also records the trap: a rebinding 'success' usually rests on the resolver log, which makes the question injection.request_forgery and the Playbook webhooks.

technique: Count the decoding passes that stand between the validator and the fetcher, by encoding one reserved character in the controlled authority once, twice and three times and reading at which depth the value stops being rejected and starts being fetched.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, read_method, url_valued_parameter, a confirmed sink, and a route whose refusal is visible in the response. jq through mcp__rk2__run_tool does the encoding offline, so the string that goes out is one the run can show it built.
baseline: The literal controlled-host URL, refused (or fetched) exactly as it is, sent twice unchanged.
variant: The same URL with the reserved character encoded once, then twice, then three times -- one request per depth, nothing else changed. The reserved character is `@`, `#`, `?` or `/` (`%40`/`%2540`/`%252540`, `%23`/`%2523`, `%3f`/`%253f`, `%2f`/`%252f`), never `.`.
control: Two. (a) The two identical baseline sends. (b) An encoded value at the same depth that decodes to something harmless on the same controlled host, which shows the decoding happened rather than the filter having merely missed a longer string.
payload_family: single, double and triple percent-encoding of one reserved character inside a controlled-host URL
runtime_writer: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125)
supported_evidence: response_differential -- body_differs between the depth that is refused and the depth that is fetched, both naming the same authority.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every depth answers the same way, so one decode sits between the caller and the fetcher and the checker saw what the fetcher saw.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the first depth at which the answer changes | 2 course of action: stop at that depth; report the count, do not go looking for a fourth layer | 3 scope of halt: the route under test | 4 resume condition: an operator asks for a deeper reading | 5 who is told: the operator, through the Finding the closed Test opens | 6 what is recorded: the exact string sent at each depth, the jq run that built it, and the Artifact label of each answer [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
notes: FINDING PATH: this row IS on it. The whole differential lives in the request line -- how many encoding layers wrap one reserved character inside the parameter value -- which is what a Test action carries, so `close_test_replay` derives `response_differential` from the Test's own assertions (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1063-1070) and writes the `testing -> supported` transition `rk2_finding_refusal` requires. ONE SPELLING CONSTRAINT, and it is load-bearing: the ladder may not be built on the DOT. rk2_test_request_problem (src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:224) refuses any specification url matching `%2e` case-insensitively in any position, so the first rung of a dot-encoding ladder is refused while `%252e` and deeper pass -- the substring `%2e` is not present in `%252e` -- and a depth ladder missing its first rung is not this reading. Every other reserved character survives every depth. Where a route's confusion genuinely needs the dot, the reading still executes through mcp__rk2__http_request and stops at an agent-filed Observation. HIGH VALUE for injection.parser_differential, one of the nine unemitted classes. 'How many decodes are between me and the sink' is a reading, not a payload list, and it is the thing that decides whether every later confusion lands. Distinct from the authority-position row: that one is about where the host ends, this one is about how many times the string is read.

technique: Drive the fetcher through a chain of escalating 3xx status codes so its error path prints the whole chain and the final body it would otherwise have hidden.

preconditions: A responder we control that emits a chosen SEQUENCE of status codes across roughly ten hops. Nothing in the tool contracts serves one: mcp__rk2__http_request only makes requests, and the recorded out-of-band channel receives arrivals -- it is not a programmable HTTP responder.
baseline: Not runnable. Would be the fetcher pointed at a single 302, answering with an opaque error and no body.
variant: Not runnable. Would be a chain incrementing through 301, 302 ... 305 and beyond before landing on the destination.
control: Not runnable. Would be the same chain landing on a harmless 200 on a controlled host, proving the chain and not the destination unlocked the body.
payload_family: a scripted redirect chain of chosen status codes
runtime_writer: None today. Were the responder to exist, the shape is ordinary: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125)
supported_evidence: response_differential, once the responder exists -- the shape is fine and it is the responder that is missing.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, on the same condition.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the row is proposed with a step that assumes a responder | 2 course of action: record it blocked and name the missing capability rather than substituting the callback channel, which cannot choose a status code | 3 scope of halt: every route that would use a chosen-response redirector | 4 resume condition: the out-of-band channel gains a scriptable responder | 5 who is told: whoever re-proposes it, through this ledger row | 6 what is recorded: that the gap is one capability -- a redirector under our control with chosen status codes and Location values [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
owner_ticket: NEW: give the recorded out-of-band channel a bounded scriptable responder (chosen status code and Location) so redirect-chain and redirect-following readings become executable
notes: Three shards found this independently and all three called it the most valuable blocked row, because the missing capability is small and well defined and unlocks a family rather than a technique. Ranked #3 in PortSwigger's Top 10 of 2025. Distinguish it from the redirect-chain row above, which is reachable precisely because it uses the TARGET's own redirector and does not need a chosen status code.

technique: Establish that the parameter is dereferenced at all before any confusion is spent on it, by separating an answer the route composed from a document it fetched -- with no correlator and no out-of-band anything.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, read_method, and a parameter enumerate-surface typed as url_valued_parameter, or an opaque query_parameter that jq decodes to a URL offline (a base64 blob that decodes to a URL is not opaque and inherits every reading that applies to what it decodes to).
baseline: The parameter set to an ordinary allowed URL, sent twice unchanged: the shape of an answer that carries a fetched document.
variant: The parameter set to a Program-controlled host on a path that certainly answers, then on a path on the same host that certainly 404s. Two different answers mean the value was dereferenced and the fetch outcome reached the caller.
control: Two. (a) The two identical baseline sends. (b) The parameter set to a string that is not a URL at all ('rk-not-a-url'): if that produces the SAME answer as the 404 path, the parameter is being validated and not fetched, and this candidate is out.
payload_family: sink discovery -- one allowed URL, two paths on a controlled host, one non-URL string; and, as a named arm that does NOT run here, the SOAP/WSDL spelling in which the dereferenced value is a service-contract URL carried in a request body
runtime_writer: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125)
supported_evidence: response_differential -- body_differs between the answering path and the 404 path on the same controlled host.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the fetch outcome does not reach the caller, which is the commonest inconclusive in this class and is not an invitation to reach further.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): the sink is identified, or the non-URL control answers the same way the 404 path did | 2 course of action: hand the confirmed sink to the parser rows; where the control matched, drop the candidate and say so | 3 scope of halt: this parameter, not the route and not the run | 4 resume condition: a different candidate parameter is named by the Task | 5 who is told: the operator, in the Task record; nothing is proposed from this step alone | 6 what is recorded: the three Artifact labels and which candidate parameters were dropped [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
notes: FINDING PATH: this row IS on it. The whole differential lives in the request line -- which path on the controlled host the parameter value names, inside our query string -- which is what a Test action carries, so `close_test_replay` derives `response_differential` from the Test's own assertions (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1063-1070) and writes the `testing -> supported` transition `rk2_finding_refusal` requires. WSDL ARM, added on a critic hand-off from g03 and carried here rather than lost: researchers.json:34 files 'a request parameter that names the WSDL the server will go and fetch' as BLOCKED, on the old and wrong reading that record_callback_interaction writes no evidence edge. The mechanism is the same question this row asks -- is the value dereferenced -- and the correction is that its detection half is an ARRIVAL and an arrival IS evidential (callback_interaction, is_evidential true, allowed_provenance {callback}, src/redkraken/migrations/20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:349). Two things keep it an arm and not a row of its own: the WSDL URL rides a SOAP request BODY, so it does not run in a read_only Task (_body_allowed, src/redkraken/execution.py:3646) and it does not reach a Finding; and serving a crafted WSDL back needs the responder the redirect-chain row names as missing. Rewritten from the mined form. Every mined version of this row uses http://127.0.0.1:1/ as the dead-port discriminator, which this Playbook's step 7 refuses outright; a Program-controlled host with an answering path and a 404 path is the same three-way reading inside the ceiling. Keep this row separate from the parser rows: 'is it a sink' and 'do the two readers agree' are two questions with two different fixes.

technique: Make a renderer honour an engine-private element that names a local path -- mPDF's <annotation file=...>, PD4ML's <pd4ml:attachment src=...> -- so the produced document carries the file back.

preconditions: None that can be met for the PROOF. The submission itself is expressible (a request body on a Task whose selection is above read_only) and the produced document comes back and is stored; what is missing is a reader for it.
baseline: Not runnable as a proof. Would be the same element naming a path that does not exist.
variant: Not runnable as a proof. Would be the same element naming a benign local path.
control: Not runnable as a proof. Would be the element with an http(s) src pointed at the declared channel, which must arrive, so a failed file leg is about the scheme and not about the element being stripped.
payload_family: mPDF annotation, PD4ML attachment, and frame elements carrying a file scheme
runtime_writer: None. The claim 'this produced document contains that file' is a content_match, whose allowed_provenance is {tool_run} ALONE (src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:233) and whose four binaries are exactly jq, js_map, js_parse and js_routes (src/redkraken/migrations/20260814T050000Z__source_becomes_a_grounded_conclusion.sql:439-449). None reads a PDF, and the browse-run exception does not help: a browse run satisfies {tool_run}, but the browser lane's twelve actions have no step that reads a stored binary artifact either.
supported_evidence: None available.
refuted_evidence: None available. A body_differs between the existing-path and missing-path arms is expressible in principle but the produced document differs on every render -- timestamps, object ids -- so the differential is not the file.
stop_conditions: 1 halt trigger (observed condition): a step proposes proving a claim about the CONTENTS of a produced binary document | 2 course of action: record it blocked and name the missing reader; do not substitute a body_differs over two renders, because a renderer's output differs on every render | 3 scope of halt: every route -- this is a property of the offline tool set, not of any target | 4 resume condition: an offline binary that reads the document format lands | 5 who is told: whoever re-proposes it, through this ledger row | 6 what is recorded: that the technique works, the harness sees the answer, and there is no kind to file it under [shape per NIST SP 800-115 App B s3.2]
owner_ticket: NEW: a fifth offline binary that reads a stored non-JavaScript artifact (a PDF or an office document) and reports whether a declared pattern is present, so content_match has a reader for the documents the door already stores
notes: The half of the renderer family that stays blocked, split out on a critic finding so it does not share a verdict with the arrival arm. The miner filed it blocked on 'content_match has no runtime writer', which is wrong -- promote_proposal files it (promote_proposal -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (the live CREATE OR REPLACE; the INSERT INTO observations with the kind the agent named is at :1116-1123, and the 20260814T070000Z definition 65 ledger rows cited is superseded)) -- but the row is still blocked on a NARROWER wall the correction does not touch: content_match takes {tool_run} alone, and none of the four binaries reads a PDF. That is a real cost of the offline tool set and it is worth a ticket, because the door already stores the document.

technique: Make the checker and the fetcher disagree about which URL is being fetched at all, by giving the parameter an allowed URL on the target's own redirector whose Location names a Program-controlled host, so validation runs before the hop and the fetcher follows it.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, read_method, url_valued_parameter, plus redirect_target on a host the route already allows. redirect_target is a registered surface fact (src/redkraken/migrations/0032_playbooks.sql:66, recomputed from a redirects_to relationship on every subject_facts rebuild) that no shipped Playbook lists in any trigger set. The redirector must be the target's own -- hosting a second origin is refused by decision, so the hop cannot come from us.
baseline: The parameter set to the allowed host's own redirector pointing at another allowed path, sent twice unchanged. The response carrying that path's content is what proves redirects are followed at all, and the two sends are what prove the answer is byte-stable.
variant: The same redirector, its destination parameter set to controlled-host-a, then to controlled-host-b: two arms whose only difference is which marked document the hop lands on.
control: Two. (a) The two identical baseline sends. (b) The parameter set directly to a controlled host with no redirector in the string, which must be REFUSED -- that is what shows the redirector and not a permissive allowlist is doing the work.
payload_family: an allowed-host URL whose response is a 3xx to a Program-controlled authority
runtime_writer: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test spec at :1063-1070; the testing -> supported transition at :1125)

refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two arms answer identically against a stable baseline, meaning the allowlist is re-applied after the hop or the fetcher does not follow 3xx.

What the corpus is missing here is the control, not the jailbreak. Most reports of this shape name the successful framing and never establish that the framing is what moved the boundary. `agentic-ai` declares `bb:effects: read_only`, and `_body_allowed` (`src/redkraken/execution.py:3646`) opens a Task whose WHOLE Playbook selection is read_only with `body_allowed: false`. Where the boundary question rides a `query_parameter` the two framings are two urls and the row reaches a Finding on the shape above. Where it rides a JSON body -- the ordinary shape of a chat endpoint -- STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION, NOT A FINDING. The difference here is a request BODY, and no Test action can carry one: an action's key set is exactly `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), a setup or cleanup step's is exactly `('method','url')` (`:346`), and `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` only although `proxy.spend` accepts `headers=` and `body=` (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`, `src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224`). Setup runs as ONE block before every action and cleanup as ONE block after (`src/redkraken/replay.py:390`, `:425`) and neither is evidence (`:432-452`), so a body- or header-borne change cannot even be interleaved between two read-back actions. `close_test_replay` is the only writer of a `testing -> supported` hypothesis transition (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`, `:1127-1131`) and `rk2_finding_refusal` opens no Finding without one (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). Say which of the two the run is in before the Test is written.

technique: Text the caller stores in an ordinary application field is later concatenated into a model prompt, so the instruction's author and the model's principal are different people; the reading is whether the pipeline separates retrieved data from instructions.

preconditions: `tech_llm` on the application, plus `body_parameter` or `query_parameter` on the storing route; a surface where our stored content becomes the model's input; a retrieval trigger we can invoke ourselves; exactly one channel per run.
baseline: Store a plainly worded item, then invoke the summarisation trigger three times and store every answer. Three, not one: `references/llm.md` makes the baseline a set because a model produces differing answers to identical input by design.
variant: Store one item whose text carries an inert directive asking for a fixed nonce marker in a fixed position, then invoke the same trigger three times. Exactly one field changed against the baseline item.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: the same directive planted where the pipeline drops it -- an ignored header, an unused parameter, a discarded document part -- which must stay invariant against the baseline set, or the step-4 difference is not the channel's.
payload_family: inert directive text carrying a nonce marker, planted in stored user content -- never an instruction to act, store or send
runtime_writer: replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` -- the kind comes from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action a `body_differs`/`status_differs` assertion names closes `response_differential`, one none names closes `response_invariant` (roster.py:404). The variant action carries the `body_differs` assertion, the control action none; the marker's return is a separate `reflected_input` edge (provenance `{receipt,tool_run}`) filed at execution.py:518. The live definition of `promote_proposal` is `20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487` and its `observations` INSERT is at `:1116-1123`; the `20260814T070000Z...:1631` site earlier ledger passes cited is superseded and behaviourally identical.
supported_evidence: `response_differential` on the variant, which is the kind the Playbook's `bb:evidence` row for `to_status=supported, role=variant` already names; the marker appears in the variant set and in none of the baseline or control answers, and the write-up cites the counts.
refuted_evidence: `response_invariant` on the variant across every repeat, against a control that was itself invariant -- the Playbook's `to_status=refuted, role=variant` row.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: the three baseline sends already differ among themselves the way step 5 would call a finding. (2) action: record the variance and stop; do not raise the repeat count to resolve an ambiguous set. (3) scope: this route on this application, not the run. (4) resume: a later Task at a stated lower temperature, or another channel on the same application. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the baseline and control Artifacts, the stored item's id so it can be removed, and that model variance, not the injection, decided the answer.

notes: HIGH VALUE within an existing Playbook: indirect injection is usually assumed to need attacker-hosted content, and it does not when the application itself stores the content the model reads back. `agentic-ai` declares `bb:effects: read_only`, and `_body_allowed` (`src/redkraken/execution.py:3646`) opens a Task whose WHOLE Playbook selection is read_only with `body_allowed: false`. So on an agentic-ai-only Task the planting request may not carry a body at all and the channel has to be the `query_parameter` the Playbook's own `bb:triggers_any` already names; a body-borne channel needs the Task's selection to include a Playbook that is not read_only, and even then the planting is setup and not a Test action. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding. Its differential between two Test actions lives in the query or path segment naming WHICH stored item the retrieval trigger is asked to summarise -- the two Test actions are `GET <trigger>?id=<clean>` and `GET <trigger>?id=<planted>`, and the planting itself happens before the replay opens rather than inside it, which is exactly what a Test action carries: an action's key set is `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`), and `record_test_action` compares method, scheme, host, port and path (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`) -- the query rides the url and is deliberately not compared. So `close_test_replay` (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`) can write the `testing -> supported` transition (`:1127-1131`) that `rk2_finding_refusal` requires (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). The planting is not evidence and must not be spelled as a setup step either: setup carries only method and url (`20260815T000000Z...:346`). D8, the OWASP identifier floor, for `agentic-ai`: no OWASP scenario covers this class. The WSTG master branch as read in full by .scratch/ticket-101/mining/owasp.json (all 122 checklist rows plus nineteen scenario pages) carries no language-model scenario, and ASVS 5.0.0 -- read as the official flat JSON at tag v5.0.0_release -- has no chapter for one. The nearest stable identifiers in either document describe the CARRIER (a stored parameter, a reflected parameter) and not the interpreter, and citing one of them would misname the class.

technique: The model as the carrier: an instruction planted in content it reads makes the PIPELINE reach a declared out-of-band correlator, so the proof is an arrival rather than the model's own prose.

preconditions: `tech_llm`; a declared and bound out-of-band correlator on the recorded channel (ticket 98); a channel kind the harness records; the model's tool or fetch surface already enumerated by the framing row so the run knows there is a carrier at all.
baseline: Trigger the same retrieval with a clean item and confirm from the answer that the pipeline ran, with nothing arriving on the channel.
variant: Plant the correlator host in the field the model reads, invoke the trigger, and watch the channel. An arrival is the pipeline having acted on our text.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: a request putting the SAME correlator host in a field the pipeline does NOT pass to the model. If that arrives too, something else in the stack fetches our strings and the model is not the carrier. A control ARRIVAL cannot serve: `is_control` and a null subject are tied by a CHECK (20261001T000000Z...:45-52), so it writes no Observation.
payload_family: a read-only reference to the declared correlator, placed in a field the model consumes -- resolve or fetch, never an effect
runtime_writer: callback.py:85 `record_callback_interaction()`; `callback_interaction` is evidential with `allowed_provenance = {callback}`. The bar itself still closes at replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` as `response_differential`, which is what the Playbook's `bb:evidence` asks for role=variant; the arrival is a further edge on the Hypothesis.
supported_evidence: Two edges, and they are not interchangeable. `response_differential` between the clean-item retrieval and the planted-item retrieval is what CLOSES the Test and is the only one that can carry the Hypothesis to `supported`. `callback_interaction` (provenance `{callback}` alone, `20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:349`) is the edge that carries the real weight, because an arrival is binary where the model's prose is not -- but it is an agent-supplied edge on the Hypothesis and can never move it to `supported` by itself.
refuted_evidence: `response_invariant` on the variant with no arrival on the channel across every repeat.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: one arrival is recorded on the correlator. (2) action: end the test at that arrival; do not escalate from a fetch to an effect. (3) scope: the run. (4) resume: a Task opened on the SINK the pipeline reached, a different subject and class. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the correlator id, the arrival row, the Receipt of the triggering request, and the field the reference was planted in.

notes: HIGH VALUE and the direct answer to this Playbook's own evidence problem: `references/llm.md` calls an action the pipeline took the strongest form of proof and the Playbook has no way to get one from prose. mined_from is empty by D7: no shard produced this reading and it is derived from the Playbook's own body and references rather than from a mined row. `agentic-ai` declares `bb:effects: read_only`, and `_body_allowed` (`src/redkraken/execution.py:3646`) opens a Task whose WHOLE Playbook selection is read_only with `body_allowed: false`. So on an agentic-ai-only Task the planting request may not carry a body at all and the channel has to be the `query_parameter` the Playbook's own `bb:triggers_any` already names; a body-borne channel needs the Task's selection to include a Playbook that is not read_only, and even then the planting is setup and not a Test action. An arrival alone does NOT reach a Finding: `close_test_replay` is the only writer of a `testing -> supported` transition (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`, `:1127-1131`) and it derives its outcome from the Test's own assertions (`:1063-1074`). The row reaches a Finding only through the retrieval pair, whose differential is the item id in the query. mined_from is empty by D7: no shard produced the correlator-carrier reading; it is derived from `references/llm.md`'s own 'an action the pipeline took is the strongest proof' line together with ticket 98's channel. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding: the differential between the Test's two actions lives in the query or path segment naming WHICH stored item the retrieval trigger reads; the correlator arrival is a further edge and reaches no Finding by itself, which is what a Test action carries (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`, `src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`, `20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`).

Its answer is the wildcard baseline every candidate is compared against; if it answers like the candidates, the origin answers every name and every 'hit' is the wildcard.

technique: A container registry inside the Program's scope asked to name what it holds: the Registry HTTP API v2 version handshake, then the repository catalogue, then one repository's tags -- three plain GETs against a caller holding nothing.

preconditions: `read_method` and `unauthenticated_endpoint` on the registry host, and the Program's scope must cover THE REGISTRY ITSELF as an application rather than the application whose images it stores. A hosted registry the target only consumes is a vendor's own service and is out of scope by the card. No headers and no body are needed.
baseline: `GET /v2/` with nothing presented, twice unchanged. That is the API's own version handshake and it is what this host answers to a caller holding nothing; the second send is the noise floor.
variant: `GET /v2/_catalog` with nothing presented, then `GET /v2/<first-repo>/tags/list` for exactly ONE repository the catalogue named. A catalogue document rather than an unauthorized document means the organisation's image inventory is published.
control: Noise floor first: the two `GET /v2/` sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: `GET /v2/<16-random-chars>/tags/list`, which must answer name-unknown rather than the catalogue's own shape. That separates 'the registry names its repositories' from 'this host answers every `/v2/` path with one page', which is what a reverse proxy in front of a dead registry looks like.
payload_family: well-known operational routes of the Registry HTTP API v2; no payload and no request body
runtime_writer: replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` -- the kind comes from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action a `body_differs`/`status_differs` assertion names closes `response_differential`, one none names closes `response_invariant` (roster.py:404). All four requests are one path each on one host, so all four are Test actions. Calling the returned document a CATALOGUE is `content_match`, provenance `{tool_run}` alone (0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed at execution.py:518 `promote_proposal()`: a `jq` run over the catalogue JSON satisfies it, and per D4 so does a `browse` run, because `browser_runs.tool_run_id` is a foreign key into `tool_runs` (20260814T040000Z...:411-417) and `enforce_kind_provenance` (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) checks only the provenance string. The live definition of `promote_proposal` is `20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487` and its `observations` INSERT is at `:1116-1123`; the `20260814T070000Z...:1631` site earlier ledger passes cited is superseded and behaviourally identical.
supported_evidence: `response_differential` between the catalogue answer and the random-repository control, with the two `/v2/` sends matching each other. `content_match` from the `jq` (or browse) run is the supporting edge that says the document IS a repository list rather than an error page shaped like one.
refuted_evidence: `response_differential` in the refuting direction, which is this Playbook's own `to_status=refuted, role=variant` row: `/v2/_catalog` hashes to the random-repository control's answer, so the host answers the same way for everything under `/v2/` and nothing is being disclosed.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: the catalogue answers and names repositories. (2) action: one `tags/list`, for one repository, and stop. Do not fetch a manifest, do not pull a layer, do not read an image config for environment values, do not attempt a push, and do not run the bearer-token dance the `WWW-Authenticate` challenge asks for -- that header is stripped from the agent view on every path (`WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS`, proxy.py:376-385, proxy.py:3083), so the dance cannot be performed here anyway. (3) scope: the registry host. (4) resume: a Task whose scope decision names the registry, for anything past the tag list; the credential-material half -- reading an image config for keys -- is `information_disclosure.credential_material` and belongs to `secrets`, not here. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the four Receipts, the catalogue Artifact and its digest, the `jq` filter or the browse run that identified it, the single repository whose tags were listed, and an explicit line saying no manifest and no layer was fetched.
owner_ticket: none -- reachable
notes: The third silently-lost hand-off. orphans folded `NEW:container-registry` into `attack-surface` -- which is this group's, not orphans' -- and wrote no row; g01 dropped it as naming none of its slugs; and the twenty-one attack-surface rows carried no registry reading. orphans recorded the consequence and it happened: `kubernetes` step 6 refuses a registry request by name and `supply-chain`'s provenance line refuses it too, so the reading falls between them unless it lands here. It is `information_disclosure.artifact_exposure`, which is this Playbook's declared class, and the class needs no new emitter. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding. Its differential between two Test actions lives in the request PATH -- `/v2/`, `/v2/_catalog`, `/v2/<repo>/tags/list` and `/v2/<random>/tags/list` on one host, which is exactly what a Test action carries: an action's key set is `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`), and `record_test_action` compares method, scheme, host, port and path (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`) -- the query rides the url and is deliberately not compared. So `close_test_replay` (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`) can write the `testing -> supported` transition (`:1127-1131`) that `rk2_finding_refusal` requires (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). D8: no WSTG scenario, ASVS v5.0.0 requirement or API Top 10 2023 id covers a container-registry catalogue read; the mining shard that found it recorded the Docker Registry HTTP API v2 spec as the source of the routes and no OWASP document names them.

preconditions: `read_method`; a name space the application actually indexes -- path segments, or an `object_identifier` parameter -- and a name in it the application ITSELF links, so the 'found' answer is known before anything is sent.
baseline: The certainly-present name: a route or identifier the served markup or the recovered route table already references. This is the 'found' answer.
variant: A small, declared, bounded set of candidate names drawn from the target's own words -- product names, internal terms, the naming pattern of a name already discovered -- one request each.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: a certainly-ABSENT name: a high-entropy string of the same shape and length. If it answers the same as the certainly-present one, the server answers uniformly -- wildcard route, catch-all rewrite, single-page-app fallback -- and nothing below it reads anything.
payload_family: name space only: path segments or an object identifier, derived from the target's own text. No request body.
runtime_writer: replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` -- the kind comes from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action a `body_differs`/`status_differs` assertion names closes `response_differential`, one none names closes `response_invariant` (roster.py:404). The status pair is what closes; `information_disclosure.identifier_oracle` is the Property the pair would support and it currently has no emitter.
supported_evidence: `response_differential`: the certainly-present and certainly-absent arms separate, and a candidate lands on the 'present' side.
refuted_evidence: `response_invariant` between the certainly-present and certainly-absent arms -- the server does not distinguish, so no oracle exists and every later 'hit' would have been the wildcard.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: the control and the baseline stop separating, or the first discriminating name is enough to state the claim. (2) action: stop; ATT&CK's goal is identification of content, not a complete inventory. (3) scope: the run. (4) resume: a Program configuration permitting a bounded discovery run (ticket 187), which is a Tool run and not this Playbook. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. The ones that ANSWER -- a parking page, a provider's unclaimed-resource page, a 404 from a host that still resolves -- are the arms this row is built on: each one is a Receipt and each one is a Test action. An origin that does not resolve at all is a DIFFERENT and weaker arm, because the door files no Receipt for it.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). baseline: A path under the branch being read that certainly does not exist, requested with the same method the candidates will use.
variant: The same certainly-absent name with the extension the candidates carry, and again with each method the candidates will use. A negative answer that MOVES between those arms means the branch has more than one shape of 'nothing here'.

preconditions: `read_method` on the root route. The reading itself is trivially available; what is missing is somewhere to file it as a claim.
baseline: The response to a plain request for the root route, stored with its headers.

preconditions: `read_method`, `unauthenticated_endpoint`; the application serves robots.txt, a sitemap, or a JavaScript bundle carrying a route table. `spa_surface` where the table comes from a bundle.
baseline: One route from the linked, crawlable surface, fetched as whatever Identity the Task was opened under. This is what an ordinary route answers.
variant: One route named ONLY by robots.txt, the sitemap, or the bundle's route table -- declared but never linked. A 401 or 403 means it exists and is guarded; a 200 means the declaration was the only control.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: a route fabricated to look like the others and present in NO declaration, which must 404 -- that is what makes a 401 mean 'exists' rather than 'the router refuses unknown shapes'. Plus a linked route of the same shape, so a declared-only route answering exactly as a linked one reads as path disclosure and nothing about access.
payload_family: none -- declared paths only, harvested offline
runtime_writer: replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` -- the kind comes from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action a `body_differs`/`status_differs` assertion names closes `response_differential`, one none names closes `response_invariant` (roster.py:404). The route list comes from `run_tool js_routes`/`js_map` and is `endpoint_discovered`, registered non-evidential; the claim rests on the status pair, not the list.
supported_evidence: `response_differential`: the declared-only route answers differently from both the linked route and the fabricated control.
refuted_evidence: `response_differential` in the refuting direction: the declared-only route hashes to the fabricated control's answer, so the declaration named nothing that is served.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: T1594's people half comes into view -- names, roles, contact details of employees. (2) action: stop before collecting any of it; third-party personal data is not this harness's subject. (3) scope: the run. (4) resume: not resumed on that material at all. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the declaration as an Artifact, the routes taken from it, and that the personal-data half was not read.
owner_ticket: none -- reachable
notes: `attack-surface` already emits artifact_exposure; what this adds is the CONTROL arm. A declared-only route that answers exactly as a linked one is not a finding, and nothing in the shipped text forces that reading. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding. Its differential between two Test actions lives in the request PATH; the Identity is held constant across every action, which is exactly what a Test action carries: an action's key set is `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`), and `record_test_action` compares method, scheme, host, port and path (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`) -- the query rides the url and is deliberately not compared. So `close_test_replay` (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`) can write the `testing -> supported` transition (`:1127-1131`) that `rk2_finding_refusal` requires (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). The Identity is fixed for the whole run, so it is a precondition and not an inter-action differential: an action names no identity (`20260815T000000Z...:377`), injection is keyed on the authorization's `identity_entity_id` (`src/redkraken/proxy.py:2911-2954`, `identity.Session.inject` at `src/redkraken/identity.py:330-340`), and ticket 131 fixes the Identity per Tool run. A reading whose only difference is 'with Identity versus without' needs two Test runs, and `rk2_finding_refusal` ties a Finding to the ONE run that settled it (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`).

preconditions: None that help: the handshake itself cannot be presented.
baseline: Would be: a correct handshake and its exact status plus response headers.
variant: Would be: the same with an unsupported version, an extension offer, and an unknown subprotocol.
control: Would be the same variations against a path that is NOT a WebSocket endpoint, subtracting the front proxy's own behaviour. Not executable.
payload_family: malformed or unusual handshake header values
runtime_writer: none. `connection` and `upgrade` are BOTH members of `proxy.HOP_BY_HOP` (proxy.py:316-329) and `forwardable()` drops them (proxy.py:635), so no upgrade is ever offered and no `101 Switching Protocols` can be the first step. `Sec-WebSocket-*` headers do forward, but a server that never saw `Upgrade` answers on the ordinary HTTP path, so any rejection read is that path's wording and not the WebSocket library's.
supported_evidence: none -- a differential collected this way would identify the front end's plain-HTTP handling, not the library, and filing it as a library identification would be a wrong claim rather than a missing one.
refuted_evidence: none.

preconditions: `tech_oauth` and `query_parameter`; a client registration the test Identity may use and whose registered `redirect_uri` is known. Nothing has to receive a code for this reading to conclude.
baseline: An authorization request with the EXACTLY registered `redirect_uri` -- a redirect status, the issue answer.
variant: One mutation per arm, each its own request: a path segment appended; a query appended; a fragment appended; the registered value as a prefix of a longer host; a subdomain prepended; a case shift; a percent-encoded traversal into the same host; a custom URI scheme in front of the allowed host; the `http://` downgrade. An arm answering as the baseline names the accepted shape.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: an UNRELATED absolute URI, which must be REJECTED -- that establishes any validation happens at all; if it is accepted the census is unnecessary and the finding is larger. For the suffix arm, also the allowed host with a foreign suffix appended (`<allowed>.invalid`), which must be rejected: that proves the suffix is being compared and not the whole string.
payload_family: substring, prefix, suffix, wildcard, normalization and scheme mutations of one registered URI

refuted_evidence: `response_invariant`: every mutation is answered exactly as the foreign-URI control is, so the comparison is equality.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: an arm is accepted. (2) action: stop at the acceptance verdict; never complete a flow that would deliver a live code anywhere we do not own, and do not stand up a receiver. (3) scope: the arm, then the run once the shape is named. (4) resume: the delivery question resumes only in the correlator-chain row, which delivers to the recorded out-of-band channel. notes: Eight mined rows across five shards are this one mechanism under different payloads. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding. Its differential between two Test actions lives in the QUERY -- one mutation of `redirect_uri` per arm on one unchanged authorization path, which is exactly what a Test action carries: an action's key set is `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`), and `record_test_action` compares method, scheme, host, port and path (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`) -- the query rides the url and is deliberately not compared. So `close_test_replay` (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`) can write the `testing -> supported` transition (`:1127-1131`) that `rk2_finding_refusal` requires (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). preconditions: `tech_oauth`; a `registration_endpoint` present in the discovery document at `/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. Run with NO leased Identity, because the question is whether a credential is needed. NOTE: this WRITES STATE on the subject.
baseline: POST a minimal client-registration document with no `Authorization`. A 401 is the healthy answer.
variant: The same POST returning a 201 with a `client_id` means registration is open. Then the same document carrying a URL-valued field the server dereferences -- a logo, a key set, a request document -- pointed at the declared correlator.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: the same POST with a deliberately MALFORMED document and no `Authorization`. A 400 rather than a 401 shows the endpoint parses before it authenticates -- the same finding in weaker form -- and separates 'open registration' from 'accepts everything'.
payload_family: a minimal registration document, then the same document with one URL-valued field
runtime_writer: replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` -- the kind comes from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action a `body_differs`/`status_differs` assertion names closes `response_differential`, one none names closes `response_invariant` (roster.py:404). For the access half. For the FETCH half: callback.py:85 `record_callback_interaction()` -- an arrival on the declared channel is evidential, so that half is reachable and not, as an earlier reading of the card had it, blocked.
supported_evidence: Agent-filed `error_detail` (provenance `{receipt,tool_run}`) for the access half -- the 201 against the malformed-document control -- filed at `src/redkraken/execution.py:518`; agent-filed `credential_effect` (`{receipt}`) where the 201 is what an unauthenticated caller got. `callback_interaction` (provenance `{callback}`) is the further edge for the fetch half. NONE of the three is a `close_test_replay` kind and none of them reaches a Finding.
refuted_evidence: Agent-filed `error_detail` recording that the endpoint answers 401 to both the well-formed and the malformed document, so it authenticates before it parses. Not `response_invariant`: no action of this reading is expressible as a Test action.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: a client is minted. (2) action: register AT MOST ONE client, record its id, and stop; do not register in a loop. (3) scope: the endpoint. (4) resume: after the registered client has been removed or handed to the Program for removal. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the registration document sent, the returned `client_id`, the Receipt, and the cleanup performed or requested; the Program contact is told regardless, because state was created on the subject.
