notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. Not the refused 'claiming a third-party resource' case -- the client is created on the subject application the Program covers -- but it DOES create state, so the state-writing precondition must travel with the row. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION, NOT A FINDING. The difference here is the REGISTRATION DOCUMENT in the request body -- the whole differential is well-formed against malformed, and both are bodies, and no Test action can carry one: an action's key set is exactly `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), a setup or cleanup step's is exactly `('method','url')` (`:346`), and `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` only although `proxy.spend` accepts `headers=` and `body=` (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`, `src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224`). Setup runs as ONE block before every action and cleanup as ONE block after (`src/redkraken/replay.py:390`, `:425`) and neither is evidence (`:432-452`), so a body- or header-borne change cannot even be interleaved between two read-back actions. `close_test_replay` is the only writer of a `testing -> supported` hypothesis transition (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`, `:1127-1131`) and `rk2_finding_refusal` opens no Finding without one (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). The reading is real and its agent-filed Observation is a real `hypothesis_evidence` edge -- `rk2_promote_hypotheses` filters on no kind (`20261025T000000Z...:530`) -- it simply cannot carry the Hypothesis to `supported`. `oauth` declares `bb:effects: mutates_session`, so `_body_allowed` (`src/redkraken/execution.py:3646`) does open the Task with a body and the reading RUNS; what it cannot do is close a Test. The fetch half's arrival is a further edge and, per the same rule, carries no Hypothesis to `supported` either.

preconditions: `tech_oauth` and `query_parameter`; `request_uri_parameter_supported` true in the discovery document at `/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, which is one GET to establish. A known `client_id`. Two URLs on the SUBJECT'S OWN origin -- one that certainly 404s and one that certainly answers 200 with a body that is not a signed request object. Nothing has to be hosted and no second origin is needed, which is what keeps this inside the refusal on hosting one.
baseline: An authorization request whose `request_uri` names a same-origin URL that certainly 404s. A fetch-failed error is the answer that says the server went and looked.
variant: The same authorization request with `request_uri` naming a same-origin URL that certainly answers 200 with a non-JWT body. A PARSE or format error instead of a fetch error means the fetch happened and the bytes came back. One parameter changed, one url per arm.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: `request_uri` set to a syntactically invalid URL, which must return a VALIDATION error issued before any fetch. That third answer shape is what separates 'the server fetches' from 'the server returns one error for every value of this parameter', and without it the fetch-versus-parse pair proves nothing.
payload_family: same-origin reference dereference: one URL that 404s, one that answers a non-JWT 200, one that is not a URL. No internal address and no correlator is required for the reading to conclude.
runtime_writer: replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()` -- the kind comes from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action a `body_differs`/`status_differs` assertion names closes `response_differential`, one none names closes `response_invariant` (roster.py:404). All three arms are one url each on one authorization path, so all three are Test actions. The server's error WORDING, which is what names fetch-failed versus parse-failed, is a separate agent-filed `error_detail` edge (provenance `{receipt,tool_run}`) at execution.py:518 `promote_proposal()`. The live definition of `promote_proposal` is `20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487` and its `observations` INSERT is at `:1116-1123`; the `20260814T070000Z...:1631` site earlier ledger passes cited is superseded and behaviourally identical.
supported_evidence: `response_differential` between the 404-target arm and the 200-non-JWT arm, against the invalid-URL control that errors before any fetch. `error_detail` is the agent-filed edge that says WHICH error each arm was.
refuted_evidence: `response_invariant`: all three arms are answered identically, so the parameter is accepted and never dereferenced -- or rejected wholesale, which the discovery document should already have said.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: an arm's `request_uri` is about to name anything other than the subject's own origin -- an internal address, a metadata service, a third party. (2) action: do not send it. Two same-origin URLs are the whole reading; pointing the parameter at internal infrastructure is a different class with a different authorization and it belongs to `ssrf-url-routing`. (3) scope: the arm. (4) resume: a Task opened on the fetch primitive in its own right, under `ssrf-url-routing`, with its own scope decision. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the discovery document, the three `request_uri` values verbatim, the three Receipts, and which of fetch-failed, parse-failed and validation-failed each produced.

notes: The mutual hand-off both g01 and g02 dropped: g01's coverage_note gave it to oauth, g02's gave it back to ssrf-url-routing, and the string `request_uri` appeared in none of the 347 ledger rows. It is oauth's own surface -- the authorization SERVER fetching a URL the CLIENT named -- and it sits beside the dynamic-registration row, whose URL-valued fields the same server fetches. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding. Its differential between two Test actions lives in the QUERY -- one `request_uri` value per arm on one unchanged authorization path, which is exactly what a Test action carries: an action's key set is `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`), and `record_test_action` compares method, scheme, host, port and path (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`) -- the query rides the url and is deliberately not compared. So `close_test_replay` (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`) can write the `testing -> supported` transition (`:1127-1131`) that `rk2_finding_refusal` requires (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). The repair packet suggested spelling this as a correlator arrival; the mined row's own same-origin discriminator is strictly better here and is what is written, because an arrival is an agent-supplied edge that cannot carry a Hypothesis to `supported` while these three arms close a Test outright. A correlator arm may be added as a further `callback_interaction` edge and it changes nothing about the Finding path. A Test specification's url may not carry a `.` or `..` PATH segment or the string `%2e` anywhere in it (`rk2_test_request_problem`, `20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:221-226`); dot segments inside the QUERY survive, because that check is applied to the path only. The door forwards all of them verbatim (`origin_form()`, `src/redkraken/proxy.py:818-828`), so the percent-encoded arms are performable and simply cannot be closed by a Test. Keep every `request_uri` value free of `%2e` or the arm drops out of the specification.

preconditions: `tech_oauth`, `query_parameter`; a client registration the test Identity may use; an open redirect on a host INSIDE the Program's scope; a declared and bound out-of-band correlator (ticket 98). The correlator is not a hosted origin, which is what makes this expressible without the refused 'host a second origin' capability.
baseline: The ordinary flow with the registered `redirect_uri`: the code lands on the registered callback and nothing arrives on the channel.
variant: The same flow with `redirect_uri` pointing at the in-scope open redirect that forwards to the correlator. An arrival carrying the code in its query, or the referrer, proves the chain end to end.
control: Noise floor first: two identical baseline sends differenced against each other -- `body_differs` fires on `Date` alone (roster.py:404). Then: the same authorization request with `redirect_uri` pointing STRAIGHT at the correlator, which must be REJECTED by the allowlist. If it is accepted there is no allowlist and the chain was unnecessary -- a different, larger finding. A control ARRIVAL cannot be the negative: `is_control` and a null subject are tied by a CHECK (20261001T000000Z...:45-52), so it writes no Observation.
payload_family: an allowlisted host whose own redirect parameter carries the correlator; the same in traversal form; `response_mode` varied, which can change how the other parameters are validated
runtime_writer: callback.py:85 `record_callback_interaction()`; `callback_interaction` is evidential with `allowed_provenance = {callback}`. The authorization request is one `http_request` or one `browse navigate`; the Playbook's bar still closes at replay.py:106 `close_test_replay()`, and the arrival is a FURTHER `hypothesis_evidence` edge.
supported_evidence: `response_differential` closes the accept/reject pair; `callback_interaction` (provenance `{callback}` alone -- no Receipt may be filed under this kind) is the edge that carries the real weight, because it says the credential left rather than that a validator was lenient.
refuted_evidence: `response_invariant`: nothing arrives on the channel across the flow, so the chain does not complete.
stop_conditions: (1) trigger: one arrival is recorded. (2) action: end the attempt; the delivered code is NEVER redeemed anywhere -- let it expire. (3) scope: the run. (4) resume: a fresh flow with a fresh correlator, one correlator per attempt. (5) told: the Task operator; the Program contact if the rules of engagement require it. (6) recorded: the correlator id, the arrival row, the authorization request verbatim, the open redirect used, and confirmation the code was not redeemed; the Program contact is told regardless, since a credential left the registered callback.
owner_ticket: none -- reachable
notes: HIGH VALUE as an unblock pattern. Every other `redirect_uri` row in the corpus stops at accept-versus-reject because delivery was believed to need an attacker origin, and hosting a second origin is refused by decision. FINDING PATH -- this row can reach a Finding. Its differential between two Test actions lives in the QUERY -- `redirect_uri` pointing at the registered callback, at the in-scope open redirect, and straight at the correlator, on one authorization path, which is exactly what a Test action carries: an action's key set is `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` and nothing else (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`), and `record_test_action` compares method, scheme, host, port and path (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1631-1636`) -- the query rides the url and is deliberately not compared. So `close_test_replay` (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`) can write the `testing -> supported` transition (`:1127-1131`) that `rk2_finding_refusal` requires (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). The traversal-form spelling of the chained target is the exception. A Test specification's url may not carry a `.` or `..` PATH segment or the string `%2e` anywhere in it (`rk2_test_request_problem`, `20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:221-226`); dot segments inside the QUERY survive, because that check is applied to the path only. The door forwards all of them verbatim (`origin_form()`, `src/redkraken/proxy.py:818-828`), so the percent-encoded arms are performable and simply cannot be closed by a Test. And the arrival, which is the evidence that matters, does NOT reach a Finding on its own: `record_callback_interaction` writes an evidential Observation and `rk2_promote_hypotheses` files it as an edge with no filter on the kind (`20261025T000000Z...:530`), but only `close_test_replay` writes a `testing -> supported` transition (`20260816T000000Z...:1016`, `:1127-1131`). The accept/reject pair is what carries the claim; the arrival is what makes it worth reporting.

The difference here is a `Referer` request header, and no Test action can carry one: an action's key set is exactly `('ordinal','role','kind','method','url')` (`20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377`), a setup or cleanup step's is exactly `('method','url')` (`:346`), and `_Door.send` calls `proxy.spend` with `url` and `method` only although `proxy.spend` accepts `headers=` and `body=` (`src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351`, `src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224`). Setup runs as ONE block before every action and cleanup as ONE block after (`src/redkraken/replay.py:390`, `:425`) and neither is evidence (`:432-452`), so a body- or header-borne change cannot even be interleaved between two read-back actions. `close_test_replay` is the only writer of a `testing -> supported` hypothesis transition (`20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016`, `:1127-1131`) and `rk2_finding_refusal` opens no Finding without one (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). The reading is real and its agent-filed Observation is a real `hypothesis_evidence` edge -- `rk2_promote_hypotheses` filters on no kind (`20261025T000000Z...:530`) -- it simply cannot carry the Hypothesis to `supported`. Arm (b) is Identity- and session-conditioned: The Identity is fixed for the whole run, so it is a precondition and not an inter-action differential: an action names no identity (`20260815T000000Z...:377`), injection is keyed on the authorization's `identity_entity_id` (`src/redkraken/proxy.py:2911-2954`, `identity.Session.inject` at `src/redkraken/identity.py:330-340`), and ticket 131 fixes the Identity per Tool run. A reading whose only difference is 'with Identity versus without' needs two Test runs, and `rk2_finding_refusal` ties a Finding to the ONE run that settled it (`20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649`). So `webauthn` has exactly ONE arm in the whole group that reaches a Finding, and it is the older-API-version path. The rewrite must say that plainly rather than let step 2 read as though every downgrade closes a Test.

technique: Ask whether a caller writes part of the policy that is supposed to constrain them, by sending a directive-shaped value into a parameter the application copies into a Content-Security-Policy and differencing the served policy against the same request carrying an ordinary value.

preconditions: web_surface, reflected_parameter, and a parameter the application demonstrably copies into a response-header value -- a report-uri or a nonce source read out of the request. The same byte-stability precondition. The request half is trivially expressible: the header VALUE pattern on our own request is printable ASCII only, but the value being planted travels in the QUERY STRING and nowhere else -- a body spelling is excluded twice over, once because _Door.send sends no body (src/redkraken/replay.py:340-351) so a body arm could never be a Test action, and once because browser-framing is bb:effects: read_only and a Task whose whole selection is read_only opens with body_allowed: false (_body_allowed, src/redkraken/execution.py:3646); and and the policy it lands in is the target's response header, which is inside the hashed transcript.
baseline: GET the route with the parameter carrying an ordinary value, and record the Content-Security-Policy as served.
variant: GET the same route with the QUERY parameter carrying a directive-shaped value, and read whether the served policy now contains it.
control: The baseline request sent twice, unchanged, asserted body_equals -- and a third arm with the parameter absent entirely, which shows the directive is generated per request rather than static. Two identical sends are the arm that separates a policy the caller wrote from a Date header.
payload_family: policy-directive fragments in a reflected parameter -- a source-list entry, a report-uri, a directive separator; the class is a value that survives into a header the browser parses as policy, not a payload list.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069, :1072) for the policy differential; promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function) and :1116 (INSERT)) for the header_policy_observed and for a reflected_input edge from the same Receipt, both of which take {receipt} provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:226 and :236).
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the directive-shaped arm is named by body_differs against the ordinary-value arm, and the differing bytes are the policy header. The agent files header_policy_observed naming the served directive and reflected_input naming where the value landed. This row IS on the Finding path: the two arms differ in the query string, which travels on the action url, so record_test_action's method/scheme/host/port/path comparison is satisfied and close_test_replay can settle it (20260815T000000Z...:1387-1397).
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the policy is identical under both values, so the directive is static and the parameter does not reach it.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the planted directive would loosen the served policy rather than only demonstrate that it is caller-written -- for example a source-list entry naming an origin. course of action: plant an inert directive that changes the header text without widening what the browser would permit, and stop. scope: this route. resume: never for the widening form; that is a change to the subject's own protection. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the exact value planted, both policies as served, and the note that the reading did not test whether the widened policy would be honoured.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: The mined row filed this blocked as 'another customer for the same missing writer'. There is no missing writer. Filed as its own row rather than folded into the framing row because the subject is different: the framing row asks what the target published, this one asks who wrote it. Ticket 211 removes this condition and ticket 101 is blocked by it; do not harden it into Playbook prose (docs/research/playbook-state-of-the-art/00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:30-33, 'the order is harness first').

preconditions: web_surface, authenticated_endpoint, read_method. Origin is in neither proxy.HOP_BY_HOP (proxy.py:315-329) nor the x-redkraken- internal prefix, so forwardable() (proxy.py:635) passes it and the target sees the value the model wrote. The answer survives too: Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials are not in WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS (proxy.py:376-385), so they are inside the hashed agent transcript. Same byte-stability precondition as the framing row. And the one the Finding path adds: because the only thing that moves between the arms is a request header, this reading runs on mcp__rk2__http_request and compare_responses, never in the replay lane.
baseline: GET the authenticated route with no Origin header at all, so a header that is always there can be told from one the request provoked.
variant: The same GET carrying Origin naming a host the target does not control, then the suffix neighbour (target.example.attacker.example), the prefix neighbour (attacker-target.example), the scheme downgrade of a trusted subdomain, and the literal null -- one arm each, pairwise, since compare_responses differences exactly two Artifacts (ticket 109).
control: The no-Origin baseline sent a second time, unchanged, asserted body_equals. Without it the Date header alone produces a body_differs and every Origin arm reads as reflected. A second control arm worth sending is an Origin of sixteen random characters at a domain nobody owns: if that is echoed too, the target reflects any Origin and the allowlist was never consulted.
payload_family: Origin request-header values, as a class of authority spellings rather than a payload list -- the target's own origin, a foreign registrable domain, a suffix neighbour, a prefix neighbour, a scheme downgrade, and the literal null.
runtime_writer: No Test writer: this differential cannot be a Test action (see notes). The Observation is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function), INSERT INTO observations at :1116) as header_policy_observed, allowed_provenance {receipt,tool_run} (0018_vocabularies.sql:236), citing the two mcp__rk2__http_request Receipts -- the no-Origin baseline and the foreign-Origin arm. A second edge of the same kind carries the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials pairing. Both land in hypothesis_evidence through rk2_promote_hypotheses (20261025T000000Z...:530).
supported_evidence: AGENT-FILED header_policy_observed, polarity supports, provenance {receipt} -- NOT one of close_test_replay's two kinds, because the Origin arm and the no-Origin arm differ only in a request header and record_test_action would see one identical action twice. The claim that matters is the pairing: an echoed foreign origin beside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, read out of the agent transcript, which keeps both headers (they are not in WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS, proxy.py:376-385).
refuted_evidence: AGENT-FILED header_policy_observed, polarity refutes -- the foreign-Origin arm's transcript carries the same policy as the no-Origin arm, so the origin was not reflected. Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with no credentials is also a refutation: that is a target publishing something it means to publish.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: four Origin values have been sent, or the two identical baseline sends did not hash equal. course of action: stop; do not sweep a subdomain wordlist through the Origin header. scope: this route. resume: an operator names further Origin spellings worth one request each, with a reason. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: every Origin sent, the Receipt for each, and the pairing verdict for each, including the negative ones.
owner_ticket: 211 -- reachable as a reading today, and it stops at an Observation rather than a Finding. Ticket 211, 'A Test action carries the header and the body it plans', is ready-for-agent and blocked by nothing, and ticket 101 is blocked by it; it is the ticket that closes this gap, priced in notes. The reading itself needs nothing new: the Origin header travels on mcp__rk2__http_request today and both CORS response headers survive into the hashed transcript.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. The differential lives in a request HEADER, and a Test action carries only a method and a url: _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:340-351) calls proxy.spend with url= and method= and nothing else, though proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), and record_test_action compares the Receipt to the action over method, scheme, host, port and path alone (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1387-1397). close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the cited run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649). The reading itself IS performable -- mcp__rk2__http_request takes a headers object -- and the agent-filed Observation is a real hypothesis_evidence edge that rk2_promote_hypotheses writes with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530). It just cannot carry the Hypothesis to supported. Five mined rows say this is blocked; all five rest on the corrected claims. HIGH VALUE: the suffix and prefix arms are injection.parser_differential wearing a CORS coat, and that class is one of the nine with no emitter -- the same three requests answer both questions. The reading's honest ceiling, which cors-xssi.md states well and which this row keeps: Access-Control-Allow-Origin describes what a browser would let a script read, so what is shown is the permission the target grants, never a read a page achieved. Exercising the permission means being a second origin and is the refused row below. Origin: null is readable as a value here; producing a genuine null origin needs a hosted sandboxed document and is refused. PRICED, NOT PERMANENT -- ticket 211, 'A Test action carries the header and the body it plans' (docs/specs/production-harness-v2/issues/211-a-test-action-carries-the-header-and-the-body-it-plans.md), is ready-for-agent, blocked by nothing, and ticket 101 is blocked BY it. The wall this row works around is three edits deep and the parts are already in the tree: proxy.spend already takes headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:340-351) forwards two keyword arguments; receipts.request_agent_sha (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:59) already holds the whole agent-view request message and is written unconditionally on the same path as response_agent_sha (proxy.py:3279), so record_test_action (20260815T000000Z...:1387-1397) gains its header and body binding with no new column; and rk2_test_spec_problem's action key set (20260815T000000Z...:377) widens from five keys to seven. One migration and about two lines of Python. Per docs/research/playbook-state-of-the-art/00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:30-33 -- 'This is why the order is harness first' -- the rewrite must NOT harden this sentence into Playbook prose: it is a dated condition, and the corpus is written once against the capability that lands.

baseline: not executed
variant: not executed
control: not executed
payload_family: a framing document -- an iframe of the target with a positioned decoy, an opener-rewriting page, or two same-origin frames of which one is credentialless.
runtime_writer: none. No runtime path writes an Observation for a reading that never runs; recorded here so the absence is a decision on the record rather than a gap somebody fills.
supported_evidence: none
refuted_evidence: none
stop_conditions: halt trigger: a run proposes to stand up an origin, a paste, a gist or a localhost page in order to frame the target. course of action: refuse, and report the framing-header reading that is already complete. scope: the run, and every future run -- this is a standing decision, not a per-Task judgement. resume: never on this harness; the refusal is on the capability card and is not a capability gap. told: the operator who owns the Task, and the refusal is written where the claim was first proposed so it is not re-proposed. recorded: the refusal, its reason, and the header reading that answers the same question.

notes: Five mined rows, one refusal, collapsed because one missing thing refuses all of them. The reason travels because DoubleClickjacking is named in the 2024 Top 10 and will be re-proposed. The reachable residue of every one of them is the framing-header reading above, and clickjacking.md is right about why that is not a loss: the claim was always about the header. technique: Read the SameSite, Secure and HttpOnly attributes that decide what a missing framing header actually costs, out of the browser's own cookie jar rather than off the wire, because the wire reading is unavailable on every path.

preconditions: web_surface, form_request, cookie_parameter, and a browse plan of at most 32 steps that can complete the login the session cookie is issued by. The wire route is closed by construction: set-cookie and set-cookie2 are in WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS (proxy.py:376-385) and response_for_agent (proxy.py:673-684) drops them before the transcript is hashed, on every path including the unbound one, so the Playbook's step 1 instruction to record Set-Cookie and its SameSite attribute cannot be followed through the door.
baseline: browse: navigate to an unauthenticated page of the origin, then read_client_state kind=cookies, and record the attribute set. The registry strips cookie VALUES before the Artifact exists, so what is stored is name, domain, path, httpOnly, secure, sameSite and prefix and nothing spendable.
variant: In the same plan, complete the login, then read_client_state kind=cookies again. The session cookie's SameSite is now readable, which is what decides whether a cross-site form POST would carry the session at all.
control: read_client_state kind=cookies on a second, unrelated path of the same origin. Identical attributes confirm the reading is about the cookie and not about the page that happened to be loaded.
payload_family: none -- a registry-owned passive client-state inventory. The class is the cookie attribute set, not a value.
runtime_writer: browser_driver.py:771 read_client_state stores the inventory as a JSON Artifact; the attribute projection is browser_driver.py:675-691 _cookie, which is where httpOnly, secure, sameSite, domain, path and prefix are written and where the value is not. The kind is registered at 20261210T000000Z__a_browser_reads_the_listener_before_it_speaks.sql:81 and the six-kind pattern at :65. The Observation is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function), INSERT INTO observations at :1116) as content_match over the stored inventory Artifact, provenance {tool_run} per 0018_vocabularies.sql:234. D4: the {tool_run} provenance is satisfied by the browse run itself, with no run_tool jq pass first -- browser_runs.tool_run_id is a foreign key into tool_runs (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:411-417) and enforce_kind_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) checks only the provenance_kind string, never which tool produced the run.
supported_evidence: neither of the two, and the ceiling is the point of the row. TEST_ACTION_KINDS is exactly ('request',) (src/redkraken/roster.py:415), so no browse step can be a Test action and close_test_replay writes nothing here. Support is an agent-filed edge on the Hypothesis, which rk2_promote_hypotheses writes with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530) -- but close_test_replay is the only writer of a testing -> supported transition (20260816T000000Z...:1125-1129) and rk2_finding_refusal requires one (20260815T120000Z...:642-649), so THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING on its own. Support is an agent-filed content_match edge over the stored cookie inventory. Pair it with the framing row's Receipt-backed Test on the same subject, which is where the Finding opens.
refuted_evidence: neither, for the same reason -- a SameSite=Strict session cookie beside an absent frame-ancestors weakens the framing claim rather than refuting it, and that judgement is recorded as a content_match edge with polarity refutes on the impact half, not as a Test outcome.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the inventory returns more entries than the driver will record canonically, or the plan cannot complete the login inside its step ceiling. course of action: stop the plan and report the framing reading without the cost modifier rather than guessing at SameSite. scope: this plan. resume: an operator supplies a shorter login path or names the cookie directly. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the plan, the steps that ran, and the explicit statement that SameSite was not read -- because 'not recorded' and 'SameSite=None' look identical in a report that does not say which.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, but only through the browser lane; the wire spelling the Playbook's step 1 asks for is permanently closed by proxy.py:376
notes: This row exists because browser-framing step 1 names Set-Cookie as one of the three headers its whole reading rests on, and that header is stripped from the agent view on every path. The Playbook instructs a step the harness cannot perform. The reading survives in the browser lane and nowhere else. The same inventory is the cookies Playbook's subject under session_handling.cookie_scope; this row carries only the half that decides how much a missing framing header costs. mined_from is empty because this row is the group's own reading, taken from the shipped Playbook and the served tool contracts rather than from a mining shard.

preconditions: form_request, state_changing_method, web_surface -- the three the Playbook already ships. Plus one its prose omits and this reading cannot run without: the route's agent transcript must be byte-identical across two immediately consecutive identical sends, because body_equals/body_differs hash the whole message. A Date at one-second granularity, a CSRF token, a request id or a rotating panel makes every arm differ and the verdict is inconclusive, not positive.
baseline: GET the document carrying the state-changing form, as whichever Identity the Task was opened under, with no Origin header. Record Content-Security-Policy (specifically frame-ancestors) and X-Frame-Options as served, citing the header text rather than a summary.
variant: GET a second route of the same deployment that the application itself frames, or that its login flow serves. The comparison is between two policies rather than one policy read alone: X-Frame-Options: DENY beside a CSP whose frame-ancestors is * is a framable page, and a grep for the header name reads it as protected.
control: The baseline GET sent immediately a second time, byte-for-byte unchanged, asserted body_equals. body_equals/body_differs compare receipts.response_agent_sha, which is the hash of the whole agent-view message including headers, so the Date header alone fires body_differs; without this arm a policy difference cannot be told from the clock.
payload_family: none -- served response-header policy values. The class is the framing directive: frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options DENY/SAMEORIGIN, and the ALLOW-FROM no current browser implements.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay derives the kind at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and inserts the observations row at :1072, off evaluate_test_assertions (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1503-1506) which compares receipts.response_agent_sha. That sha is the whole agent-view HTTP message -- status line, headers, body -- built by proxy.py:878-887 transcript() and stored at proxy.py:3105. The header_policy_observed the Playbook's bb:evidence declares is filed separately by promote_proposal at 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function) and :1116 (INSERT), provenance {receipt,tool_run} per 0018_vocabularies.sql:236, citing the same Receipt.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the variant action is named by the body_differs assertion against the baseline, so close_test_replay derives response_differential for it. The agent files header_policy_observed from the baseline Receipt as the supporting edge that names which directive was served; rk2_promote_hypotheses writes that edge with no filter on the cited kind.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- where the write document and the sibling hash identically, the served policy is uniform and no policy is missing on the write page in particular. The agent files header_policy_observed with polarity refutes naming the origins the policy does permit.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the two identical baseline sends do not produce the same response_agent_sha. course of action: stop the reading, do not send the variant, and do not narrow the comparison to a projection chosen after the fact. scope: this route only; the run continues on other routes. resume: when the route is re-read and the identical pair hashes equal, or when an operator names a stable sibling route. told: the operator who owns the Task, in the Task's own record. recorded: both Receipts, both hashes, and the verdict inconclusive with the reason 'transcript not byte-stable'.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: Nine mined rows filed this Playbook blocked on 'header_policy_observed has no runtime writer' and 'no assertion names a header'. Both are wrong. The kind is filable through promote_proposal, and body_differs already catches a header-only difference because the hashed artifact is the whole message. What is really missing is nothing; what the Playbook lacks is the byte-stability precondition, which is the corpus defect this row fixes -- browser-framing declares header_policy_observed with no runtime writer named and no statement of the one precondition the comparison needs.

technique: Ask whether page script writes a URL-supplied value into the cookie jar and reads it back on the next load as trusted data, turning a one-shot reflection into a stored one.

preconditions: web_surface, url_valued_parameter or any parameter the page's own script reads, cookie_parameter, and a browse plan. document.cookie is a sink as well as a source, and both halves of the round trip are inside the twelve actions.
baseline: browse: navigate to the page without the parameter, then read_client_state kind=cookies, and record the jar.
variant: In the same plan, navigate again with the parameter carrying a distinguishable value, then read_client_state kind=cookies again and capture_dom. A new cookie name, or a changed one, is the write.
control: Navigate a third time without the parameter and read the jar again. If the cookie is present in that arm too, the value came from the server and not from the URL, and the reading is over.
payload_family: a distinguishable inert marker in a client-read parameter -- searchable, not script, and not a value that would break the code that stores it.
runtime_writer: browser_driver.py:771 read_client_state with kind=cookies, projecting through browser_driver.py:675-691 _cookie, which stores the attributes and drops the value; capture_dom (browser_driver.py:803) stores the document. The Observation is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function), INSERT INTO observations at :1116) as reflected_input over the stored DOM Artifact, allowed_provenance {receipt,tool_run} per 0018_vocabularies.sql:226, satisfied here by the browse tool run. D4: the {tool_run} provenance is satisfied by the browse run itself, with no run_tool jq pass first -- browser_runs.tool_run_id is a foreign key into tool_runs (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:411-417) and enforce_kind_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) checks only the provenance_kind string, never which tool produced the run.
supported_evidence: neither of the two, and the ceiling is the point of the row. TEST_ACTION_KINDS is exactly ('request',) (src/redkraken/roster.py:415), so no browse step can be a Test action and close_test_replay writes nothing here. Support is an agent-filed edge on the Hypothesis, which rk2_promote_hypotheses writes with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530) -- but close_test_replay is the only writer of a testing -> supported transition (20260816T000000Z...:1125-1129) and rk2_finding_refusal requires one (20260815T120000Z...:642-649), so THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING on its own. Support is an agent-filed reflected_input edge naming the parameter and the cookie name it landed in.
refuted_evidence: neither -- the jar is identical with and without the parameter, filed as reflected_input with polarity refutes.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the marker chosen would execute, or would break the code that stores it. course of action: replace it with an inert searchable token and re-run; a payload that breaks the storing code destroys the very path that would show the link. scope: this plan. resume: immediately, with the inert marker. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the marker, both jars, and the captured DOM, so a later reading can find where the value resurfaces.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: The cookies Playbook reads the jar for scope and browser-storage reads the session out of storage; neither asks whether page script writes caller input into either, which is why this row sits here rather than there. The cookie VALUE is stripped before the Artifact exists, so the proof is the name and the attribute set plus the captured DOM, not the value read back.

technique: Ask whether the origin registers a service worker whose scope covers the authenticated routes, so a client-side component the page's own scripts can reach sits between the session and every response it sees.

preconditions: web_surface, authenticated_endpoint, stable_session, and a browse plan of at most 32 steps that can complete the login. read_client_state accepts kind service_workers -- the six-kind pattern is at 20261210T000000Z__a_browser_reads_the_listener_before_it_speaks.sql:65 and the six rows at :78-83, and roster.py:441 carries read_client_state in BROWSER_ACTIONS. No model-authored JavaScript is involved: the projection is the driver's.
baseline: browse: navigate to the origin unauthenticated, then read_client_state kind=service_workers. The registrations and versions visible before any session exists.
variant: In the same plan, complete the login, then repeat the read. A registration whose scopeURL covers the authenticated routes is the reading: responses to those routes pass through a component that outlives the page.
control: read_client_state kind=service_workers on a second path of the same origin under the same session. Identical registrations confirm the reading is about the ORIGIN's registration rather than about the page that happened to be loaded -- a worker registered by one route and not another is a different and weaker claim.
payload_family: none -- a registry-owned passive client-state inventory. The class is the registration's scopeURL and status, not a value.
runtime_writer: browser_driver.py:771 read_client_state, which calls _client_state at browser_driver.py:694; the service_workers branch is browser_driver.py:722-747, projecting registrationId, scopeURL and isDeleted off ServiceWorker.workerRegistrationUpdated and registrationId, scriptURL, status and runningStatus off ServiceWorker.workerVersionUpdated, and storing the result as a JSON Artifact. The Observation is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function) and :1116 (INSERT)) as content_match, allowed_provenance {tool_run} (0018_vocabularies.sql:234). D4: the browse run satisfies that provenance directly, with no run_tool jq pass first -- browser_runs.tool_run_id is a foreign key into tool_runs (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:411-417) and enforce_kind_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) checks only the provenance_kind string, never which tool produced the run.
supported_evidence: neither of the two, and the ceiling is the point of the row. TEST_ACTION_KINDS is exactly ('request',) (src/redkraken/roster.py:415), so no browse step can be a Test action and close_test_replay writes nothing here. Support is an agent-filed content_match edge over the two stored inventories, which rk2_promote_hypotheses writes with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530) -- but close_test_replay is the only writer of a testing -> supported transition (20260816T000000Z...:1125-1129) and rk2_finding_refusal requires one (20260815T120000Z...:642-649), so THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING on its own. Pair it with the delivery-and-replay row on the same subject.
refuted_evidence: neither -- no registration, or a registration whose scopeURL does not reach the authenticated routes, refutes the claim, and that is filed as content_match with polarity refutes over the two inventories.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the plan cannot complete the login inside its 32-step ceiling, or the inventory returns registrations for an origin other than the one under test. course of action: stop the plan and report the storage reading without the worker modifier rather than guessing at scope. scope: this plan. resume: an operator supplies a shorter login path. told: the operator who owns the Task, in the Task's own record. recorded: the plan, the steps that ran, both inventories, and the explicit statement that the worker's CACHE CONTENTS were not read -- the registry returns registrations and versions, not what a worker has stored, and 'not recorded' and 'nothing cached' must not look the same in a report.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, browser lane only.
notes: D11 routing sweep for a thin slug: browser-storage sat at three rows, and a text sweep of all 665 mined rows for client-storage language returned nothing routed away -- the six hits are browser-script, browser-messaging and attack-surface rows that belong where they are. So this row is not a recovered mined row; it is the sixth read_client_state kind, which no row in the ledger used. mined_from is empty because the reading comes from the registry itself (browser_client_state_kinds, 20261210T000000Z...:78-83). It is the same corpus defect the inventory row fixes: the shipped Playbook's step 4 says 'This harness has no action that reads Web Storage', which has been false since 20261210T000000Z, and service_workers is the kind that statement hides furthest. HONEST CEILING: the registry returns the registration and its scope, never the Cache Storage contents, so the claim is that a component exists in the path -- not that a response was cached.

technique: Ask whether the value the target delivered to page script authenticates on its own, by replaying it as the only credential on a Task holding no leased Identity and differencing that answer against the same route asked with nothing at all.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, read_method, web_surface, and stable_session as the baseline. One precondition the Playbook's prose does not state and the reading cannot survive without: identity.Session.inject (identity.py:329-338) removes every caller-set header whose name the origin's Identity owns and unconditionally replaces cookie, then appends its own. So 'send the route again with the body-borne value as the only credential and no cookie at all' is unachievable on a Task holding a lease -- the door will re-attach the session and the variant becomes the baseline. The variant arm runs on a Task opened with no Identity (anonymous_identity_available), and the body-borne value goes in a header name that Identity does not own.
baseline: The authenticated read as the Task's own leased Identity, with the whole exchange stored: the request that authenticated, the response body, and which field carried a token, a bearer, a session identifier, a signed blob or an API key. This is a separate Task from the variant and its Receipt is cited rather than replayed.
variant: On a Task with no leased Identity, the same route with the body-borne value as the only credential -- in Authorization, or in whatever header the page's own requests use -- and no cookie. The same authenticated content coming back is the reading.
control: On the same no-Identity Task, the same route carrying nothing at all, sent twice unchanged. The empty pair is the byte-stability check and the arm that rules out a route that answers the same thing to everyone; without it a route that never authenticated reads as a leak.
payload_family: caller-presented credential material recovered from the response body -- bearer token, session identifier, signed blob, API key -- replayed in the header the application's own scripts use. The class is a credential the target handed to script, not a payload.
runtime_writer: No Test writer: the variant presents the body-borne value in a request header and the replay lane sends none (see notes). The credential_effect the Playbook's bb:evidence declares for both the control and the variant is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function), INSERT INTO observations at :1116), allowed_provenance {receipt} (0018_vocabularies.sql:232), citing the leased-Identity Receipt, the token-only Receipt and the credential-less Receipt. rk2_promote_hypotheses writes all three edges (20261025T000000Z...:530).
supported_evidence: AGENT-FILED credential_effect, polarity supports, provenance {receipt} -- one edge from the leased-Identity baseline (the session works when held the intended way) and one from the token-only arm on the no-Identity Task (the same authenticated content came back with the script-readable value as the only credential). That pair is exactly what the Playbook declares. It is NOT response_differential: the token rides an Authorization or application-specific request header, which _Door.send never sends.
refuted_evidence: AGENT-FILED credential_effect, polarity refutes -- the token-only arm answers the way the credential-less arm does, so the body-borne value authenticates nothing and the session travels only in a cookie the page cannot read.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the value about to be replayed belongs to an Identity other than the Task's own, or the replay would spend rather than read -- a write verb, a consumed single-use token. course of action: stop; the Playbook is read_only and the credential it replays is the tester's own. scope: this route. resume: never for another Identity's value; for a write verb, only where an operator names it. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the field the value arrived in and the Receipt it arrived on, never the value itself, and never unredacted in the report.
owner_ticket: 211 -- reachable as a reading today, and it stops at an Observation rather than a Finding. Ticket 211, 'A Test action carries the header and the body it plans', is ready-for-agent and blocked by nothing, and ticket 101 is blocked by it; it is the ticket that closes this gap, priced in notes. The reading also needs a Task opened with NO leased Identity for the variant arm, because identity.Session.inject (identity.py:329-338) replaces caller-set cookie and every static Identity header; that is a Task-shape precondition, not a harness gap.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. The differential lives in a request HEADER, and a Test action carries only a method and a url: _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:340-351) calls proxy.spend with url= and method= and nothing else, though proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), and record_test_action compares the Receipt to the action over method, scheme, host, port and path alone (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1387-1397). close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the cited run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649). The reading itself IS performable -- mcp__rk2__http_request takes a headers object -- and the agent-filed Observation is a real hypothesis_evidence edge that rk2_promote_hypotheses writes with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530). It just cannot carry the Hypothesis to supported. The credential-less control pair on the no-Identity Task IS Test-expressible on its own (same url, same method, no caller headers) and is worth running as one, but it settles the route's behaviour toward an anonymous caller, not this claim. No mined row covers the Playbook's own core reading; the two that name browser-storage are both client-state inventories. Written from the Playbook itself, corrected on the one point that would have voided every run of it: without the no-leased-Identity Task, Session.inject makes the variant and the baseline the same request. That correction is the procedure this Playbook's declared credential_effect kind was missing. mined_from is empty because this row is the group's own reading, taken from the shipped Playbook and the served tool contracts rather than from a mining shard. PRICED, NOT PERMANENT -- ticket 211, 'A Test action carries the header and the body it plans' (docs/specs/production-harness-v2/issues/211-a-test-action-carries-the-header-and-the-body-it-plans.md), is ready-for-agent, blocked by nothing, and ticket 101 is blocked BY it. The wall this row works around is three edits deep and the parts are already in the tree: proxy.spend already takes headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:340-351) forwards two keyword arguments; receipts.request_agent_sha (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:59) already holds the whole agent-view request message and is written unconditionally on the same path as response_agent_sha (proxy.py:3279), so record_test_action (20260815T000000Z...:1387-1397) gains its header and body binding with no new column; and rk2_test_spec_problem's action key set (20260815T000000Z...:377) widens from five keys to seven. One migration and about two lines of Python. Per docs/research/playbook-state-of-the-art/00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:30-33 -- 'This is why the order is harness first' -- the rewrite must NOT harden this sentence into Playbook prose: it is a dated condition, and the corpus is written once against the capability that lands.
finding_path_note: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states

preconditions: web_surface, spa_surface or any page that authenticates in the browser, and a browse plan of at most 32 steps. The Playbook's step 4 asserts this reading is impossible; it is not. read_client_state accepts kind local_storage, session_storage, indexeddb_names, cookies, service_workers and message_listeners -- the pattern is at 20261210T000000Z__a_browser_reads_the_listener_before_it_speaks.sql:65 and the six rows at :78-83, and roster.py:441 carries read_client_state in BROWSER_ACTIONS.
baseline: browse: navigate to the origin unauthenticated, then read_client_state for each of local_storage, session_storage and indexeddb_names. Three inventories before any session exists.
variant: In the same plan, complete the login, then repeat the same three reads. Which keys appeared, and what they hold.
control: The unauthenticated inventory, so a key present in both arms is not read as a session artefact. Repeat one of the three reads on a second path of the same origin, so a key that follows the page is not read as a key that follows the session.
payload_family: none -- three registry-owned passive client-state inventories. Unlike the cookies kind these are not value-stripped, so what comes back is untrusted content in the ordinary sense.
runtime_writer: browser_driver.py:771 read_client_state, which calls _client_state at browser_driver.py:694 -- DOMStorage.getDOMStorageItems for local_storage and session_storage (browser_driver.py:696-711) and IndexedDB.requestDatabaseNames for indexeddb_names (:712-718) -- and stores the result as a JSON Artifact. The Observation is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function), INSERT INTO observations at :1116) as content_match over that Artifact, provenance {tool_run} per 0018_vocabularies.sql:234. D4: the {tool_run} provenance is satisfied by the browse run itself, with no run_tool jq pass first -- browser_runs.tool_run_id is a foreign key into tool_runs (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:411-417) and enforce_kind_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) checks only the provenance_kind string, never which tool produced the run.
supported_evidence: neither of the two, and the ceiling is the point of the row. TEST_ACTION_KINDS is exactly ('request',) (src/redkraken/roster.py:415), so no browse step can be a Test action and close_test_replay writes nothing here. Support is an agent-filed edge on the Hypothesis, which rk2_promote_hypotheses writes with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z...:530) -- but close_test_replay is the only writer of a testing -> supported transition (20260816T000000Z...:1125-1129) and rk2_finding_refusal requires one (20260815T120000Z...:642-649), so THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING on its own. The Hypothesis is carried by agent-filed content_match edges over the before/after inventories; the Finding needs the Receipt-backed Test, which is the delivery-and-replay row above on the same subject.
refuted_evidence: neither -- an inventory identical before and after authentication refutes the persistence claim, and that is filed as content_match with polarity refutes over the two stored Artifacts.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: an inventory returns a value that is plainly a live credential, or the driver refuses the read because the inventory exceeds what it will record canonically. course of action: stop reading further keys, do not carry values into a later request from this Playbook, and route the credential to the replay row above where the reading is bounded. scope: this plan. resume: when the reading is re-opened under the replay row, whose stop conditions govern spending. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the key names and the fact of the value, redacted; handle-untrusted-content governs everything that comes back.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: This row is the corpus defect fix for browser-storage. Step 4 of the shipped Playbook says: 'This harness has no action that reads Web Storage. There is no probe for localStorage, no probe for sessionStorage, and adding one would be adding an expression evaluated in the page.' All three sentences are stale -- the action exists, it is registry-owned, and it evaluates no model-authored expression. The Playbook's honest half survives and is worth keeping: a value in a closure or a memory-held store is still not seen, and a reading that wants to assert where the value lives reports inconclusive for that part. What changes is that localStorage and sessionStorage are now among the things it CAN assert.

technique: Ask whether a host the served document already trusts is a name nobody currently holds, by requesting it and reading a hosting provider's own disowning document out of the body, against a fabricated label under the same provider suffix that must produce the same document.

preconditions: web_surface plus a candidate list that came from the target's own served bytes -- CSP source-list entries, script and link src hosts, storage and CDN hostnames pulled out by js_map, js_parse or js_routes. There is no DNS tool: run_tool is exactly jq, js_map, js_parse and js_routes, so dig, subfinder and subzy have no equivalent and the candidate list cannot come from a sweep. Each candidate host must be inside the Program's scope grant. And the candidate must ANSWER: a name that does not resolve leaves receipts.response_agent_sha null, and evaluate_test_assertions returns NULL for a body assertion over a null sha (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1500-1502), which is inconclusive and not a refutation.
baseline: GET a host named in the same trusted-source list that is plainly in use, sent twice unchanged. Two hundreds with the vendor's real content, hashing equal, is what a claimed name looks like and is the byte-stability arm.
variant: GET the candidate host. A body carrying a provider's unclaimed-resource string -- NoSuchBucket, 'There isn't a GitHub Pages site here.', a PaaS domain-mapping-not-found, a registry repository-not-found -- is a reference the application still emits pointing at a resource nobody holds.
control: GET a fabricated random label under the same provider suffix, which must return the SAME disowning document. That is what proves the shape means 'nobody owns this' rather than 'this host is down', and it is the arm the whole reading turns on. A second control worth the request: a path the serving host certainly does not have, which must return the deployment's own not-found -- if the candidate's body and the deployment's own 404 are the same document, the fingerprint proved nothing.
payload_family: none -- hostnames extracted from the target's own served bytes, requested unchanged. The class of value read back is the provider's disowning document, not a payload.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, tech_sql, and a sort or pagination parameter that is not an allow-list -- usually in a POST body. This is the parameter the Playbook's step 1 ranks first, and for a reason that is the whole technique: SQL has no bind placeholder for an identifier, so ORDER BY $col and LIMIT $n are hand-built even in codebases that parameterise everything else.
baseline: sort = a real column. Rows in that order, sent twice unchanged for stability.
variant: sort = an expression rather than a name -- a CASE that orders one way when a condition holds and another when it does not. Which of the two orderings comes back is the boolean, and it needs no error at all.
control: sort = a column that certainly does not exist. It must produce an error or leave the order unchanged. If it is identical to the baseline the parameter is not reaching the query and the expression arm proves nothing. Backticks around the value are a common false comfort and do not close the identifier context.
payload_family: identifier-position values -- a real column name, a nonexistent one, and an order-determining expression. The differential is over result ORDERING, which is cheap and needs no error and no extraction.

supported_evidence: response_differential -- the expression arm is named by body_differs against the real-column arm, and the ordering it produced is the one the expression predicts.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the expression arm, the real-column arm and the nonexistent-column arm all hash together, so the parameter is an allow-list lookup and not a concatenated identifier.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the ordering does not change under any arm, or the nonexistent column produces the baseline answer. course of action: stop; the parameter is bound or allow-listed and the reading is refuted or void respectively. scope: this parameter. resume: with the next-ranked parameter, per the Playbook's own ordering. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the three orderings and the expression used, never a column name read out of the catalogue.

It is carried here because the sort parameter is this Playbook's own step-1 first preference and no mined row covers it under this slug. The distinction the two Playbooks split on is the one the shipped step 6 already draws: where the input decides which stored field the query filters on, the class is injection.query_field and the Playbook is orm; where it is concatenated into the statement text, it is this one. mined_from is empty because this row is the group's own reading, taken from the shipped Playbook and the served tool contracts rather than from a mining shard.

technique: Ask whether a text grader between the caller and the database, rather than the database, decided the response -- first by sending an obviously hostile value on a parameter the application does not consume, then by re-spelling the rejected payload once so the bytes fall outside the enumerated set while staying inside what the engine's grammar accepts.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, plus a surface map that says which parameter names the route actually consumes, so 'unused' is a fact and not an assumption.
baseline: The route with an unused parameter carrying an inert value -- the ordinary response, unchanged, because the application ignores the parameter. Sent twice, which is the byte-stability arm.
variant: Two spellings, one axis. First: the same unused parameter carrying an obviously hostile value. A 406, a 403 or a challenge page there is a filter, because the parameter cannot possibly reach a query. Second: the payload the route already rejected, re-sent with ONE minimal transformation that changes the bytes a signature matches without changing what the engine would parse -- an inline comment where a space was, mixed case in a keyword, a dollar-quoted string where a quote was.
control: The neutral value re-sent alongside, under the same conditions. Three outcomes, three verdicts: still rejected and identical, consistent with the value never reaching a parser; accepted and matching the neutral baseline, a filter was grading and the database treats the value as data; accepted and differing from the neutral baseline, the filter was the only thing between the caller and a parser, which is the strongest of the three because it names both defects.
payload_family: one minimal re-spelling of a rejected value, never a chain -- a chained transformation that succeeds says nothing about which link mattered. The generalisable rule is to spell so the bytes fall outside the deny list's enumerated set while remaining inside the engine's grammar; a deny list that strips a fixed word list plus space, semicolon and /**/ misses /***/ and every mixed case.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072, off receipts.response_agent_sha.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the re-spelled arm is named by status_differs or body_differs against the neutral control, and the differing status is the accept/reject flip.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the hostile value on the unused parameter changes nothing and the re-spelling changes nothing, so no grader is deciding and the refusal, where there was one, came from the application.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the re-spelled payload gets past the filter. course of action: stop, unless the bypassed request produces a differential the neutral baseline does not. Getting past the filter is not a result -- a managed WAF in front of parameterised queries can be walked around all day and every bypass proves only that the WAF has gaps, which its vendor documents. scope: this route. resume: with the boolean pair, on the now-unfiltered spelling. told: the operator who owns the Task, if a bypass was found and no differential followed, because that is a note about the filter and not a finding. recorded: the transformation applied, the three outcomes, and the verdict each implies.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: The Playbook's step 5 already sends an equally hostile string that is not valid SQL in that position, and that control is entangled with the route: it still goes to a parameter the application reads, so a differential from it has two possible authors. The unused-parameter probe is cleanly disentangled and costs one request. Recommend it be added AHEAD of the existing third arm rather than instead of it -- they answer different questions: is there a grader at all, and did the grader produce this particular differential.

technique: Ask whether a value stored cleanly by one route is concatenated into a statement by a different route later, by storing two values that differ only in a clause the engine would evaluate and differencing the READING route's two answers.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, state_changing_method on the write route. The reading route must be reachable by the same Identity, and the stored field must be one the Identity is allowed to set on itself. Two Artifacts per arm -- the write and the read -- and a read route that is byte-stable. AND the write has to be expressible as a method and a url: _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:340-351) sends no body for an action or a setup step, and sql-injection is bb:effects: read_only so a Task whose whole selection is read_only opens with body_allowed: false anyway (_body_allowed, src/redkraken/execution.py:3646). Where the store takes its value in the query string the whole reading is one Test and reaches a Finding; where the store needs a form or JSON body, the two writes happen on mcp__rk2__http_request under a Task whose selection is not entirely read_only, the Test shrinks to nothing, and the row stops at an agent-filed Observation.
baseline: Store an ordinary value, then read the profile route twice. Two identical reads establish what unchanged looks like on a route that carries a session and a timestamp; without that pair the whole reading is noise with a verdict attached.
variant: Store a value carrying a clause that evaluates true, then read the same route.
control: Store the neutralised twin -- same length, same metacharacters, clause evaluates false -- and read again. Both arms went through the same write path, so the write is not a variable between them. The write action is deliberately named by no assertion, so it stays response_invariant and claims nothing.
payload_family: an inert, searchable marker carrying one clause -- a token that will show up in a later response body without being SQL. Never a payload that breaks the second query: that destroys the very route that would have shown the link.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072, deriving response_differential for the READ action because the body_differs assertion names it and response_invariant for the write action because no differencing assertion names it. The stored-marker anchor the reference calls for is filed by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function) and :1116 (INSERT)) as state_change from the WRITE Receipt, allowed_provenance {receipt} (0018_vocabularies.sql:230).
supported_evidence: response_differential on the READ action -- body_differs between the two stored-value arms.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two read answers hash identically against a read baseline that was itself stable, so the stored value was bound rather than concatenated by the second route.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the value about to be planted is one the reading would not accept firing at an unknown time, on an unknown route, with nobody watching. course of action: replace it with the inert marker and re-plant; a value stored during a reading may fire days later in a batch job, in a report nobody requested this week, in an export a human triggers by hand, long after the reading that planted it closed as refuted. scope: this subject. resume: with the inert marker. told: the operator who owns the Task, and the marker goes in the record so a later effect can be traced back to the request that caused it. recorded: the marker, the field, the write Receipt, both read Receipts, and the state_change anchor.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: sqli-advanced-sqli-techniques.md calls second order the most valuable idea in the pack and says the Playbook cannot chase it on its own because it reads one subject. It can, if the two arms are both writes and only the read is asserted on -- the differential lands on the reading route and needs no cross-Task anchor to be a verdict. The reference's state_change anchor is still worth writing and IS writable (correction 3 confirms promote_proposal files it under {receipt} provenance from the write Receipt); it is the handle a later reading needs, not the evidence this one closes on. Second-order readings produce the most confident wrong answers in this class in both directions, which is why the inert marker and the recorded anchor are stop conditions rather than advice. ON THE FINDING PATH only in the query-string spelling of the write; the body spelling stops at an agent-filed state_change plus reflected_input pair with no Finding behind it, for the reason in preconditions. Ticket 211 removes this condition and ticket 101 is blocked by it; do not harden it into Playbook prose (docs/research/playbook-state-of-the-art/00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:30-33, 'the order is harness first').

technique: Ask whether the database evaluated a clause the caller supplied, by sending two arms whose values differ only in a clause the engine resolves true or false and differencing the two stored responses against a baseline that was checked for stability first.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql. The parameter comes from the state view rather than out of the URL, ranked sort column, then pagination bound, then filter, then anything else. The engine must be named first, because the control has to parse on it. One further precondition the Playbook does not state: where the route requires a fresh anti-CSRF token or a value that may not repeat, every arm returns the same rejection and the route reads as not injectable -- harvest the token per request from a response the same Identity can fetch, and where it is bound to something the model cannot set, the verdict is inconclusive rather than refuted.
baseline: The request with the parameter carrying an ordinary value, sent twice, unchanged, both through mcp__rk2__http_request as whichever Identity the Task was opened under.
variant: The same request with a clause the engine evaluates to true appended -- value' AND '1'='1 in the quoted form, or the numeric form the quote-only reading misses entirely: id=7 against id=8-1, which is arithmetic the engine performed and needs no quote and no error.
control: The same value, same length, same metacharacters, with the clause evaluating false. It is a control in the strongest sense available because it contains every character the variant does; a control that drops the quote differs in the encoding AND in what a filter would match, and the comparison then has two variables. The identical baseline pair is the second control and it is not optional: body_equals/body_differs compare receipts.response_agent_sha, the hash of the whole agent message, so a Date header alone fires body_differs. Three rounds of the pair, six requests, interleaved with the baseline rather than sent as a block, because backend latency and deployment state drift on the scale of seconds.
payload_family: a clause the engine resolves to a constant truth value, in the quoting the enclosure requires -- and its length-matched, metacharacter-matched negation. Not a payload list: one clause, two truth values.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay derives the kind at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and inserts the observations row at :1072, off evaluate_test_assertions (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1503-1506) comparing receipts.response_agent_sha.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the true arm is named by body_differs against the false arm, so close_test_replay derives response_differential for both actions. Supported requires all three: the two arms differ in every round, the two baseline requests were invariant against each other, and the filter probe did not reproduce the true arm.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two arms are invariant against each other against a baseline that was itself stable. The value went in as data and came out as data, and the Playbook writes the refutation down with its own evidence rather than leaving the hypothesis open for the next Task to re-test.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the two identical baseline requests do not hash equal, or a differential appears in one round of three and not the other two, or the route answers 403 to every arm, or the query result never reaches the response at all. course of action: where nothing holds still, this Playbook cannot read the route and says so; where the rounds disagree, the verdict is inconclusive rather than supported, because two agreeing rounds cannot tell a stable difference from a coincidence that happened twice. scope: this endpoint and this parameter. resume: an operator names a stable projection or a different parameter; a re-read is a new baseline, never an edit to this one. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: all eight Receipts, what moved between the two baselines, and the projection fixed BEFORE the conditional pair was sent -- fixing it afterwards is how the answer you hoped for appears.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: Four mined rows collapse here -- the tautology-against-its-negation, the boolean oracle where nothing is printed, the arithmetic-equivalence numeric form, and the token-harvesting precondition. They are one reading with one control design. The numeric form is kept inside rather than split out because it answers the same question with a different carrier and shares the neutralised-twin discipline; it is worth naming explicitly because a quote-only reading walks past every route that concatenates into arithmetic.
