preconditions: the filter-clause row above already established a stable two-way response split on this route. query_parameter, and a lookup whose filter the reading has already shown it can close and re-open.
baseline: The injected disjunction naming an attribute that certainly does not exist -- <term>)(|(<nonexistent-attribute>=* -- which must return the FALSE shape. Sent twice unchanged.
variant: The same disjunction naming a foreign attribute the application never queries -- description, then mail, then memberOf, one arm each and pairwise, since compare_responses differences exactly two Artifacts (ticket 109). A TRUE shape says the attribute exists on the entry.
control: The same disjunction against a search term known to match no entry. It must stay FALSE. If it returns TRUE the clause is matching the whole directory rather than that entry, and every attribute claim taken under it is unsupported. This is the arm the whole reading turns on.
payload_family: an injected LDAP disjunction naming a foreign attribute, and the same disjunction over an attribute name that cannot exist. The question is EXISTENCE of the attribute on the entry -- never its value.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay derives the kind at 20260816T000000Z...:1064-1069 and inserts at :1072, off evaluate_test_assertions (20260815T000000Z...:1503-1506) over receipts.response_agent_sha.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the foreign-attribute arm is named by body_differs against the nonexistent-attribute arm, against a control that stayed FALSE for an entry that does not exist. ON THE FINDING PATH in the query-string lookup spelling.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the foreign attribute and the nonexistent one return the same shape, so the clause is confined to the attributes the application already queries and the primitive does not pivot.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: an attribute's existence has been established, or the no-such-entry control returned TRUE. course of action: stop at attribute EXISTENCE. Do not chain into per-character extraction of userPassword or any credential-bearing attribute on a live target; that is the refused extraction row. scope: this parameter on this route; the run continues elsewhere. resume: an operator names a further spelling worth one request each, with a reason. told: the operator who owns the Task, in the Task's own record. recorded: both Receipts per arm, the attribute names tried, the control's verdict, and the explicit statement that no attribute value was read.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable in the query-string lookup spelling.
notes: ROUTING (D6.3): orphans.json folded[4] and folded[5] routed the XPath and LDAP readings to g03/sql-injection and this group had not written them; the repair pass does. The destination contradiction the critic flagged is settled in the source and not by preference: structured-injection's own prose sends these here -- 'Where the value reaches a query rather than a document parser, the class is injection.query_language and the Playbook is sql-injection' (src/redkraken/playbooks/structured-injection/playbook.md:122-126) -- and structured-injection's bb:outputs is ["injection.document_parser"] alone, so it may not emit the class these readings produce. sql-injection's bb:outputs is ["injection.query_language"] and does. Distinct from the prefix oracle: that one asks what the value is, this one asks what the schema is, and the mined row says so in as many words. Both stop short of reading a value. CAVEAT: most LDAP attributes are case-insensitive, so any value this family recovers is case-folded.

preconditions: the filter-clause row above already established that a caller-supplied clause is evaluated, and the route already answers differently for a matching and a non-matching lookup. AND one the sources do not state: the reading must already know the value it tests a prefix of, from what the application itself displays. A prefix predicate over an unknown value is the extraction ladder and is refused.
baseline: A substring predicate that cannot match -- (attr=\7f*) over an attribute the entry has -- which must return the FALSE shape. Sent twice unchanged, which is also the byte-stability arm.
variant: The same substring predicate carrying the first character of a value the application already displays for that entry -- (attr=<known-first-char>*) -- which must return the TRUE shape. One character, already public, and no second character.
control: Both predicates re-sent unchanged at the end of the run. If the TRUE and FALSE shapes have drifted, the split was application state, a lockout or a rate limiter rather than the filter, and every verdict taken under it is void. A second control: the same known-good prefix against an entry that does not exist, which must return the FALSE shape -- otherwise the clause is matching the directory rather than the entry.
payload_family: an LDAP substring wildcard over an attribute whose value the reading already knows -- (attr=<known-prefix>*) and an impossible-byte twin. Exactly two requests, plus their re-reads. Never an alphabet.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay derives the kind at 20260816T000000Z...:1064-1069 and inserts at :1072, off evaluate_test_assertions (20260815T000000Z...:1503-1506) over receipts.response_agent_sha.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the known-prefix arm is named by body_differs or status_differs against the impossible-prefix twin, and the split is stable across the end-of-run re-read. ON THE FINDING PATH in the query-string lookup spelling.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two prefixes return the same shape, so the clause is evaluated but the substring match is not reading the stored value, and the primitive is narrower than it looked.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the oracle has been confirmed on the one already-public character, or the end-of-run re-read shows the shapes have drifted. course of action: stop. Do not send a second character, and do not sweep an alphabet -- full extraction is a volume problem rather than a proof problem, the request count grows as alphabet x length, and it is the refused extraction row in this Playbook. scope: this parameter on this route; the run continues elsewhere. resume: an operator names a further spelling worth one request each, with a reason. told: the operator who owns the Task, in the Task's own record. recorded: both Receipts, the exact predicates, the re-read verdict, and the explicit statement that the tested character was already public.
owner_ticket: 101 -- reachable. The class this reading demonstrates the primitive FOR, information_disclosure.identifier_oracle, is one of the nine no Playbook emits, and ticket 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs (D3). The row's own class, injection.query_language, sql-injection emits.
notes: ROUTING (D6.3): orphans.json folded[4] and folded[5] routed the XPath and LDAP readings to g03/sql-injection and this group had not written them; the repair pass does. The destination contradiction the critic flagged is settled in the source and not by preference: structured-injection's own prose sends these here -- 'Where the value reaches a query rather than a document parser, the class is injection.query_language and the Playbook is sql-injection' (src/redkraken/playbooks/structured-injection/playbook.md:122-126) -- and structured-injection's bb:outputs is ["injection.document_parser"] alone, so it may not emit the class these readings produce. sql-injection's bb:outputs is ["injection.query_language"] and does. Kept as its own row rather than folded into the filter-clause row because it answers a different question: that one asks whether the clause is evaluated, this one asks whether the clause can READ. The distinction is what decides the severity of the finding and it is the distinction the mined rows draw too. Bounded to an already-public character by this group, not by the source: the source walks the alphabet and calls it the technique. CAVEAT: most LDAP attributes are case-insensitive, so a recovered value is case-folded and the report must not claim the casing.

preconditions: would be: the quoting already known to break, otherwise both arms fail at the first statement and the comparison is about nothing.
baseline: would be: the inert value, twice, to fix the projection.
variant: would be: the enclosure, a separator, then a second statement that is valid and does nothing.
control: would be: the same length, same separator, same metacharacters, with the second statement deliberately misspelled so it cannot parse. If the two responses are identical, nothing parsed past the separator and the sink does not stack.
payload_family: a no-op second statement and its unparseable twin -- the read_only reduction of the stacked-query family, which selects a constant and touches nothing.
runtime_writer: none is exercised. As with the shape row, the evidence layer is not the obstacle: it is a body difference close_test_replay would write as response_differential (20260816T000000Z:1069, :1072). Naming that here is what makes the refusal legible as a decision.
supported_evidence: none exercised -- would be response_differential.
refuted_evidence: none exercised -- would be response_invariant.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: any payload carrying a statement separator. course of action: refuse, per the shipped Playbook's step 7 ('stack a second statement') and sqli.md's flat refusal of stacked queries. scope: this Playbook. resume: only on a decision by whoever owns the read_only line. told: the operator who owns the Task and the ledger. recorded: the refusal and the argument against it, so the argument is not re-derived from scratch by the next reading.
owner_ticket: NEW: 'Decide whether the stacked-query refusal should read "stacked queries that do anything" rather than "stacked queries"'
notes: The corpus refuses stacked queries on the grounds that 'a second statement is a write by construction'. That is true of every stacked payload the v1 pages contain and false of this one, and the distinction matters a lot: whether the sink stacks is the single fact that separates a contained injection from one that reaches file writes and command execution, and it is the fact a triager most wants in the report. A no-op second statement answers it at zero risk. Filed refused because the Playbook's prose refuses it, with the ticket that would change the prose -- not softened into reachable from this seat.

technique: Ask, as a boolean over an oracle that already works, whether the injection context holds a privilege -- server-role membership, superuser, bulk-operations or the file roles -- instead of proving it by attempting the privileged action.

preconditions: a working boolean oracle -- this row is worthless before the ordinary pair has succeeded and worth a lot immediately after -- plus the engine named, since the predicate is dialect-specific.
baseline: The confirmed true arm and false arm from the ordinary boolean pair, so the oracle is known to work before it is asked a question whose answer is unknown.
variant: The privilege predicate substituted into the true-arm position -- IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin')=1 or the fn_my_permissions bulk-operations count on MSSQL, current_setting('is_superuser')='on' or the pg_roles membership query for pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files and pg_execute_server_program on PostgreSQL.
control: The negation of the same predicate. Exactly one of the two must return the true response; if both do, or neither, the oracle is not reading what the reading thinks it is and the answer is discarded.
payload_family: a privilege predicate substituted into an established boolean position -- a class of yes/no questions about the injection context's own authority, never a payload that exercises it.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the predicate arm is named by body_differs against its own negation.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the predicate and its negation return the same answer, so the oracle is not reading the predicate and the row concludes nothing.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: a true answer to a privilege predicate. course of action: record the answer and do NOT act on it. A true IS_SRVROLEMEMBER is a sentence in the impact section, not a licence to run the next payload; the step after WAITFOR DELAY that proves the injection is not another confirmation of the injection, it is an action on a domain-joined host. scope: this parameter, and the run for the escalation family. resume: never on this Playbook; command execution, file read, file write, linked servers, OPENROWSET, EXECUTE AS and impersonation are all out. told: the operator who owns the Task, because the answer changes the report's severity and nothing else. recorded: the predicate, its negation, both answers, and the engine the fingerprint step named.

notes: HIGH VALUE, and it is the cleanest answer to a real tension in the corpus. sqli-remote-code-execution.md argues impact belongs in the narrative 'argued from what the finding permits', and the best evidence it can source is 'whether errors indicate an unusually privileged role' -- an inference from an error string. This turns that inference into an evidenced boolean at the cost of two requests, with no write, no extraction and no configuration change. It is precisely the step that lets the Playbook keep refusing xp_cmdshell while still reporting at the right severity.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, a confirmed enclosure, a route whose response identifies WHICH record it returned, and one scalar whose value the reading can predict from application state the target already displays.
baseline: The enclosure plus AND id=1 and a comment, which returns the record whose id is 1 and establishes that the injected equality steers row selection at all. Sent twice for stability.
variant: AND id=(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a relation the application itself exposes), with the record predicted in advance from a count the application already displays.
control: The same scalar plus one. The engine must return the NEXT record. A text grader reproducing bodies cannot produce an off-by-one shift in row identity, which is what makes this control stronger than the neutralised twin: it is satisfiable only by something that evaluated arithmetic and selected a row.
payload_family: a scalar expression the reading can predict from public state, used as a row selector. Non-sensitive by construction: a count or a constant expression, never a byte of somebody's password.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the two predicted-row arms are named by body_differs against each other, and each response carries the record identity the reading named before sending.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two arms return the same record, so the injected equality steers nothing.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the scalar being predicted is not derivable from public application state, or a step proposes to substitute a scalar over the target's data. course of action: refuse the second -- the source file's own version selects ASCII(SUBSTRING(password,1,1)) and reads a bcrypt hash one character per request, which is the refused extraction row wearing this row's clothes. scope: this parameter. resume: with a non-sensitive scalar, or not at all. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the predicted record identity, sent BEFORE the request, and the record that came back.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: HIGH VALUE and it belongs in the shipped Playbook as an optional step 3b. sqli-blind-sql-injection.md names the confirmation-bias trap precisely -- the signal is small, the observer chooses the projection, and somewhere between comparing full bodies and comparing status codes is a projection that shows exactly the difference you were hoping for. Its answer is a discipline (fix the projection first). This is the mechanical version of the same discipline: a predicted row identity fixes the projection before the request is sent and cannot be satisfied by a text grader. It is the strongest read_only evidence in this Playbook.

technique: Make a deliberately impossible type cast carry the evaluated constant back in the response, and prove the engine evaluated it by sending two casts that differ only in the constant, so the differing bytes ARE the constant.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, a known enclosure, and a route that returns the engine's own message rather than a generic handler page -- which is frequently gated behind a header the caller can set, and where it is, that gate is its own reading and belongs to exceptional-conditions.
baseline: An inert value, then a cast that cannot fail: the enclosure plus AND 0=CAST((SELECT 1) AS INT) and a comment. Sent twice for stability.
variant: The same statement with an impossible cast of a constant the reading chose: AND 0=CAST((SELECT 'AAAA') AS INT).
control: The same statement, same length, same failure mode, one different constant: AND 0=CAST((SELECT 'BBBB') AS INT). If the two bodies differ, the differing bytes are the constant, and the engine both evaluated the expression and surfaced its result -- with no target data read. If the control produces the same error as the variant, the error is about the type and not about an injection, which is the pairing PostgreSQL's helpfulness makes essential: a verbose, quoted, positioned error with a HINT line looks exactly like proof and is also what a failed integer cast of a query parameter produces.
payload_family: an impossible cast over a constant the READING supplied -- two constants of the same length, chosen for distinguishability and nothing else. Never a cast of VERSION(), a table name, or an aggregate over the catalogue: that is the refused extraction row.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072, off receipts.response_agent_sha. The error text is filed alongside by promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function) and :1116 (INSERT)) as error_detail, allowed_provenance {receipt,tool_run} (0018_vocabularies.sql:227), citing the same Receipt.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the two constant arms are named by body_differs against each other, so close_test_replay derives response_differential. The error_detail edge names the mechanism the differential proves.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two constant arms hash identically, so the message is the same whatever was cast and nothing evaluated the expression.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: a step proposes to cast something other than a constant the reading supplied. course of action: refuse; casting VERSION(), a table name or STRING_AGG over information_schema is the extraction row and is refused. scope: this parameter. resume: never for the extraction form. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: both constants, both messages, and the note that the reading read nothing belonging to the target.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: HIGH VALUE. Both engine references pin their error step on an error_detail observation and require a neutralised control before promoting anything. Correction 3 confirms error_detail IS filable via promote_proposal from a Receipt, so the references are not stranded -- but the Test that CLOSES still writes only one of two kinds, and 'the message says X' is not one of them. Swapping the assertion from 'the message says X' to 'the message differs between two constants' keeps the same control discipline, lands the closing Observation inside what close_test_replay writes, and keeps error_detail as the supporting edge. That correction should propagate to sqli-postgresql-specific-techniques.md and sqli-intro-to-mssql-sql-server.md. MSSQL messages are unusually descriptive, frequently quoting the offending fragment, which makes this channel more productive there and the corresponding false positive more likely.

preconditions: a confirmed boolean-observable injection point. This step runs BEFORE the boolean pair is trusted on a strict engine: PostgreSQL refuses '1' = 1 where MySQL accepts it, so an arm written in incompatible types is a syntax error being reported as a differential.
baseline: The enclosure plus AND 1=1, which is the true response, and the enclosure plus AND 1=2, which is the false one. Both already established.
variant: A tautology built from a function only one family implements -- a conversion or connection function on MySQL, the version expression on PostgreSQL, the family-specific numeric function on MSSQL -- one arm each. Matching the true response says the function parsed there.
control: An expression no family implements, which shows that a rejection means the parser looked rather than that the route rejects unfamiliar bytes. Where the engine-specific form matches the FALSE response rather than the true one, the function did not parse on that engine, which is also an answer.
payload_family: dialect discriminators -- a function-existence tautology per family, and one expression no family implements. The fingerprint stays minimal: enough to pick the control, and no more. Not @@VERSION, which is a read of the target's configuration the reading does not need.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072. Reads no error message, so the reading does not depend on error_detail at all.
supported_evidence: response_differential -- the family-specific arm is named by body_differs against the known-false response and body_equals against the known-true one.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every family-specific arm matches the false response and the no-family control does too, so nothing is parsing and the fingerprint is unavailable.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the engine is named. course of action: stop. The fingerprint exists to build a control that parses -- concatenation is || on PostgreSQL and + on MSSQL, and a control written in the wrong dialect is a syntax error being reported as a differential -- and it never runs in order to escalate. scope: this parameter. resume: not needed. told: nobody; this is an internal step. recorded: the engine, and the fact that it was established by acceptance rather than by clock or by error text.

notes: The Playbook's step 1 makes naming the engine mandatory and gives no procedure for it that does not read an error. This is the procedure, and it lands on evidence the harness is allowed to write. Both engine references make the same point from the dialect side: a control built with || errors on MSSQL and the resulting differential is entirely the reading's own doing.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, a confirmed enclosure, a recorded out-of-band channel (ticket 98), a correlator unique per request, a window long enough for a queued job, and the discipline to call a late arrival uncorrelatable rather than positive.
baseline: A request with an inert value and no name to resolve, with the collector watching. No arrival is expected, and its absence over the same window is what makes an arrival mean anything.
variant: The injected expression with a correlator unique to this request in the hostname it resolves.
control: A CONTROL arrival fired at the channel directly, to prove the channel is alive and the collector is reading it during this window. A control arrival writes NO Observation -- is_control and a null subject are one state tied by a CHECK (20261001T000000Z__a_control_arrival_is_what_makes_silence_a_finding.sql:42-52) -- and that is exactly right here: it establishes liveness without pretending to be evidence about the subject.
payload_family: a name-resolving expression whose hostname is a correlator the runtime minted for this subject. The correlator carries NO target data: the line between this row and the refused exfiltration row is exactly whether it does, and the two payload shapes are one edit apart.
runtime_writer: record_callback_interaction, whose current definition is 20261001T000000Z__a_control_arrival_is_what_makes_silence_a_finding.sql:323 over the original at 20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:659. The kind callback_interaction is registered is_evidential = true with allowed_provenance {callback} at 20260812T040000Z:348-350. The edge onto the Hypothesis is written by rk2_promote_hypotheses (20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:66) from an agent-supplied observation_id, with no filter on the cited kind.
supported_evidence: neither of the two -- and that is not a block. The arrival is a callback_interaction, which is evidential, and it carries a bar as a hypothesis_evidence edge. What it cannot do is close a Test: close_test_replay writes only the two kinds, and a Finding needs a closed Test (findings.opened_by_test_run_id), so this row supports the Hypothesis and the Finding needs a Receipt-backed lane. Provenance is {callback} alone, so no Receipt may be filed under this kind.
refuted_evidence: neither -- silence is not a refutation. No arrival over the declared window against a live control arrival is inconclusive: the expression may not have executed, or the resolver may not have reached the channel, and this reading cannot tell those apart.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: an arrival lands outside the declared window, or a correlator arrives that no request in this run minted. course of action: call it uncorrelatable and do not report it. Batch jobs run on their own schedule and shared collaborator space receives lookups from crawlers, sandboxes and payloads somebody else planted months ago on Programs nobody here is testing. scope: this reading. resume: with a fresh correlator and a declared window. told: the operator who owns the Task. recorded: the correlator per request, the window, the control arrival, and the honest claim -- an arrival says something on the target's network resolved a name, which is weaker than 'the database evaluated my expression': a WAF resolving hostnames it finds in bodies, a logging pipeline enriching records, and a security product detonating suspicious strings each produce the same signal.

notes: sqli-out-of-band-dns.md refuses this on five grounds and two of them are now factually wrong: 'it needs infrastructure the Playbook does not have' and 'correlation between a lookup and a request' are both supplied by ticket 98's recorded channel. Its remaining three objections survive and are carried above as the guard rails, because they are good ones. Two limits are real and are stated rather than softened: an SMB-speaking listener does not exist and is not wanted, so the UNC-path spellings that capture NetNTLM are the refused row and not this one -- same function, same statement shape, one changed hostname, two completely different dispositions, which is exactly the kind of adjacency a refusal gets walked around by accident.

preconditions: none available, and the refusal is about cost rather than capability.
baseline: not executed
variant: not executed
control: not executed
payload_family: a self-referential XPath count() stacked inside a predicate. Its cost is superlinear in the size of the document being walked, and the reading cannot know that size before it sends.
runtime_writer: none. No runtime path writes an Observation for a reading that never runs; recorded so the absence is a decision on the record rather than a gap somebody fills.
supported_evidence: none
refuted_evidence: none
stop_conditions: halt trigger: a run proposes a payload whose cost to the target is not bounded before it is sent -- a self-referential count(), a nested walk, or any expression calibrated by watching the target slow down. course of action: refuse, and use the boolean oracle row above, which answers the same question in two requests. scope: the run, and every future run -- a standing decision, not a per-Task judgement. resume: never in this form; a bounded-cost timing lever would be a different row. told: the operator who owns the Task, and the refusal is written where the claim was first proposed so it is not re-proposed. recorded: the refusal, its reason, and the reachable reading that replaces it.
owner_ticket: none -- refused on cost. There is no ticket, because the unblocking capability is the ability to impose unbounded load on a subject and that is a capability this harness should not acquire. Note that the miner filed this blocked on 'timing_differential has NO runtime writer', which is the retracted reading (BRIEF.md correction 3): the kind IS filable by promote_proposal under {receipt} provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:224) and Receipts carry waited_ms (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:56-58). The row is refused anyway, for the other reason, and it matters that the reason on the record is the true one.
notes: ROUTING (D6.3): orphans.json folded[4] and folded[5] routed the XPath and LDAP readings to g03/sql-injection and this group had not written them; the repair pass does. The destination contradiction the critic flagged is settled in the source and not by preference: structured-injection's own prose sends these here -- 'Where the value reaches a query rather than a document parser, the class is injection.query_language and the Playbook is sql-injection' (src/redkraken/playbooks/structured-injection/playbook.md:122-126) -- and structured-injection's bb:outputs is ["injection.document_parser"] alone, so it may not emit the class these readings produce. sql-injection's bb:outputs is ["injection.query_language"] and does. Both source pages warn about this in their own words -- 'may quickly result in a DoS', and 'the payload's cost is superlinear in document size, there is no safe calibration pass against a live target'. The reachable residue is the boolean oracle row above, which needs no clock. Distinct from this Playbook's SQL time-based row, which is reachable: pg_sleep(2) against pg_sleep(0) is a delay the reading chooses and the target does no work for, and that row's ceiling is the assertion vocabulary (roster.py:404-409 names no duration) rather than the target's cost.

technique: Read the injected expression's execution off the clock, by sending an unconditional fixed delay against the same statement asking for a zero delay, several interleaved samples of each, and claiming the separation between two sampled distributions.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, a confirmed enclosure, the engine named (there is no SLEEP() on MSSQL and no LIMIT either; the pair is WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:2' against '0:0:0' there and pg_sleep(2) against pg_sleep(0) on PostgreSQL), and the route's own gateway ceiling measured first. This runs only after the boolean pair and the error ladder have both returned nothing.
baseline: The same statement asking for a delay of zero, several samples, interleaved with the variant rather than batched -- backend latency drifts on a scale of seconds and ten payload requests followed by ten control requests measures the drift.
variant: The same statement asking for a fixed two-second delay, same number of samples, interleaved.
control: The zero-delay arm IS the control and it must be the same statement: pg_sleep(0) against pg_sleep(2), never 'the payload' against 'no payload', because the second comparison includes the cost of parsing the payload, of any WAF inspecting it, and of whatever else differs between two unlike requests. Alongside it, the observed gateway ceiling: if the route's gateway cuts at three seconds and the payload asks for five, both arms return at three, the distributions overlap, and a live injection reads as refuted.
payload_family: an unconditional fixed delay and its zero-valued twin, in the engine's own spelling. Never the conditional form over data: a delay behind a predicate about the target's contents is blind extraction with a slower clock, and every bit costs the target the full delay.
runtime_writer: promote_proposal at 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (function) and :1116 (INSERT), writing a timing_differential Observation with {receipt} provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:223). The measurement exists on the Receipts themselves: receipts.ts_arrival, receipts.ts_egress and receipts.waited_ms are columns at 0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:56-58 and are written by the door at proxy.py:3275-3277.
supported_evidence: neither of the two, and the ceiling is the whole of the row's honesty. TEST_ASSERTION_KINDS is exactly status_equals, status_differs, body_equals and body_differs (roster.py:404-409) -- nothing duration-shaped -- so no Test can close on a delay and close_test_replay will derive response_invariant for a correctly-run timing arm, which asserts nothing about the timing. Support is an agent-filed timing_differential edge citing the Receipts' waited_ms across the interleaved samples; rk2_promote_hypotheses accepts it because it filters on no kind. A Finding still needs a closed Test, so a timing reading alone opens none.
refuted_evidence: neither -- and where the payload's delay exceeds the observed gateway ceiling the honest verdict is inconclusive rather than refuted, because both arms return at the ceiling and the distributions overlap for a reason that has nothing to do with the database.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: two seconds does not separate the distributions. course of action: take more samples, never a longer sleep. Escalating the delay until it works is how a reading becomes an outage nobody decided to cause, and on a route with a connection pool ten seconds is an outage of the route. Heavy-query timing as a substitute -- an aggregate over a generated series -- is out for the same reason: the CPU it burns is not knowable in advance. scope: this parameter. resume: with more samples inside the same delay budget, or not at all. told: the operator who owns the Task, before the first delayed request, because the reading deliberately holds the target's connections. recorded: every sample's waited_ms, the interleaving order, the observed gateway ceiling, and the verdict.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable as a supporting edge only. The ticket that would let a timing reading CLOSE a Test is NEW: 'A Test assertion that names a duration, mapped by close_test_replay onto timing_differential'.
notes: Three mined rows filed timing blocked on 'timing_differential has no runtime writer'. It has one -- promote_proposal -- and the Receipts carry the measurement in waited_ms. What is genuinely absent is a duration-shaped ASSERTION, which is a narrower and different statement, and it means a timing reading can support a Hypothesis and can never open a Finding by itself. That is the honest resolution of the disagreement between sqli-time-based-sqli.md, which describes the unconditional delay with a paired control as 'the half the Playbook uses' and gives it three good rules, and playbook.md step 7, which forbids sleeping the database outright. Both are defensible and neither knew the actual shape of the limit; that should be corrected in the reference.

technique: Read the shape of the sink's result set without reading its contents -- walk ORDER BY ordinals to the boundary, widen a UNION of NULLs to the match, and rotate one reading-supplied literal through the positions to find which column reaches the page and which types it accepts.

preconditions: would be: confirmed quote-breaking and a route that surfaces an error distinguishably from an empty result. The ordinal sweep would have to be written as pairwise steps, since compare_responses differences exactly two Artifacts (ticket 109), so a ladder of ten ordinals is nine pairs and not one comparison.
baseline: would be: ORDER BY 1, which must succeed on any result set.
variant: would be: ORDER BY n raised to the error boundary and then bisected; then UNION SELECT NULL,... widened to the arity match; then one reading-supplied literal rotated through the positions.
control: would be: ORDER BY 1 re-sent immediately after each failing ordinal. If the supposedly-safe ordinal has ALSO started failing, the route is degrading rather than answering and the boundary found so far is noise. The opposite-direction ramp is the second control: ordering succeeds until it exceeds the column count and a union fails until it matches, so the two bound the answer from both sides and each alone can be misread.
payload_family: ordinals, NULL lists and reading-supplied literals -- values that extract nothing and answer only how wide the result set is, which types it accepts, and which position reaches the page.
runtime_writer: none is exercised. The evidence layer is not the obstacle: the ordinal boundary and each typed position are status or body differences that close_test_replay would write as response_differential at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072. The refusal is a prose decision, and naming the writer here is what makes that visible.
supported_evidence: none exercised -- would be response_differential.
refuted_evidence: none exercised -- would be response_invariant.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: any step that walks ORDER BY ordinals, counts columns, or sends a UNION. course of action: refuse, per the shipped Playbook's step 7, which forbids sending a union and counting columns outright, and per sqli.md, which refuses UNION SELECT and everything downstream. scope: this Playbook. resume: only if whoever owns the read_only line decides otherwise, in writing. told: the operator who owns the Task, and the ledger, because this refusal is a decision somebody made and not a limit somebody found. recorded: the refusal and the tension, so the next reading does not resolve it by accident.
owner_ticket: NEW: 'Decide whether read_only admits result-set shape probing that extracts nothing (ORDER BY ordinal ladder, UNION NULL arity, literal rotation)'
notes: Three mined rows filed this reachable, judging against the capability card alone, and they are right that the card refuses nothing here: NULL arity and type rotation extract not one byte. The shipped Playbook refuses it anyway. The ledger's job is to record the tension rather than resolve it from this seat -- a Playbook's read_only declaration is harness-enforced, and reclassifying it is a decision with an owner. What makes it worth a row: knowing the shape of the sink's result set is what makes an injection reportable as more than a boolean, and if this stays refused the report has to argue impact from the differential alone, which sqli-remote-code-execution.md already says is the version that holds up.

technique: Read the target's data through a confirmed injection -- the per-character boolean or timing loop, the UNION dump, the aggregate that collapses many rows into a single-row sink, the catalogue walk, and the out-of-band variant that concatenates a value into a hostname -- in SQL, and the same three ladders in the two sibling query languages this Playbook now covers: the XPath //text() union dump and character loop, and the LDAP attribute-prefix walk over the alphabet.

stop_conditions: halt trigger: any step that reads a value belonging to the target through a confirmed injection, including one character of one column of one row. course of action: refuse. Three reasons, all from the shipped references. What comes back is credentials and personal data, which then live in this harness's observation store under a retention policy nobody wrote for it -- and the aggregate and QUERY_TO_XML variants are worse rather than better on this point precisely because they are efficient. The cost is decisive: a 32-character hash is around 256 requests with bisection, times a column, times a row, against a rate-limited Program, to prove something the second request already proved. And the verdict was complete at the differential, so every extracted byte adds severity to a narrative and zero evidence to a hypothesis. scope: the run and every future run. resume: never on this Playbook. told: the operator who owns the Task, with the refusal and its reason, so the escalation is not proposed again as the obvious next step. recorded: the refusal, the three reasons, and the differential that already closed the claim.
owner_ticket: none -- refused by standing decision and by the Playbook's own step 7, not by capability. The NetNTLM half is additionally blocked: the capture needs a service impersonating SMB on a host this harness runs, and the recorded out-of-band channel records name resolutions and HTTP arrivals rather than completing an NTLM exchange. That capability should not be acquired, so there is no ticket for it either.
notes: Collapsed into ONE row on purpose. Bisection, SQL-Anding, the union dump, the aggregate collapse, the catalogue walk, the DNS-label exfiltration and the NetNTLM capture are seven payload families and one reading -- read the target's data -- refused for one reason, and filing them separately would multiply the unrunnable part of the catalogue sevenfold for no gain. The one genuinely new idea buried in this material has been lifted out into the predicted-row row, where the selector carries a non-sensitive scalar. Note the mechanical adjacency that gets refusals walked around by accident: the same statement shape that fires a correlator-bearing arrival is the reachable execution probe, and the same shape with a value concatenated into the hostname is this refusal. Widened in the repair pass to hold the extraction halves of the XPath and LDAP rows this group took over from orphans (D6.3), so that the reachable XPath and LDAP rows below cannot be 'completed' by somebody adding the walk. The sources' own stop conditions say the same thing: 'Confirm the oracle on 2-3 characters and stop', 'Do not pull the full document from a live target', 'do not proceed to the character-at-a-time attribute walk'.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_sql, and a string-valued input that reaches a query -- the Playbook's own subject, but the reading applies to any string input the surface takes.
baseline: The input carrying a plain value, sent twice unchanged, which is the normal answer and the byte-stability arm.
variant: The same value with a single trailing apostrophe: a changed status, or an error body.
control: The same value with TWO apostrophes, balanced. It must return to the baseline answer. That is the whole technique: if the doubled quote restores the original response, a quote is being consumed by SQL syntax; if it errors too, something is rejecting the character rather than parsing it.
payload_family: quote balancing -- one metacharacter, present once and present twice. Not a payload list; the balanced control is the entire reading and it is what a payload list omits.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay at 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1069 and :1072. supported_evidence: response_differential -- the single-quote arm is named by status_differs or body_differs against the balanced-quote control, and the balanced arm hashes with the baseline.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- all three arms hash together: the quote never reached a parser and nothing consumed it.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: three requests have been sent. course of action: stop; do not proceed to a payload that reads or writes data on the strength of a quote answer alone. Error-based detection over-reports (a JSON serialiser, a regex or a template can throw on an apostrophe) and under-reports (a global exception handler turns a syntax error into a tidy 400), which is why this is a supporting step and the boolean pair is the primary one. scope: this input. resume: the boolean pair, on the enclosure this reading revealed. told: the operator who owns the Task, only on an inconclusive. recorded: the three answers and the enclosure they imply.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: One row, not forty. sqli-identifying-vulnerabilities.md already calls the second rung of the payload ladder the one that gets skipped and the one that separates a parser from a filter; the shipped Playbook does not carry it as a step. Correction to the reference on one point only: it says error_detail is where this lands, and correction 3 confirms error_detail IS filable by promote_proposal from a Receipt -- so the reference's pairing discipline holds and the reading is not stranded, provided the Test itself closes on the differential.

preconditions: selector-position injection already confirmed by the union row above. The reading needs three distinguishable states, not two: empty (a node-set where a string was expected), a value (a scalar), and the application's own no-results render (past the end). A route that cannot show all three cannot run this.
baseline: would be: f=<field> | /*[1], which must render empty.
variant: would be: the ladder extended one rung per request -- /*[1]/*[1], then /*[1]/*[1]/*[1] -- until a scalar prints, then the last index stepped sideways to /*[2], /*[3].
control: would be: one rung past the first printing depth, which must return the application's no-results render rather than another value. Without that arm 'empty' and 'too deep' are the same observation and the depth number is a guess.
payload_family: XPath positional wildcards in a confirmed selector position -- /*[n] ladders. Values that name nothing and return only how deep the document is and how many siblings sit at a level.
runtime_writer: none exercised. Were the refusal lifted the writer would be close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z...:1064-1069, :1072): each rung is a query-string variation, so the whole ladder is Test-expressible and would reach a Finding.

refuted_evidence: none exercised -- would be response_invariant.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the row is proposed at all. course of action: refuse, and report the selector-position injection the union row already established. scope: the run, and every future run until the ticket below is decided. resume: when an operator decides whether read_only admits shape probing that extracts nothing. told: the operator who owns the Task, and the refusal is written where the claim was first proposed. recorded: the refusal, its reason, and the reachable reading that answers the neighbouring question.

notes: ROUTING (D6.3): orphans.json folded[4] and folded[5] routed the XPath and LDAP readings to g03/sql-injection and this group had not written them; the repair pass does. baseline: Task A (owner Identity): GET the socket route with the owner's channel in the query and the RFC 6455 handshake headers, sent twice unchanged. The two sends must be identical for the later comparison to mean anything.
variant: Task B (second Identity): the byte-identical request with the first Identity's channel name, and a third send from a Task with no leased Identity.
control: The baseline sent twice unchanged in Task A, asserted body_equals against itself. Without it a 400/403 pair is equally well explained by the Date header or by a route that refuses everything.
payload_family: RFC 6455 upgrade header set (upgrade, connection, sec-websocket-key, sec-websocket-version) plus one channel name in the query string
runtime_writer: No writer is ever reached. proxy.forwardable() (src/redkraken/proxy.py:635) drops every name in proxy.HOP_BY_HOP (src/redkraken/proxy.py:315-329), which contains both 'connection' and 'upgrade', and src/redkraken/proxy.py:2898 rebuilds the wire headers as [('Host', authority), *forwardable(...)]. The target therefore never sees an upgrade request and never answers 101.
supported_evidence: none. The Playbook declares credential_effect for the control and variant roles; the kind is filable via src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487) with {receipt} provenance, but there is no differential to file because both variants of the shipped channel-subscription-pair fixture answer the same 400 to a handshake with no Upgrade header (src/redkraken/fixtures/channel-subscription-pair/app.py:98-101).
refuted_evidence: none. The Playbook declares response_invariant for the refuted transition; the invariant a stripped handshake produces is an invariant about our own egress, so filing it would be a false refutation.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the first handshake through the door returns a status other than 101 while carrying no Upgrade header on the wire. Course of action: stop the reading at step 2 and do not send the second or third handshake. Scope of halt: the route, not the run -- other Playbooks on the same Task continue. Resume condition: an egress path that forwards connection and upgrade, or a Receipt field that records the 101 the door could not relay. Who is told: the operator, through an inconclusive verdict naming the missing capability in those words. What is recorded: the two Receipts, the stripped header names, and the sentence 'the door removed upgrade and connection before the target saw them'.
owner_ticket: NEW -- Forward or record the upgrade handshake: let one declared reading emit connection/upgrade through the door, or record the 101 on the Receipt so authorization.channel_subscription has a bounded execution path
notes: Correction applied: pd-web-b5.json filed its handshake rows with an unverified precondition ('I did not find a stripping rule'). The rule exists and is named above, so these rows are blocked and not unverified, and the cause is our own egress rather than the target. This blocks the whole shipped Playbook: every one of its six steps is a handshake. The channel-subscription-pair fixture cannot grade it either -- app.py answers 400 BAD_HANDSHAKE on both halves without Upgrade: websocket, so the pair is indistinguishable through this door. Separate from the same wall: a Test action carries only {ordinal, role, kind, method, url} (roster.py _TEST_SPEC_PARTS) with no headers field at all, so even an unstripped handshake could not be replayed as the Test that hypothesis testing -> supported requires (0015_epistemic_corrections.sql:195-197). REPAIR PASS: this row keeps its blocked verdict and is no longer the whole of the Playbook -- the two reachable rows above carry the half of the reading the strip leaves standing, so browser-realtime is no longer the only Playbook of fifty without a reachable row. Test action shape restated with its real citation: an action element is exactly {ordinal, role, kind, method, url} (src/redkraken/roster.py:1185-1197) and _Door.send passes only url and method (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), so even an unstripped handshake could not be replayed.

variant: not runnable -- the same frame with one field substituted

preconditions: bb:triggers_all as shipped: multiple_test_identities, query_parameter, websocket_surface. Plus a socket route whose channel name travels in the query string, and two Tasks -- a run acts as whichever Identity its Task was opened under and there is no argument for it.
baseline: Task B (the second Identity): GET the socket path with a channel name that names nothing at all, twice unchanged, asserted status_equals and body_equals. This is the shape of a refusal from this route to this caller, and everything below is read against it. No Upgrade or Connection header is spelled, because forwardable() would drop both anyway.
variant: Same Task B, same path, with the FIRST Identity's channel name in the query. A status or body differing from the baseline means the route read the channel name and reached a decision about it before it reached the handshake check.
control: Same Task B, same path, with Task B's OWN channel name in the query. It must differ from the no-such-channel baseline in the direction of acceptance. Without it, a route that answers one 4xx to everything reads as a check. Second control: Task A (the owner Identity) asking for its own channel, which is what says the route answers anybody at all.
payload_family: one channel name at a time in the query string -- a name the first Identity owns, a name the second owns, and a name nobody owns. Never a list of candidate names: enumerating channel names is a wordlist and the shipped reference refuses it by name.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited. Every arm is a GET differing only in the query, which is exactly what a Test action carries, so this closes through the Test lane on its own. src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.) files the credential_effect edge the shipped bb:evidence asks for, allowed_provenance {receipt} (0018_vocabularies.sql:231).
supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the foreign-channel arm named by a status_differs assertion against the no-such-channel baseline, in one run held at the second Identity. Plus an agent-filed credential_effect edge from the same Receipts, which names the mechanism the differential does not.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the foreign-channel arm answers exactly as the no-such-channel baseline did -- the route did not read the channel, or read it and refused this caller.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: all three arms return the same status and the same body, which is what a route that checks the handshake first looks like. Course of action: report inconclusive on the entitlement question and record which check the route reached; do not add a fourth channel name and do not start guessing names. Scope of halt: the route. Resume condition: a socket surface with an HTTP-side authorization step, or the ticket that would let the handshake through. Who is told: the Task's verdict, and an operator where the route refused every arm identically. What is recorded: the four Receipts, the status and body of each arm, and the channel name each carried.
notes: FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. This row is on it: the difference is a query parameter under one Identity. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). Two arms differing only in the query are therefore held apart by the ordinal-to-receipt binding and not by that guard, so the arms must be recorded in plan order and never re-ordered. WHY THIS ROW EXISTS: browser-realtime was the only Playbook of fifty with no reachable row, and the reason was that both of its rows asked for the handshake, which our own egress strips. This is the half of pd-web-b5:21 that survives the strip -- the mined row asks whether the upgrade itself is authorized, and what the door can still send is the same request without the two headers forwardable() removes. Honest ceiling, and the Playbook's step 4 discipline applied one step earlier: an HTTP-side decision is not a subscription. What this proves is that the route reached an authorization decision about a channel name; it does not prove a socket would have opened. The shipped channel-subscription-pair fixture cannot grade this one either, because app.py checks Sec-WebSocket-Key and Upgrade before it looks at the cookie or the channel (src/redkraken/fixtures/channel-subscription-pair/app.py:98-101) and answers 400 BAD_HANDSHAKE to both halves once 'upgrade' is dropped -- so on the fixture this row refutes, correctly, and the fixture grades nothing. That is ticket 101's to record, not to fix.

preconditions: query_parameter, reflected_parameter, web_surface, plus a route that FILTERS rather than encodes -- established first by the encoder census row, since a route that encodes returns escaped for every mutation and answers nothing.
baseline: Mission A: navigate, fill the field with the plain marker string containing rk-probe-marker, click, wait_for, probe markup_injection. Verdict escaped.
variant: Mission B: the identical plan with exactly one mutation applied to the marker -- a case flip, a <rk-<rk-probe nesting, a solidus where a space is expected, or the three syntax characters written in their fullwidth compatibility forms. Verdict reflected is the disagreement.
control: Mission C: the identical plan with a mutation the tokenizer also rejects -- a genuinely broken tag, or a compatibility character that does not fold to syntax. It must stay escaped. Plus, for the closing Test, the plain arm sent twice unchanged through http_request asserted body_equals.
payload_family: one normalisation per run: ASCII case and nesting mutations of the marker, and the fullwidth / small-form / modifier spellings of < = > that fold to ASCII under NFKD
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/browser_driver.py:645-650 (Mission.probe -> Mission._kept, stream 'probe') for the probe Artifact; a browse run IS a tool run, because browser_runs.tool_run_id is a foreign key into tool_runs (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:411-417) and enforce_kind_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) checks the provenance_kind STRING only, never which tool produced the run -- so a {tool_run} kind may cite the browse run directly with no jq pass over the stored Artifact first. fill types a plan-supplied literal -- browser_action_arguments gives fill.value the 'text' kind, '^[^[:cntrl:]]+$' bounded at 512 characters (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:117-118, 239-240) -- so a mutated marker is expressible while the probe's expression stays the registry's. src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.)
supported_evidence: response_differential from the companion http_request Test that names the mutated arm in a body_differs assertion; the escaped-then-reflected pair itself is filed by the agent as reflected_input citing the two browse tool runs.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant when the mutated arm also returns escaped -- the filter models the normalisation and the two components agree.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: a second mutation is about to be added to a run that already carries one. Course of action: stop and start a new run; a run carrying two mutations answers about neither, and a sweep is the fuzzer browser-script step 7 refuses. Scope of halt: the run. Resume condition: one mutation, one named control leg. Who is told: nobody -- this is a self-check inside the reading. What is recorded: the mutation by name, the three plan digests, and the three verdicts.
notes: HIGH VALUE: this emits injection.parser_differential, one of the nine property classes that exist and no Playbook emits. Two miner claims corrected here. (1) pd-web-b2 and portswigger filed the CDATA-split and DOMPurify-mXSS payloads as blocked because 'inject types step[payload] from the registry'; that is true of inject and false of fill, which types arguments['value'] (src/redkraken/browser_driver.py:564-570), so those payload families are reachable through fill. (2) The genuine ceiling is the 512-character text bound, which is exactly what defeats the DOMPurify deep-nesting shape -- its flattening threshold is 512 nodes. A literal NUL cannot be typed either, so the \x00 spellings only work where the server decodes %00 itself. REPAIR PASS. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. browser-script's shipped bb:triggers_all is query_parameter, reflected_parameter, web_surface, so by the Playbook's own admission rule every value this reading plants has a QUERY carrier as well as whatever field the mission types it into. That is what puts this row on the Finding path: the companion Test sends the same string in the query, where a Test action can carry it. Where the only carrier is a form POST the row stops at an Observation and reaches no Finding -- and under bb:effects read_only the body cannot be sent at all. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). Two arms differing only in the query are therefore held apart by the ordinal-to-receipt binding and not by that guard, so the arms must be recorded in plan order and never re-ordered.

preconditions: query_parameter, reflected_parameter, web_surface, and the encoder census already run, since a route that encodes on output answers the same for every input encoding and settles nothing.
baseline: GET the route with ?q=<marker>%3C<marker>, the singly encoded delimiter, sent twice unchanged and asserted body_equals. Stored as Artifact A.
variant: GET the same route with ?q=<marker>%253C<marker>, the doubly encoded form. A body equal to A means two decode passes ran between the parameter and the sink, which is the defect ASVS v5.0.0-1.1.1 names; a body differing from A means one pass ran and the second encoding survived as text.
control: GET the same route with the raw delimiter, ?q=<marker><<marker>, as the third arm. Where the raw arm, the singly encoded arm and the doubly encoded arm are all one document, the route is normalising rather than decoding twice and the reading has learned that instead. Plus the two identical baseline sends, because body_differs fires on the Date header alone.
payload_family: one syntax character at a time in three encodings -- raw, %XX, %25XX -- and the overlong and mixed-case spellings of the same byte where the route is a proxy that folds them
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited. Every arm is a GET differing only in the query, so this closes through the Test lane with no browser and no probe row. The per-encoding reading is an agent-filed reflected_input Observation, allowed_provenance {receipt,tool_run} (0018_vocabularies.sql:225-226), written by src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.)
supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the doubly encoded arm named by a body_differs assertion against the raw control, with the two identical baseline sends asserted body_equals in the same specification.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the doubly encoded arm and the singly encoded arm are byte-identical -- exactly one decode pass ran, which is what the requirement asks for.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the route answers 400 to the percent sign itself, or a front end rejects the doubly encoded form before the application sees it. Course of action: record which component refused and stop; a refusal at the edge is a fact about the edge and is not this claim. Scope of halt: the route. Resume condition: a parameter whose value reaches the application unfiltered, established by the encoder census. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: the four Receipts, the three Artifact hashes, and which pair the comparison found equal.
notes: WRITTEN IN THIS REPAIR PASS because pkb-completed-web:2 was folded silently into the encoder census and the fold was indistinguishable from a drop -- which is the coverage blocker this pass exists to fix. It is a different question from the census: the census asks WHICH context the value landed in, this asks HOW MANY TIMES it was decoded on the way, and the two have different controls and different fixes. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. This row is on it. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). Two arms differing only in the query are therefore held apart by the ordinal-to-receipt binding and not by that guard, so the arms must be recorded in plan order and never re-ordered. Note the specification-url wall does not bite here even though the payload is percent-encoded: rk2_test_request_problem refuses '%2e' specifically and a path segment that is '.' or '..' (20260815T000000Z...:222-225), and %3C is neither -- but a decode-pass reading aimed at the DOT would be refused, and belongs to file-resolution where the same wall is already recorded.

preconditions: web_surface and a served script bundle. reflected_parameter is NOT required, which is what makes this the step that runs before the trigger set is even satisfied.
baseline: Fetch the bundle through mcp__rk2__http_request so it is stored content-addressed, then run mcp__rk2__run_tool with js_routes over it and record the routes and parameter names it returns.
variant: Run js_parse over the same Artifact and record every assignment whose right-hand side is a document, location or name source and whose left-hand side is an innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, href, src or eval sink. The pair list is the product.
control: Run the same two tools over a bundle from a route the reading is not about -- a vendor chunk, or the same bundle at a second path. A pair that appears in both is the framework's and not this application's, and must be subtracted before any pair is called a lead.
payload_family: no payload; two offline tool runs over one stored Artifact
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.) The kind is content_match, allowed_provenance {tool_run} alone (0018_vocabularies.sql:233-234), and js_parse, js_map, js_routes and jq are the four binaries the run_tool enum admits. A model that READS the bundle and reports the pairs has produced no observation at all, which is the single most common way this reading is filed as done and is not.
supported_evidence: content_match from the js_parse or js_routes run, filed by the agent, citing the tool run. Nothing else: THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND REACHES NO FINDING. There is no request differential in it, so close_test_replay has nothing to close and no testing -> supported transition is available. It is a lead-producing reading, filed as one.
refuted_evidence: content_match with an empty pair set, which refutes the premise the browser rows rest on rather than any claim of its own -- there is no client-side sink here and the mission budget belongs elsewhere.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the bundle is minified past the point js_parse returns a usable tree, or the source map is absent and js_map returns nothing. Course of action: record the tool's own failure and stop; do not read the bundle by eye and report the result as a match. Scope of halt: the bundle. Resume condition: a served source map, or a second bundle path. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: the Artifact hash of the bundle, the tool run ids, and the pair list each returned.
notes: WRITTEN IN THIS REPAIR PASS. pd-web-a:24 is mined reachable and had no ledger row: it lived in the fragment row's notes as 'the cheapest high-yield reading in the whole shard', inside a BLOCKED row, where nothing will ever execute it. That is precisely the silent fold the coverage blocker names. Filed honestly against the Finding-path rule: it is reachable and it does NOT reach a Finding, because it makes no request and therefore has no differential a Test could close. Saying so is the point -- a corpus that lets a reading of this shape look like a settled claim is worse than one that omits it. Its value is that it decides which of the five reachable browser rows above is worth the mission budget, and it is unaffected by the fragment block below because it never navigates.

technique: Name the reflection's escaping context without guessing it, by sending one delimiter raw and again as its entity form and asking whether the two stored responses are the same document.

preconditions: query_parameter, reflected_parameter, web_surface. No browser is involved and no probe row is needed, which is what makes this the step before the mission rather than a second version of it.

variant: GET the same route with ?q=<marker>"<marker>, the raw delimiter, stored as Artifact V. V equal to A means the raw character was encoded on the way in; V differing from A means it reached the sink raw.
control: The baseline request sent twice unchanged, asserted body_equals. This is the load-bearing control here: without it body_differs fires on the Date header and every character reads as surviving.
payload_family: the raw form and the entity form of one delimiter at a time -- double quote, apostrophe, less-than, greater-than, solidus, backtick -- and the escaping routine's OWN escape character, sent alone and doubled, which is the reading pkb-completed-web:1 adds: a routine that escapes the quote and not the backslash lets the backslash consume the escape it just wrote.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016) for the closing Test, whose variant arm a body_differs assertion names; the per-character reading is an agent-filed reflected_input Observation written by src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487), citing the variant's own Receipt.
supported_evidence: response_differential on the raw arm against the entity arm, with the two-identical-sends control asserted body_equals in the same specification.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant when the raw arm and the entity arm are byte-identical -- the encoder ran, and that is a stronger refutation than a marker that never arrived.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the two identical baseline sends differ from each other. Course of action: stop; the route is not byte-stable and no per-character verdict from it means anything. Scope of halt: the route. Resume condition: a byte-stable route, or a comparison narrowed to a region the census can hold constant. Who is told: the Task's verdict as inconclusive, naming which of the two sends moved. What is recorded: both baseline Artifacts and the difference the compare-responses script returned.
notes: One reading, not forty payloads: greater-than encoded while the double quote survives is the attribute-escape case, both raw is the raw-HTML case, neither raw is the encoded case. It decides which of the browser rows below is worth the mission budget, and it needs no browser_probes row -- which matters because the registry holds exactly one. REPAIR PASS. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. This row is squarely on it: baseline and variant differ in the query string and nowhere else, no browser is involved, and the Test closes it directly. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). Two arms differing only in the query are therefore held apart by the ordinal-to-receipt binding and not by that guard, so the arms must be recorded in plan order and never re-ordered. FOLDED HERE with their mined ids now visible rather than described in prose: pkb-completed-web:1 (does the escaper escape its own escape character) is the same reading with the backslash as the delimiter and is in payload_family above; pd-web-b4:23 (markup that survives an identifier validator) is this census asked at a validator rather than at a renderer -- the reachable half is the status differential on the accepting route, and where that route needs a POST body it is unsendable under read_only and stops before it starts.
