preconditions: query_parameter, reflected_parameter, web_surface; an id/name-permitting or quote-permitting HTML sink established by the census and the absorption row; and a correlator minted through mcp__rk2__mint_callback against a channel the operator declared.
baseline: Mission A: fill one inert anchor with no id and no open attribute, whose href names correlator B. No arrival on B, because nothing makes the page fetch it.
variant: Mission B: fill either the two-anchor clobber whose name attribute supplies the url a page reads through the window.x || {} pattern, or the unterminated attribute whose value names correlator A. An arrival on A is the evidence.
control: Mission C: a byte-identical repeat of Mission B minting correlator C. Both A and C must arrive. Two identical missions arriving is what makes the fetch a property of the sink rather than one event; a single arrival cannot be told from a crawler. The negative arm additionally uses a different id so the fetch is attributable to the clobbered name rather than to the presence of any element.
payload_family: inert markup that names a URL: and the unterminated
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/callback.py:85 -> record_callback_interaction. callback_interaction is registered is_evidential = true with allowed_provenance {callback} (20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:349) and rk2_promote_hypotheses writes hypothesis_evidence from an agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530).
supported_evidence: Two edges doing two different jobs, and the distinction is the point. The Test that carries the hypothesis to supported is the companion http_request differential -- the correlator-bearing markup in the QUERY against the plain arm, named by a body_differs assertion -- and its Observation is close_test_replay's response_differential. The ARRIVAL is an agent-filed callback_interaction edge: a real, unfiltered hypothesis_evidence edge that names the mechanism, and one that cannot by itself move a Hypothesis to supported, because close_test_replay is the only writer of that transition.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant from the companion Test when the marker arm and the plain arm are byte-identical. Silence on the channel is NOT a refutation and must not be filed as one -- a CONTROL arrival writes no Observation at all, because is_control and a null subject are one state tied by a CHECK (20261001T000000Z__a_control_arrival_is_what_makes_silence_a_finding.sql:45-52).
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the URL under the injected attribute would resolve anywhere other than the minted correlator on the declared channel. Course of action: stop; a collector the operator did not declare is exfiltration to a third party whether or not the reading meant it. Scope of halt: the run. Resume condition: the URL rewritten to the minted correlator, and the channel confirmed to serve a canary. Who is told: the operator, before the mission runs, because the channel is theirs. What is recorded: the correlator, the arrival label, the mission plan digest, and the fact that the swallowed bytes were not read -- only that a fetch happened.
notes: Correction applied, twice. pd-web-a.json and pkb-completed-web.json both filed the sink half of dangling markup blocked on the claim that record_callback_interaction writes no hypothesis_evidence edge. It does; ticket 98's own migration calls callback_interaction evidential in as many words (20260928T040000Z__the_out_of_band_refusal_was_reversed.sql:19). Two real limits stand and are stated above: a control arrival files nothing, and the provenance is {callback} alone so no Receipt may be filed under this kind. DEDUP: the dangling-markup sink half and the DOM-clobbering-of-a-URL-valued-global row are one mechanism under two names -- caller-typed inert markup makes the target's page fetch our correlator -- and are one row here, with both sources kept. This row also needs the shipped Playbook's step 7 amended: it currently says the reading 'does not call out to a collector', which is a ceiling the declared OOB channel does not violate. REPAIR PASS, and this is the row the Finding-path rule changes most. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. So the honest split is: the Test proves the markup was REFLECTED, from a query-borne differential; the arrival proves it was ACTED ON, and rides as a supporting edge that stops at an Observation. A row that claimed the arrival closed the transition would be claiming a writer that does not exist. browser-script's shipped bb:triggers_all is query_parameter, reflected_parameter, web_surface, so by the Playbook's own admission rule every value this reading plants has a QUERY carrier as well as whatever field the mission types it into. That is what puts this row on the Finding path: the companion Test sends the same string in the query, where a Test action can carry it. Where the only carrier is a form POST the row stops at an Observation and reaches no Finding -- and under bb:effects read_only the body cannot be sent at all. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). stop_conditions: Halt trigger: a request is about to write a value into a record another user loads. owner_ticket: NEW -- If stored injection is wanted at all it needs its own Playbook with effects other than read_only, a declared cleanup and a named owner; it is not an extension of browser-script
notes: Recorded with its reason so it is not re-proposed: writing markup into a record other users load is the same problem as an executing payload with a longer fuse, and the maintainer reference is explicit that nothing here writes. variant: Register a profile whose name is a harmless string that shadows no live route -- rk-<nonce> -- then GET /rk-<nonce> again. A profile page where a 404 stood is the namespace mounted at the root.
control: Two identical sends of the baseline, first and last, whose stored Artifacts must hash alike. body_differs compares response_agent_sha (20260815T000000Z...:1503-1506) and that sha covers the whole message -- status line, headers and body (proxy.py:878 transcript, proxy.py:3088) -- so a Date header alone makes any two sends differ. A route that is not byte-stable across the pair is not a route this reading can difference, and the verdict is inconclusive. Then GET a SECOND unregistered root path, /rk-<second nonce>, after the registration. It must still 404. That separates 'the profile route shadows the root' from 'the deployment started rendering a profile for every path', which is the boring explanation this reading has to rule out.
payload_family: one caller-chosen profile name that routes to nothing today. NOT index.php, login.php, signup.php, admin, static, api or robots.txt -- see stop_conditions.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 calls close_test_replay, which derives the Observation kind from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action any status_differs/body_differs assertion names -- as its action or as its against -- becomes response_differential, any other action becomes response_invariant (20260816T000000Z...:1064-1074). The post-registration GET is named by a body_differs assertion against the pre-registration GET of the same url, so its Observation is response_differential. That same call writes the testing->supported hypothesis_transitions row at 20260816T000000Z...:1125, which is what rk2_finding_refusal requires before a Finding may open (20260815T120000Z...:644-649) -- and this row can reach it, because both differenced arms are plain GETs whose whole difference is the path. BESIDE IT, and only as a supporting edge: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 issues promote_proposal, live at 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with its observations INSERT at :1116-1123, which files an agent-filed content_match over the two stored profile documents naming the registered name inside the page the root path served.

refuted_evidence: response_invariant, role variant: a spec whose only assertion on the post-registration GET is body_equals(against=the pre-registration GET) names it with no differing assertion, so close_test_replay derives response_invariant -- the root path still 404s after the name was registered, the profile namespace is not mounted at the root, and the claim is refuted. stop_conditions: halt trigger (observed condition): the mount is proved -- the harmless name serves a profile where a 404 stood | course of action: STOP THERE. Do not register a name that collides with a live application route. The mount is the finding; taking /login or /index.php is the destructive step and the reading does not need it, because what a real collision would do follows from the mount and does not have to be performed | scope of halt: the run | resume condition: never on this subject without a written operator decision naming the route to be shadowed | who is told: the operator, through mcp__rk2__park_for_human, with the halt trigger quoted verbatim | what is recorded: the Receipt label of every arm sent before the halt, which arm triggered it, and the three Receipt labels, the name registered, and an explicit line saying the collision was ARGUED from the mount and not performed
notes: THE HAND-OFF THAT DIED, now landed (repair/orphans.json finding 3). g04's coverage_note says 'HANDED OFF: pd-web-b4[21] (username/namespace collision under cms) goes to the orphans group' and no ledger row was ever written for it. cms is one of the nine thin Playbooks D11 names, at two rows, with three shipped references that produced nothing. CLASS, AND A CORRECTION TO THE FINDING THAT ASKED FOR THIS ROW: the repair packet calls this 'the cheapest emitter for injection.unclaimed_reference'. It cannot be. cms is bb:category authorization and playbook.py:427-435 refuses every bb:outputs entry outside the category's own family -- 'category_mismatch ... is not in the {category} family' -- so an injection.* leaf in cms's bb:outputs is unstorable by construction. The row is filed under cms's own shipped class, authorization.parallel_route: a second route to the same records that outranks the application's own is exactly what that leaf names, and here the second route is one the caller created.  FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW REACHES A FINDING. The differential lives in the request line (the PATH -- /rk-<nonce> before registration against /rk-<nonce> after it, with a second unregistered root path as the catch-all control), which is exactly what a Test action carries ({ordinal, role, kind, method, url}, roster.py:1184-1197) and what record_test_action compares (method, scheme, host, port, path; 20260815T000000Z...:1386-1391), so close_test_replay sees both arms and can write the testing->supported transition rk2_finding_refusal requires (20260816T000000Z...:1125; 20260815T120000Z...:644-649). CONSTRAINT ON THE SPELLING: rk2_test_request_problem refuses any '.' or '..' path segment and any '%2e' anywhere in a specification url (20260815T000000Z...:217-226). The door forwards both verbatim because origin_form() removes nothing (proxy.py:818-828), so an arm spelled that way is performable but CANNOT be closed by a Test -- it falls back to the Observation ceiling. Every arm this row names is spelled without them.  The registration POST between the two arms is NOT part of the Test and does not need to be: it is setup the agent performs through mcp__rk2__http_request, and the Test then replays two plain GETs on two different urls. That is what keeps this row Finding-bearing while almost everything else in this file is not. The identifier match has to be a jq run over the stored Artifact, and the Playbook has to say so. preconditions: read_method, tech_cms, plus one profile name already known to exist -- taken from the application's own answers, never guessed and never harvested by enumeration. authenticated_endpoint is not needed for this arm, which is what makes it the step before the parallel-route reading.
baseline: GET the root-relative path of the known profile name, twice unchanged, asserted body_equals. A profile page means the user namespace is mounted at the root.
variant: GET a root-relative path that is an APPLICATION route name -- /login, /admin, /api, /robots.txt -- and compare against the baseline shape. An application page means the two namespaces are separate; a profile-shaped 404 or a profile page means they share a path space and a registered name could shadow a route.
control: GET a root-relative name nobody holds and no route serves, /rk-unclaimed-name. It must 404. Without it, a profile-shaped answer at /login cannot be told from a catch-all that renders a profile shell for every path, which is the single most common false reading of this question.
payload_family: root-relative path segments: one name known to exist, the application's own route names, and one name that is neither. All GETs, at most five, each asked once.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited. supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the application-route arm named by a status_differs assertion against the unclaimed-name control -- the shape that says the two namespaces overlap.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the application-route arm answers exactly as the unclaimed name did, or when the known profile is served under a prefix of its own -- the namespaces are separate and the collision question does not arise.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the deployment answers every root-relative name with the same page. Course of action: report inconclusive and stop; the reading cannot separate a mounted namespace from a catch-all and a sixth name would be a scan. Scope of halt: the origin. Resume condition: a deployment whose unclaimed-name control 404s. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: the four Receipts, the status and body shape of each, and the name each carried.
notes: WRITTEN IN THIS REPAIR PASS. pd-web-b4:21 was mined reachable, handed by g04 to the orphans group by name, and died there -- no row, no folded entry, no dropped entry. This is the half of it that a read_only Playbook can execute, and it is the half that decides whether the other half is worth anything: if the namespaces do not share a path space, no registered name can shadow a route and the write experiment is pointless. The registration half is the row below. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. This row is on it -- every arm is a GET differing only in the path. baseline: GET the application path under test -- /login -- before anything is registered. The application's own page, sent twice unchanged and asserted body_equals.
variant: Register a user whose name is that same string, then GET the same path again. The profile page where the application page was is the claim: the profile route shadows the application route.

runtime_writer: Not reached under this Playbook, and the two reasons are independent. (1) The registration is a POST with a body, and a Task whose whole Playbook selection is bb:effects read_only opens with body_allowed false -- the value is the maximum over the selection (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, :3667, used at :3052) -- and cms is read_only with bb:baseline stable_session, its step 7 saying in as many words that it does not write, install or upgrade. (2) The class this reading emits is injection.unclaimed_reference, and cms CANNOT declare it: src/redkraken/playbook.py:428-435 refuses any bb:outputs entry that does not start with the Playbook's own bb:category, cms's category is authorization, and the refusal is raised as category_mismatch at load. So this is not the missing-emitter case D3 settles -- adding a line to cms's bb:outputs would not load.
supported_evidence: would be response_differential on the before-and-after GETs, named by a body_differs assertion against the unclaimed-name control; not filed under this slug.
refuted_evidence: would be response_invariant, when the application page is served unchanged after the registration; not filed under this slug.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the registration succeeds and the cleanup that releases the name does not. Course of action: stop the whole run, not the route, and tell an operator immediately -- a name held on somebody's production namespace is a change this reading cannot undo. Scope of halt: the run. Resume condition: the name released and confirmed released by a GET. Who is told: an operator, directly, and the Task's verdict. What is recorded: the registration Receipt, the name, the cleanup Receipt and its status.
owner_ticket: NEW -- A Playbook with bb:category injection and bb:effects other than read_only to hold injection.unclaimed_reference's registration half. Priced: cms cannot take it, because src/redkraken/playbook.py:429 requires every bb:outputs entry to carry the Playbook's own category prefix; and no read_only Playbook can send the registration, because _body_allowed is the maximum over the selection (src/redkraken/execution.py:3667). So the cost is one new Playbook document plus its playbook_outputs seed migration, not an edit to an existing one.
notes: WRITTEN IN THIS REPAIR PASS, and it PARTLY DISPUTES the finding that asked for it. The critic's fix says to write this as 'the cheapest emitter for injection.unclaimed_reference on a surface the harness can actually reach'. The reading is real and it is filed here rather than dropped -- but it cannot be a cms row, and the refutation is one line of source: src/redkraken/playbook.py:428-435 raises category_mismatch for any bb:outputs entry outside the Playbook's own bb:category family, and cms's category is authorization. Ticket 101 edits bb:outputs; it cannot edit them past that check. So this is recorded as out_of_scope FOR CMS with the ticket that would place it, and its reachable read half is the row above, which is a cms row and does execute. preconditions: bb:triggers_all as shipped: read_method, spa_surface, tech_edge_proxy, plus an https subject the door has not met before -- proxy.py:2818-2821 measures each (program, host, port) once for as long as the door is up.
baseline: Two ordinary reads of the subject presenting nothing, recording the protocol each response was delivered over, Alt-Svc and Strict-Transport-Security, with the word absent for each that is not there.
variant: The measurement receipt for the same target: tls_version, cipher and alpn as the door negotiated them on its own socket with nothing downstream.
control: The two ordinary reads sent unchanged, asserted body_equals, which is what settles that the advertisement is the deployment's policy and not one fleet member's. The measurement's own control is a SECOND FIELD off the same citable receipt, not a second handshake -- ticket 116's proof files the version as variant and the cipher as control from one receipt (20261018T000000Z__a_probe_only_claim_becomes_a_finding.sql:268-285), and a second handshake is refused anyway.
payload_family: no payload; a handshake taken by purpose, and three response headers read as text
runtime_writer: The Receipt is written by src/redkraken/proxy.py:2776 (Handler._measure) through record_transport_measurement (20260923T000000Z__the_runtime_takes_its_own_transport_measurement.sql:346), on lane proxy_internal (same file:394). The Observation over it has only ever been written by a migration DO block (20261018T000000Z...:268). The AGENT's writer, src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487), cannot reach it: src/redkraken/proposal.py:227-228 drops any proposal element citing a proxy_internal receipt with reason receipt_proxy_internal, and the agent cannot even see the row -- 0020_state_access.sql:281-283 puts a RESTRICTIVE policy on receipts for role rk2_state USING (lane <> 'proxy_internal'), which no later migration relaxes. THE TRANSPORT WALL, read in source this pass and stronger than any earlier version of this row said. transport_makeability seeds transport.tls_configuration and transport.certificate_trust as probe_only (src/redkraken/migrations/0025_transport_claims.sql:204-216). transport_evidence_guard (same file:361-395) refuses ANY hypothesis_evidence row with polarity 'supports' on a probe_only class whose cited Observation is not transport_parameters_observed -- so on a transport.tls_configuration Hypothesis even a close_test_replay response_invariant is refused at INSERT. And transport_parameters_observed has NO agent-reachable writer: transport_observation_guard (same file:300-350, the transport_citable test at :314 and the metadata.transport test at :324-331) demands a transport_citable Receipt AND a non-empty metadata.transport, while the live promote_proposal hardcodes metadata to jsonb_build_object('proposal', ..., 'element', ...) (20261008T000000Z...:1116-1123), so the element raises, is caught by the surrounding EXCEPTION handler and lands in proposal_drops. THIS REFUTES THE HARNESS CARD'S OWN TABLE, which lists transport_parameters_observed as writable from '{receipt} -- a Receipt whose transport fields are populated and transport_citable'. It is not writable by the agent at all, by any path. That is a card error and it is recorded here rather than argued.
supported_evidence: none reachable. transport_parameters_observed is evidential with allowed_provenance {receipt} (0025_transport_claims.sql:250) and transport_observation_guard (same file:299-322) demands a transport_citable receipt -- which is exactly the class of receipt the agent may neither read nor cite. A second, independent bar: v_records never projects wire_tls_version, wire_cipher or wire_alpn (20260814T080000Z__a_refutation_is_kept_and_made_due.sql:1265-1286), so even a citable handle would hand the agent a label and no values.
refuted_evidence: none reachable, for the same two reasons. The Playbook declares transport_parameters_observed for the refuted transition as well.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: no citable receipt can be obtained -- which here means every time, from the agent's side. Course of action: stop at step 2; do not substitute the ordinary path, do not read this harness's own certificate, do not report what the proxy negotiated. Scope of halt: the reading, on every subject, until the capability exists. Resume condition: an agent-visible handle on a transport measurement -- either a projection carrying the three allowed_fields, or a citable reference that survives proposal.py's proxy_internal drop. Who is told: an operator, through an inconclusive verdict that names the missing capability in those words, which the shipped Playbook's step 6 already instructs. What is recorded: the two ordinary reads, their three advertised values, and the sentence that the measurement exists and is not reachable from here.
owner_ticket: NEW -- Give the agent a citable handle on a transport measurement: project wire_tls_version, wire_cipher and wire_alpn into the receipt record and admit that one receipt past proposal.py's proxy_internal drop, or the class stays unemitted
notes: Correction applied, and the miners' verdict was right for the wrong reason. owasp.json, pd-infra.json and pd-web-a.json all said transport_parameters_observed has NO RUNTIME WRITER. It has two -- record_transport_measurement for the Receipt and promote_proposal for the Observation -- and the class is still not agent-reachable, because the one receipt it may cite is on the one lane the agent may not cite. That is a narrower and more actionable statement, and it names the exact line to change. Two further facts the shipped Playbook gets wrong and should not: the measurement is NOT requested by purpose from the model -- it is taken automatically after the first https exchange with a target (proxy.py:3362), so step 2's 'request the measurement' has no argument behind it; and step 3's 'repeat the measurement' cannot happen, because proxy.py:2818-2821 refuses a second measurement of a target it has already measured while the process is up. http-desync is one of the ten Playbooks the corpus defect names, and this is why: it declares one kind, and the kind's provenance is unreachable from the model's side. REPAIR PASS: the verdict is unchanged and the reason is now three walls instead of two, the third being the promote_proposal metadata hardcode above -- which matters because it means projecting the wire fields into the receipt record (the unblock this row's owner_ticket asks for) is NOT sufficient on its own. PRICE of the unblock, so the operator can decide it: promote_proposal would have to carry an element-supplied metadata object through to the observations INSERT (one CREATE OR REPLACE, one migration), v_records would have to project wire_tls_version, wire_cipher and wire_alpn (20260814T080000Z...:1265-1286), and proposal.py:227-228's proxy_internal drop plus 0020_state_access.sql:281-283's RESTRICTIVE policy would both have to admit that one lane. Three files and two migrations -- larger than a patch and smaller than a redesign, which is exactly why it is a ticket.

payload_family: CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE header obfuscation, CL.0, 0.CL with an early-response gadget, the double desync, H2.CL, H2.TE, chunk-extension malformation, and a body split so a filtered keyword straddles a chunk boundary
runtime_writer: No writer is reachable and the claim cannot be written down at all. transport.request_framing is registered unmakeable in transport_makeability (src/redkraken/migrations/0025_transport_claims.sql:222-228 -- the earlier citation of :191-203 was wrong; :191 is the CHECK constraint on the makeability column and :203 is the INSERT's first line), and transport_hypothesis_guard is an ENABLE ALWAYS trigger on hypotheses (same file:291-294), so a restore cannot skip it. stop_conditions: Halt trigger: a request body is about to carry hand-spelled chunk framing, or a second length header is about to be attempted. Course of action: do not send it; the body IS a model-authored string and chunks CAN be typed into it, which is precisely the hazard -- the door's recomputed length and the typed framing would disagree, and that disagreement is the ambiguous framing this corpus refuses to construct. Scope of halt: the run, and the class permanently. Resume condition: none through this harness; a raw-socket test outside it, against a target an operator has confirmed in scope, in a window they arranged. Who is told: an operator, via an inconclusive verdict naming the missing capability as 'the interception proxy re-serialises every request, so framing cannot be observed'. What is recorded: the refusal, its two independent causes, and nothing that was sent.
owner_ticket: NEW -- No unblock is sought. Record only, so the class is not re-proposed as a documentation gap; a future ticket that wants it is asking for a second egress path and should be answered by the one-egress-path rule
notes: Consolidated deliberately: seven mined rows across five shards share one refusal and one mechanism, and seven rows would multiply the unrunnable catalogue for no gain. The second reason travels with the first and is the one that settles it: the remainder prefixes the next request on that connection, and the next request belongs to somebody who is not part of this engagement -- no bounded blast radius and no undo. Ticket 96 giving http_request a body argument changed nothing here, and the shipped Playbook's step 6 already says so; a reading that wants to test framing should read that paragraph rather than spend an attempt discovering it. The cache half belongs elsewhere: what a front end stored and handed to the next caller is information_disclosure.cached_response and web-cache asks it with a read that reaches nobody else. REPAIR PASS: the transport_makeability citation is corrected from :191-203 to :222-228, which is where the transport.request_framing row actually sits. Nothing else moves -- the refusal is a decision and the reason travels with it. One half of pkb-checklist:45 is NOT refused and is recorded so it is not lost inside this fold: request-TARGET mangling is performable, because origin_form() (src/redkraken/proxy.py:818-828) removes nothing and forwards '../', '..%2f', '..;/' and '//' verbatim. It is not this Playbook's, though -- where the front end and the application resolve one path differently the class is authorization.edge_rule (deployment) or information_disclosure.cached_response (web-cache), and neither is in the transport family http-desync's bb:category confines it to.

preconditions: read_method, spa_surface, tech_edge_proxy. Response headers are handed back to the caller (ticket 94), and neither Alt-Svc nor Strict-Transport-Security is in WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS (src/redkraken/proxy.py:376), so both survive to the agent view.
baseline: GET the subject presenting nothing, and record the three values, writing absent for each header that is not there.
variant: GET the subject a second time, unchanged, and record the same three. A value that moved between two sends is one fleet member's configuration and not the deployment's policy.
control: The two sends ARE the control, and that is the whole point of doing it twice: with body_differs firing on the Date header, an assertion of body_equals over the pair is what makes any later comparison mean something. A third read against a route on the same origin that the front end serves differently separates a per-route header from a deployment-wide one.
payload_family: no payload; two identical reads and three named response headers
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited. for the response_invariant over the two identical sends. src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.) for the header_policy_observed Observation, whose allowed_provenance is {receipt,tool_run} (0018_vocabularies.sql:235-236) and which therefore cites the read's own Receipt directly. BOTH edges are admissible ONLY on a transport.header_policy Hypothesis, which transport_makeability seeds agent_ok with allowed_fields '{}' (src/redkraken/migrations/0025_transport_claims.sql:217-221), so transport_evidence_guard returns NEW at its makeability check (same file:370) and never reaches the kind test.
supported_evidence: response_invariant over the two identical sends, written by close_test_replay, plus an agent-filed header_policy_observed edge naming each of the three values or its absence -- BOTH carried on a transport.header_policy Hypothesis. Filed on a transport.tls_configuration Hypothesis, which is http-desync's only declared output, EVERY supporting edge is refused at INSERT by transport_evidence_guard. That is the correction this pass makes and it is the difference between a row that runs and a row that raises.
refuted_evidence: response_differential when the two sends disagree on any of the three, which refutes the premise rather than the claim -- the deployment has no single advertisement to compare anything against.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the two reads disagree on any of the three values. Course of action: stop and report inconclusive, saying which of the three moved; do not average them and do not take the second. Scope of halt: the subject. Resume condition: a stable pair of reads, or a subject pinned to one fleet member. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: both Receipts, the three values from each, and the word absent where one was missing.
owner_ticket: 101 -- add transport.header_policy to http-desync's bb:outputs. This is the D3 case: the harness executes the reading and the Runtime writes the Observation; what is missing is a line in a bb:outputs, and ticket 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs. It is admissible: src/redkraken/playbook.py:429 requires every output to carry the Playbook's own bb:category prefix, http-desync's category is transport, and transport.header_policy carries it. The alternative -- moving the row to browser-framing, which already emits the class -- leaves http-desync with no executable step at all, and the Playbook then describes only readings its own harness refuses.
notes: REWRITTEN IN THIS REPAIR PASS, and it partly applies and partly disputes the blocker that named it. APPLIED: the mechanism the critic found is real and is now in runtime_writer and supported_evidence above -- on a probe_only class, transport_evidence_guard refuses a header_policy_observed supporting edge at INSERT, and transport_parameters_observed cannot be filed by any agent path. The row as previously written would have raised. DISPUTED: the verdict 'blocked'. The critic's own fix concedes the reading 'is still a fine transport.header_policy reading (agent_ok, header_policy_observed)', and the two file:line facts that settle it are src/redkraken/migrations/0025_transport_claims.sql:217-221, where transport.header_policy is seeded agent_ok with the reason 'the agent-lane receipt is sufficient', and the same file:370, where transport_evidence_guard RETURNs NEW for any class that is not probe_only. Nothing in the schema binds a Hypothesis's property_class to its Task's Playbook outputs -- playbook_outputs is read by the SELECTION query (20260823T000000Z__a_playbook_is_chosen_before_the_model_reads_it.sql:278-283, which reports 'class_mismatch' as a reason a Playbook is not OFFERED) and by check_playbook_integrity, not by a hypothesis trigger. So the reading executes, the evidence writes, and the only defect is a corpus line -- which is D3's exact case and D3 is binding. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. This row does not need one: it is an INVARIANT reading, its two arms are byte-identical, and close_test_replay writes response_invariant for an action no status_differs or body_differs assertion names (20260816T000000Z...:1063-1069). THE TRANSPORT WALL, read in source this pass and stronger than any earlier version of this row said. transport_makeability seeds transport.tls_configuration and transport.certificate_trust as probe_only (src/redkraken/migrations/0025_transport_claims.sql:204-216). transport_evidence_guard (same file:361-395) refuses ANY hypothesis_evidence row with polarity 'supports' on a probe_only class whose cited Observation is not transport_parameters_observed -- so on a transport.tls_configuration Hypothesis even a close_test_replay response_invariant is refused at INSERT. And transport_parameters_observed has NO agent-reachable writer: transport_observation_guard (same file:300-350, the transport_citable test at :314 and the metadata.transport test at :324-331) demands a transport_citable Receipt AND a non-empty metadata.transport, while the live promote_proposal hardcodes metadata to jsonb_build_object('proposal', ..., 'element', ...) (20261008T000000Z...:1116-1123), so the element raises, is caught by the surrounding EXCEPTION handler and lands in proposal_drops. THIS REFUTES THE HARNESS CARD'S OWN TABLE, which lists transport_parameters_observed as writable from '{receipt} -- a Receipt whose transport fields are populated and transport_citable'. It is not writable by the agent at all, by any path. That is a card error and it is recorded here rather than argued. This is step 1 of the shipped Playbook and it remains the only step that executes; the other three steps are the rows above and below.

preconditions: multiple_test_identities and query_parameter or body_parameter; a route whose subject is implied by the session, and a parameter name harvested from the delete or edit calls of a neighbouring route rather than guessed.
baseline: GET the route with the subject implied by the Task's Identity, twice unchanged, asserted body_equals. The caller's own collection.
variant: The same URL with the harvested parameter naming a second account the operator owns. A different collection means an implicit subject can be overridden by an explicit one.
control: Repeat the baseline immediately after the variant. It must return the caller's own collection unchanged, so the difference is attributable to the parameter and not to the collection having changed between reads.
payload_family: an identifier parameter the route never advertised -- user_id, account_id, owner_id, customer_id, profile_id -- carrying a subject the operator owns
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016) for the query arm, which is a Test action's {method, url} exactly; src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487) for the body arm, which the Test lane cannot carry.
supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the parameter-bearing arm named by a body_differs assertion against the repeated baseline.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the parameter changes nothing and the repeated baseline confirms the route is stable.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the parameter is about to name a subject the operator does not own. Course of action: refuse; the reading is proved on two accounts the operator holds and does not need a third party's identifier. Second trigger: the parameter name is about to be guessed rather than harvested. Course of action: stop and harvest it, or record that the reading does not apply. Scope of halt: the route. Resume condition: a harvested name from a sibling route. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: where the parameter name was harvested from, and the three Receipts.
notes: The shipped Playbook is about an alternate lookup ARGUMENT on a route that already takes one; this is about a route that takes NONE, where the check is 'whatever the session says' until a parameter overrides it. The source's own method is the useful part and should reach the prose: harvest the parameter name by watching what the delete and edit calls of neighbouring routes send, rather than trying a list. REPAIR PASS. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. The query arm is on it and closes directly. The body arm gains the same second reason as the shape census: under a read_only-only selection the body cannot be sent (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, :3667), so it is not a Test arm and not a request either. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). Two arms differing only in the query are therefore held apart by the ordinal-to-receipt binding and not by that guard, so the arms must be recorded in plan order and never re-ordered.

technique: Ask whether the object named in a request is checked against the caller, by sending one request twice from two Tasks that differ only in the Identity each was opened under, and differencing the two stored responses.

preconditions: bb:triggers_all as shipped: multiple_test_identities, object_identifier; bb:triggers_any: body_parameter, path_parameter or query_parameter. Two Tasks, because a run acts as whichever Identity its Task was opened under and there is no argument for it; the object parameter read from the state view, not guessed from the URL.
baseline: Two readings under one label, and the repair pass separates them because only one of them can be the Test. (a) THE CLOSING TEST, one run held at Identity B: action 1 is a GET for an object B owns, which is the control arm; action 2 is the byte-identical GET for the object A owns, which is the variant arm. One Identity, two paths, and that is a request-line differential a Test action can carry. (b) THE CORROBORATION, in Task A: the same request for A's own object, sent twice unchanged and asserted body_equals, which is what says the object is there and the route is byte-stable.
variant: Within the closing Test's single run at Identity B, the arm naming A's object. One variable moves and it is the object identifier in the path or query. The two-Task version -- one request, two Identities -- is the reading a human describes and is filed as an agent Observation, not as the Test.
control: The arm naming B's OWN object, in the same run at the same Identity. This is the step most runs skip and it is what makes the variant mean anything: without it a refusal under B is equally well explained by a session that was never valid, a route that rejects everything, or a rate limit. The two identical sends in Task A are the second control, against the Date header.
payload_family: one object identifier held constant while the Identity moves -- never a substituted identifier, which would be two variables
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited. The two arms are one run at one Identity differing only in the object identifier, which record_test_action compares over method, scheme, host, port and path (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.) files the two-Task reading as response_differential and, optionally, a credential_effect edge naming the mechanism the differential does not, both allowed_provenance {receipt} (0018_vocabularies.sql:219-220, :231).
supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the foreign-object arm named by a status_differs or body_differs assertion against the own-object control arm, in one run held at Identity B. Plus agent-filed response_differential edges for the two-Task reading, both citing Receipts made in Task B.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the variant is invariant against a control that succeeded -- the session is good and the server still refused.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the identifier has to be re-encoded to travel under the other session. Course of action: stop and record that instead; the comparison now has two variables and the answer is about neither. Second trigger: the variant differs in a way the difference cannot attribute -- a generic error page, a redirect to a login the control did not hit, a rate limit. Course of action: report inconclusive, which is the honest answer. Scope of halt: the endpoint. Resume condition: an identifier that survives the second session unchanged. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: the three Artifacts and the difference the compare-responses script returned, not a description of it.
notes: Two runtime facts the shipped Playbook's step 2 should carry, because a model following it as written will hit both. (1) The baseline Receipt is made in Task A and cannot be cited from Task B: src/redkraken/proposal.py:232 drops an element citing another run's Receipt as receipt_other_run. The reading still closes, because the two edges bb:evidence requires for supported are the variant and the CONTROL, and both of those are made in Task B -- but the Playbook's sentence 'the differential is made by comparing the Receipts they produced' has to mean read, not cite. (2) The Test that supplies the transition's Receipt runs under one identity_slot (src/redkraken/replay.py:133, 205) and its actions carry only {ordinal, role, kind, method, url}, so the Test cannot itself be the two-Identity differential; it is a single-Identity request Test whose Receipt the transition cites, while the evidence profile is satisfied by the agent's own Observations. REPAIR PASS, and this is the row the Finding-path rule improves rather than weakens. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. A replay run carries ONE identity_slot (src/redkraken/replay.py:133, passed to open_test_replay at :205), so a two-Identity comparison cannot be one Test. The closeable shape is a single run held at one Identity whose arms differ in the request line; the second Identity's reading is filed by the agent as a supporting Observation on the same Hypothesis. The previous version of this row left the whole claim resting on agent-filed edges and used the Test only as a Receipt supplier. It does not have to: an IDOR reading held at ONE Identity, whose two arms name two objects, is a request-line differential and closes through close_test_replay directly. The two-Task comparison is still worth doing and is still filed -- it is what says A can see the object at all -- but it is the corroboration and not the settlement. One precise consequence for a query-only differential, which is what most of this group's Test arms are: record_test_action compares the receipt against the action over method, scheme, host, port and path and DELIBERATELY NOT over the query, 'because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns' (20260816T000000Z...:1620-1635). Two arms differing only in the query are therefore held apart by the ordinal-to-receipt binding and not by that guard, so the arms must be recorded in plan order and never re-ordered.

preconditions: object_identifier plus one of path_parameter or query_parameter, and one account the operator owns. multiple_test_identities is not needed for this arm, which is what separates it from the row above.
baseline: GET the route with the caller's own identifier in its native shape, sent twice unchanged and asserted body_equals.
variant: The same route with the identifier re-spelled -- an integer where an opaque value is expected, a name where an integer is, a wildcard segment, or the nil UUID. A record that is not the caller's, or a collection where a single object was expected, means the lookup accepts a shape the ownership check never anticipated.
control: A well-formed identifier of the ORIGINAL shape that certainly names nothing -- a UUID the reading minted itself. It must 404. Without it, 'the route returned a record' cannot be told from a route that returns the caller's own record whatever it is sent.
payload_family: shape substitutions on one identifier: integer for opaque, name for integer, wildcard segment, nil UUID, and the value wrapped in an array
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016) for the query and path arms, whose actions are {method, url} and nothing else, so the Test closes them directly; src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487) for the body arm, which the Test lane cannot carry.
supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the re-spelled arm named by a body_differs assertion against the minted-identifier control.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when every re-spelling answers the same way the minted control did.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: a re-spelling returns a record that is not the caller's. Course of action: stop at that shape; the claim is that the lookup accepts it, not how many records it will yield. Second trigger: a shape is about to be tried with a write verb. Course of action: refuse; this row is read verbs only. Scope of halt: the endpoint. Resume condition: none needed -- the reading is complete at the first shape that answers. Who is told: the Task's verdict, and an operator if a record belonging to somebody outside the engagement came back. What is recorded: the shape by name, the three Receipts, and the identifier of the record returned.
notes: A precise limit worth stating: a Test action carries no body field at all (roster.py _TEST_SPEC_PARTS 'actions'), and TEST_REQUEST_METHODS admits POST and PUT without one -- so the array-wrapping arm, {"id":[19]} in place of {"id":19}, can be SENT by http_request and cannot be replayed as the Test that closes the transition. Query and path arms are unaffected. The array arm is also the reachable half of the NoSQL operator family and belongs with nosql-injection when the backend is a document store; it is here only as an identifier shape. The corrected okf_concept for this row is still playbooks/object-ownership.md -- the second identifier is the source id, not the concept. REPAIR PASS. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. The query and path arms are on it; the array-wrapping arm is not, and gains a second and stronger reason: it needs a request body, and a Task whose whole selection is bb:effects read_only opens with body_allowed false (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, :3667) -- so it cannot be SENT under object-ownership alone, not merely not replayed. Where it is sent from a Task that also selected a Playbook admitting to changing something, it stops at an agent-filed Observation and reaches no Finding. One further spelling wall on the wildcard-segment arm: rk2_test_request_problem refuses a path segment that is '.' or '..' and any '%2e' (20260815T000000Z...:222-225), so a wildcard spelled as a dot segment cannot be a Test arm even though origin_form() would forward it.

technique: Ask whether two lookup arguments for one object type are guarded by the same check, by fetching a foreign object first by the identifier the interface uses and then by an alternate key the schema also accepts.

preconditions: object_identifier plus body_parameter or query_parameter, and an introspection result or observed traffic showing more than one lookup argument on one type -- a username, a slug or an address beside the id.
baseline: Query the type by id for an object the Identity owns, twice unchanged. Populated both times, asserted body_equals.
variant: Query the SAME foreign object by the alternate argument. Populated where the id path denied is the finding.
control: Query the foreign object by ID. It must be DENIED. Without this the variant's success is ordinary access to something that was public all along.
payload_family: lookup-key substitution on one type -- id, username, slug, email -- with the object held constant
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487) for both response_differential Observations, citing the two Receipts the run made; src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016) supplies the test-linked Receipt. Where the queries travel as POST bodies the Test lane cannot replay them, so the closing Test has to be a GET-shaped arm on the same subject or the transition has no Receipt to cite.
supported_evidence: response_differential for the variant role (the alternate key answered) and the control role (the id path denied), both from Receipts the same run made.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the alternate key denies the same way the id path did.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the first populated response to the alternate key. Course of action: stop; one foreign object, read-only, is the whole claim. Second trigger: the alternate key is about to be swept across a range of values. Course of action: refuse; that is an identifier oracle with a different class and a different budget. Scope of halt: the type. Resume condition: none needed. Who is told: the Task's verdict. What is recorded: the two queries side by side, both Receipts, and the identifier of the foreign object.
notes: Distinct from the shape census: that one re-spells the SAME key, this one uses a DIFFERENT key, and the two fail for different reasons -- a coercion in the lookup versus a resolver somebody added without the guard. Where the alternate key also distinguishes an identifier that exists from one that does not, the by-product is information_disclosure.identifier_oracle, which is one of the nine unemitted classes and belongs to the orphans group rather than here; this row must not be widened into a sweep to reach it. REPAIR PASS. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. Where the alternate key travels in the query, the row is on it and closes directly. Where it travels in a POST body -- which is the ordinary shape for the GraphQL surface the source describes -- it is off it twice: the Test lane carries no body, AND the body cannot be sent at all from a Task whose whole selection is read_only (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, :3667). In that case the row stops at an agent-filed response_differential and reaches no Finding, and the closing Test has to be a GET-shaped arm on the same subject or the transition has no Receipt to cite.

preconditions: multiple_test_identities, object_identifier, state_changing_method on the second route. The last of those is what puts it outside this Playbook.
baseline: Task B: PATCH or PUT the object B owns, naming one property, and read what comes back. This establishes that the write path works for this caller and what a successful write answers.
variant: Task B: the same write shape naming the object A owns, with the identifier taken from a listing route rather than guessed. A success, or an answer that differs from the refusal the control draws, is the claim.
control: Task B: the same write shape naming an identifier that certainly names nothing -- a UUID the reading minted itself. It must fail. Without it, a success on A's object cannot be told from a route that answers 200 to every write it is sent. Plus the read of A's object from Task B afterwards, which is what says the write landed rather than being accepted and discarded.
payload_family: identifiers harvested from one route and presented to another, under a write verb
runtime_writer: The reading executes and the Runtime writes its Observation; what it needs is a Task whose Playbook selection is not read_only throughout, because _body_allowed is the MAXIMUM over the selection (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, :3667, used at :3052) and a write needs a body. src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited. for the identifier differential, which travels in the path. src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.) for the state_change edge, allowed_provenance {receipt} (0018_vocabularies.sql:229-230), cited from the read that sees the side effect.
supported_evidence: response_differential, written by close_test_replay for the foreign-object arm named by a status_differs assertion against the minted-identifier control -- a request-line differential in the path, under one Identity. Plus an agent-filed state_change edge from the confirming read. Where the write's PAYLOAD rather than its identifier is the variable, the differential is in a request body, the Test lane cannot carry it, and that arm stops at an Observation and reaches no Finding.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the foreign-object write refuses the way the minted-identifier control did while the baseline shows the write path works for this caller.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the second leg is about to use a write verb. Course of action: stop and hand the reading to the Playbook that holds the class -- authorization.state_transition on api-authorization, or authorization.object_property_write, which is one of the nine classes nothing currently emits. Scope of halt: the reading, under this slug. Resume condition: none here; the chain resumes under a Playbook whose effects admit a write and whose baseline is not a stable session. Who is told: the operator, with both routes named, because the disclosing half is a finding on its own. What is recorded: the disclosing route, the identifiers it handed over, and the refusal to use them under a write verb.
owner_ticket: 101 -- authorization.object_property_write has no emitter among the fifty Playbooks. The class is admissible on object-ownership: src/redkraken/playbook.py:429 requires an output to carry the Playbook's own bb:category prefix, object-ownership's category is authorization, and authorization.object_property_write carries it. Ticket 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs, so the gap closes inside this ticket. SECOND, SEPARATE EDIT the same ticket must make or this row does not run: object-ownership is bb:effects read_only with bb:baseline stable_session and its step 6 says in as many words that it does not write to an object, so bb:effects and bb:risk must move together -- playbook.py:95-112 will not let risk sit below what effects imply -- or the write half needs its own Playbook.
notes: RE-STATED IN THIS REPAIR PASS from out_of_scope to reachable, per DECISIONS.md D3, which names this row explicitly ('g04 object-ownership x1'). D3's reasoning applies: the BRIEF's rule is that a row is blocked, refused or out_of_scope when it cannot name a bounded execution path AND evidence the Runtime can write, and a missing emitter is neither -- the harness sends the request and promote_proposal writes the Observation. DISAGREEMENT RECORDED, AND THE DECISION FOLLOWED, which is what D3's own preamble asks for: the emitter gap is not this row's only obstacle. The reading needs a request body, and no Task whose whole selection is read_only can send one (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, :3667) -- so 'reachable' here means reachable from a Task that selected something else alongside object-ownership, and the owner_ticket above says so rather than leaving a reader to discover it. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. The identifier arm is on it; the property-payload arm is not. THE READ HALF of the chain -- a listing that discloses identifiers it should not -- is information_disclosure and is already covered by the first object-ownership row above; splitting them is what stops a run reporting the chain under a read_only Playbook and mutating an object to do it.

preconditions: multiple_test_identities, object_identifier, and a served bundle in which the transformation is visible -- or one known reference-and-object pair from which it can be recovered.
baseline: The caller's own reference, decoded offline with js_parse over the bundle and jq over the decoded value, so the structure is named rather than assumed.
variant: The reference recomputed for a neighbouring identifier and sent through the ordinary two-Task reading above.
control: A recomputed reference for an identifier that certainly does not exist, which shows the recomputation is right rather than the route being permissive; plus the two identical baseline sends.
payload_family: a recomputed opaque reference -- a hash, an encoding or a keyed transform recovered from the client, never guessed
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123. (The 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition every earlier version of this row cited is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical.) The offline half writes content_match, allowed_provenance {tool_run} (0018_vocabularies.sql:233-234); its admissible producers are the four binaries in the run_tool enum -- jq, js_map, js_parse, js_routes -- AND a browse run, because browser_runs.tool_run_id is a foreign key into tool_runs (20260814T040000Z...:411-417) and enforce_kind_provenance checks the provenance_kind string only (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364). The network half writes response_differential from its own Receipts and src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay, live definition 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016. The Observation kind is derived from the specification's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1069) and inserted at :1072; the ONLY testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row any runtime writes is that function's, at :1125, and 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649 is the gate that will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run cited.
supported_evidence: content_match from the js_parse or jq run that names the transformation in the bundle, carried as a supporting edge; plus response_differential for the variant and control roles from the request half.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, when the recomputed reference is refused while the control shows the recomputation is correct.
stop_conditions: Halt trigger: the transformation cannot be recovered from the bundle or from a known pair. Course of action: stop; guessing an opaque reference is a sweep, not a reading, and the control that would rule out a permissive route no longer exists. Scope of halt: the endpoint. Resume condition: a bundle or a pair that names the transform. Who is told: the Task's verdict as inconclusive, naming what could not be recovered. What is recorded: the tool run label, the artifact hash of the bundle, and the recovered transform stated explicitly so the recomputation is checkable.
notes: The row that makes the content_match provenance concrete for this slug: an obfuscated reference is the one place in object-ownership where an offline tool run carries evidence rather than context, and it only counts because jq and js_parse are two of the four binaries the enum admits. A model that 'reads the bundle' and reports the transform has produced no observation at all. REPAIR PASS: D4 applied to the phrasing -- 'the four binaries' is not the whole of {tool_run} provenance, because a browse run satisfies it too; this row's own reading uses js_parse and jq, so its steps do not change, but the Playbook prose must not tell the next reader that a browse run cannot carry the kind. FINDING PATH: an Observation an agent files lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out, but only close_test_replay writes a testing -> supported transition, so the TEST ITSELF must be the differential. A row reaches a Finding only where its difference lives in the request line -- method, scheme, host, port, path, query -- or in which Identity the run was opened under. The network half is on it: the recomputed reference travels in the path or the query and the Test closes it directly. The offline half is not, and stops at a content_match Observation -- which is correct, because recovering a transformation is not a claim about the target's authorization.

preconditions: tech_edge_proxy, web_surface, read_method, header_parameter. X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Client-IP and X-Custom-IP-Authorization are in NEITHER proxy.HOP_BY_HOP NOR the x-redkraken- internal prefix, so they forward. 127.0.0.1 is printable ASCII and is a HEADER VALUE, not our url -- scope.address_refusal (src/redkraken/scope.py:250) refuses loopback as a destination we dial, not as a string a target reads.
baseline: GET the refused path twice with no forwarded header. The refusal, shown stable.
variant: The same request with exactly one forwarded-address header set to a loopback or internal literal, one header per request.
control: (a) The two identical baseline sends. (b) The same header set to an ordinary public address the deployment has no reason to trust, which must still be refused. That is what separates 'the rule trusts this header' from 'any extra header confuses the edge'.
payload_family: caller-written client-address and caller-written trust headers, one per request
runtime_writer: promote_proposal -- src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (the live CREATE OR REPLACE; the INSERT INTO observations carrying the kind the AGENT named is at :1116, and the proposal element lists are open, src/redkraken/roster.py:1356-1370), reached from src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -- the agent files credential_effect or header_policy_observed, both {receipt} or {receipt,tool_run} (src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:229,236), from the two mcp__rk2__http_request Receipts. close_test_replay is NOT in this row's chain: it cannot see a header.
supported_evidence: credential_effect, agent-filed through promote_proposal from the arm's Receipt, provenance {receipt} -- a 403 becoming a 200 in answer to a caller-written trust header is a response to a presented credential. header_policy_observed rides alongside as the edge that names the header. NOT response_differential: a Test action cannot carry the header the two arms differ by.
refuted_evidence: credential_effect with polarity refutes: the refusal is identical under every forwarded header, so the decision is not made on a caller-supplied address. Agent-filed from the same Receipts; no Test closes here.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed condition): the listed header names are exhausted, or the public-address control also turns the refusal into a 200 (which means the edge reacts to the header's presence, not its value) | COURSE OF ACTION: stop and report inconclusive naming the control's behaviour; do not sweep an address range through the header | SCOPE OF HALT: the route | RESUME CONDITION: an operator or a surface fact names the header the backend actually reads -- an echo route, a debug route, a leaked error page | WHO IS TOLD: the Task's record; the operator if a protected route was served | WHAT IS RECORDED: each header name and value, both statuses, and the public-address control's status
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. These same headers are what make rate_limiting.per_origin -- one of the nine property classes no Playbook emits -- reachable at all, because they are the only caller-writable input to a per-origin key that survives our door. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. The whole differential of this row is a request HEADER, one of the caller-written forwarded-address names. A Test action carries a method and a url and nothing else: _Door.send calls proxy.spend with `url` and `method` only (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), although proxy.spend accepts headers and a body, and record_test_action compares the Receipt to the action over method, scheme, host, port and path (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1387-1391). So close_test_replay never sees the two arms this row differences, and close_test_replay (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125) is the only writer of a hypothesis_transitions row whose from_status is `testing` and whose to_status is `supported`, and rk2_finding_refusal (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649) will not open a Finding without one joined through test_run_receipts to the very Test run being cited. The agent-filed Observation named above IS a real hypothesis_evidence edge -- rk2_promote_hypotheses (20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) writes it from an agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind -- and that is the whole of what this reading produces. Write it up as an Observation, not as a settled claim.

preconditions: read_method, tech_edge_proxy, web_surface, and a path the front end refuses. The method enum on mcp__rk2__http_request is exactly GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE HEAD OPTIONS, so the whole survey is seven calls and no eighth is spellable.
baseline: GET the refused path twice, unchanged. The refusal, shown stable.
variant: The same path under each of the other six methods, one per request, everything else identical.
control: (a) The two identical GET sends above. (b) The same six methods against an unrestricted path, which must be served or must 405 CONSISTENTLY -- so a 200 on the arm is the rule's verb list and not the deployment answering every unusual verb the same way.
payload_family: the seven-member method enum against one path; no body, no headers beyond the baseline's
runtime_writer: close_test_replay -- src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072 (INSERT INTO observations, kind derived from the Test specification), reached from src/redkraken/replay.py:106
supported_evidence: response_differential -- a status_differs assertion names the arm method's action against the GET baseline (401/403 turning into 200, or a HEAD served where GET was refused).
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every method answers the same refusal, so the rule is bound to the resource and not to a verb list.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed condition): a method that mutates (PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is about to be sent against a path whose effect is not known, or the seven methods are exhausted | COURSE OF ACTION: send the read methods and OPTIONS only; park the mutating three for an operator rather than sending them, because this Playbook is declared read_only and a 200 to a DELETE is a deletion | SCOPE OF HALT: the run. bb:effects is read_only and a mutating verb is outside what the Playbook was approved as | RESUME CONDITION: an operator grants the mutating half explicitly against a target where a write is admitted | WHO IS TOLD: the operator, through mcp__rk2__park_for_human, before any mutating verb leaves | WHAT IS RECORDED: each method, its status, whether the arm's answer was the application's, and the fact that the mutating verbs were withheld
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: Deduplicated across pd-web-a 'The edge rule is not the same for every method', pd-web-b4 'Authorization constraint written as a verb list' and pkb-completed-web 'The authorisation rule names a method list'. Two corrections to what the miners recorded. notes: Harness-reachable, and it CONFLICTS with the shipped ceiling: file-resolution step 8 refuses stream wrappers wholesale. That refusal was written against the escalation (read source, read config, build a chain, execute) and this is the separable acceptance question, whose variant discloses nothing the reading did not already hold. Ticket 101 should decide it explicitly as a step rather than leave the ceiling reading as if it also refused the acceptance question. One correction the reference needs either way: php-filter-chain-lfi-rce.md states the chain's prerequisite as a caller-controlled include plus a guessable path, and php://temp as the chain's own resource removes the path requirement (pd-web-b2.json:4), which also means open_basedir is no longer a mitigation for it. Dedup: pd-web-b2.json:2, pd-web-b2.json:4 and pkb-completed-web.json:66 are one reading. ON THE FINDING PATH. The differential is in the request line, so the Test itself can be the differential and close_test_replay can carry the Hypothesis to 'supported'. Two spelling rules the specification checker imposes and the step text must repeat: rk2_test_request_problem (20260815T000000Z:194-227) refuses a '.' or '..' segment in the PATH -- it tests split_part(path, '?', 1) against '(^|/)\.\.?(/|$)', so the query string is NOT searched -- and refuses '%2e' ANYWHERE in the url, query included. A traversal that rides the query string spelled with literal dots is therefore Test-expressible; the same traversal percent-encoded is not, and the same traversal moved into the path is not. D4 correction applied, and one narrower fact behind it. The acceptance question closes on body_differs alone -- wrapper arm against plain arm, both miss controls answering like a miss -- and needs no decode, so the row is on the Finding path with two GETs and one compare_responses. If the base64 IS decoded for the report, jq is the wrong reader: the registry gives jq exactly two arguments, filter and input (20260814T030000Z__an_offline_tool_becomes_evidence.sql:205-207), with no raw-input flag, so a non-JSON body does not parse. The reader that does work is a browse run, which is a tool_run by FK (20260814T040000Z...:417) and satisfies content_match's {tool_run} directly per D4. ONE HAZARD THIS ROW INHERITS AND THE STEP TEXT MUST CARRY. Every arm here differs from every other arm ONLY in the query string, and record_test_action (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1630-1637) matches a Receipt to its action on the method, the scheme, the host, the port and the path -- and says in its own comment that it does not compare the query, because only the query's digest is on the Receipt. So the runtime cannot detect an arm's Receipt being recorded against the wrong ordinal. The Test still closes and the differential is still real; what is missing is the runtime's check that the arms were matched honestly. The discipline that substitutes for it: record each arm's Receipt immediately after its own send, never in a batch at the end.

preconditions: a relying-party endpoint that accepts a token plus an identity field and issues a session; a valid token for an account the Program controls and a second account the Program controls. NOTE the trigger gap: identity-parsing's bb:triggers_all is state_changing_method plus tech_saml, so this reading cannot fire on an OAuth or OIDC deployment as the Playbook is declared today.
baseline: POST the token together with its own identity. A session for that account. Sent twice.
variant: POST the same token together with the SECOND account's identifier, then read the identity route carrying the returned session to see which account it belongs to.
control: Two legs: the identical baseline pair, and a structurally valid but never-issued token submitted with the first identity, which must fail. That separates 'the endpoint trusts the identity beside the token' from 'the endpoint accepts anything in that field'.
