refuted_evidence: response_invariant, agent-filed -- the substituted request is answered the way the unissued token is, or the session belongs to the token's own subject.
stop_conditions: (1) halt trigger, observed: a session is issued for an account other than the one the token names (2) course of action: log the session out through the application's own route and stop; do not substitute a third identity (3) scope of halt: route -- the session-issuing endpoint (4) resume condition: the operator confirms the second account is ours and a bounded re-run is agreed for the report (5) who is told: the engagement operator, immediately (6) what is recorded: both identifiers, the token used, the session issued and its logout
owner_ticket: reachable, and the reading needs no ticket. But it is UNGRADABLE -- it stops at an Observation and cannot open a Finding -- and per D3's own reasoning (a gap that closes inside a ticket is not 'blocked') the ticket that would make it gradable is named rather than left implicit: NEW -- Let a Test request carry the header and body the door already accepts. PRICED IN SOURCE THIS PASS, and the price is smaller than the corpus prose that routes around it: (1) rk2_test_spec_problem closes the key set of a Test request by name -- setup and cleanup admit 'method' and 'url' only (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:345-350), an action admits 'ordinal, role, kind, method, url' only (:375-379) -- so two key-set checks widen in one CREATE OR REPLACE; (2) rk2_test_request_problem (:194-227) gains validation for the two new keys, reusing the door's own patterns already written down in roster.py (header NAME ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}\Z, VALUE ^[\x20-\x7e]{0,1024}\Z, body 0..65536), same migration; (3) _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) passes headers= and body= through -- proxy.spend already accepts both (proxy.py:4216-4224), so this is two lines and NO proxy, door-schema or identity work; (4) one real design question, and only one: record_test_action (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1630-1637) matches a Receipt to its action on method, scheme, host, port and path, and deliberately not on the query, so two actions differing only in a header or a body would be as indistinguishable to it as two differing only in the query already are -- either the Receipt gains a request digest or the new keys inherit the looseness the query has. _body_allowed (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646) needs no change: a read_only selection stays body-less, which is ticket 96's rule and not a defect.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the SAML or OIDC document rides in a POST body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. From pkb-completed-web.json:47. It is the same reading the shipped Playbook performs for a signed assertion whose subject is stated twice -- two readers, one credential, an identity they disagree about -- carried out on the OAuth-client half, and its class is the same authentication.federation_trust. The corpus defect it exposes is the trigger set, not the class: tech_saml alone means this Playbook never fires on the deployments where the reading is cheapest. Deliberately NOT folded in here: the third-party half (a genuine provider token minted for a different client_id, or a provider that never verified the email claim) is refused -- it needs an OAuth client the tester registers at a vendor's own authorization server, which the card refuses as claiming a third-party resource and as a vendor API subject, and the in-scope alternative of editing an aud or email claim needs a signing primitive this harness does not have (pd-web-b4.json:34, pkb-completed-web.json:49). THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. Its differential is not in the request line, so no Test action can express it: _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) hands proxy.spend a url and a method and nothing else, on every part of a specification (replay.py:390-395). The Observation is agent-filed through promote_proposal, lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z:530, which does not filter on the cited kind) and can never carry the Hypothesis from 'testing' to 'supported' -- close_test_replay (20260816T000000Z:1125) is the only writer of that transition and rk2_finding_refusal (20260815T120000Z:640-650) demands it. The reading is legitimate and reportable; it is not a Finding, and a Playbook step must not promise one. Concretely: every arm of this row differs from its baseline in the POSTED DOCUMENT, and a Test request carries no body at any position. Note that bb:effects for identity-parsing is mutates_session, not read_only, so _body_allowed (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646) returns true and the ORDINARY door does carry the document -- the wall here is the replay lane alone, not the Task's authority. The Test that could still be written -- two identity-route GETs, one per session, differenced on body_differs -- is a different claim (which account is behind this session) and must not be labelled as proof of the parsing defect. One deployment-shaped escape hatch worth naming: where the relying party takes the token and the identity as QUERY parameters rather than in a posted body, the whole differential moves into the request line and the row IS on the Finding path. That is the shape to look for first.

preconditions: tech_orchestrator; a route with a server-side-dereferenced URL parameter (url_valued_parameter); operator authorisation to name an address on the target's side of the boundary.
baseline: Parameter set to the fetcher's own allowed host, sent twice unchanged.
variant: Parameter set to a cluster-internal service name, and at most once more to a service name the application's own body already mentioned.
control: The identical baseline pair, plus a name of the same shape that no cluster would define, so 'the suffix resolved' is separated from 'this fetcher answers every unknown host identically'.
payload_family: internal service DNS names as a parameter value the target resolves, never as this harness's own url.
runtime_writer: none -- nothing is sent. Capability-wise the writer would be close_test_replay, src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016, which derives the Observation kind from the Test SPECIFICATION at :1060-1070 and writes the one hypothesis_transitions row a Finding needs -- from_status testing, to_status supported, actor_kind runtime -- at :1125, driven from src/redkraken/replay.py:106: the internal name is a parameter VALUE the target resolves and not a URL this door dials, so scope.address_refusal (scope.py:250) never sees it and three ordinary requests would do it. That is exactly why it needs recording as a refusal rather than as a limit.
supported_evidence: none.
refuted_evidence: none.
stop_conditions: (1) halt trigger, observed: a run proposes any address on the cluster's side of the boundary -- a service name, an orchestrator API, a kubelet, an etcd member, a registry, a dashboard (2) course of action: refuse before the request; step 6 of this Playbook is that a reading which resolves one of those names has left the scope the Program granted (3) scope of halt: run -- this Playbook does not go into the cluster at any depth (4) resume condition: no resume under this Playbook; a corpus decision would have to move it, and ssrf-url-routing's ceiling names Kubernetes service addresses explicitly too (5) who is told: the model proposing it, through the drop reason, and the operator if such a request was actually sent (6) what is recorded: the refusal, both ceilings it rests on, and the fact that the technique is harness-reachable so the refusal is a decision and not a gap
owner_ticket: NEW -- Decide whether a fetcher-position reading may name one cluster-internal service address, and if so which Playbook carries the operator gate; today two Playbook ceilings refuse it and neither owns the decision
notes: From pd-infra.json:1, which marked it reachable. Harness-reachable it is; permitted it is not, and the two are different fields. Two independent corpus ceilings refuse it -- kubernetes step 6 forbids requesting anything in the cluster, and ssrf-url-routing's ceiling names a Kubernetes or Consul service address explicitly -- so it is a new-Playbook or operator-gate question rather than a step either Playbook may quietly grow. Recorded with the reason attached because it is cheap, it works, and it will be re-proposed. ATT&CK added per the cross-cutting finding that kubernetes, deployment and supply-chain carry no ATT&CK identifier between them: T1526 Cloud Service Discovery is the technique name for exactly this control-plane reading, and mining/methodology.json:11 dropped it for exactly the reason this row refuses it -- there is no in-scope step. baseline: A link-local address in the same range with nothing behind it, sent twice; it fails one way.
variant: The metadata root only -- never an identity, credentials, user-data, public-keys or token path.
control: The identical baseline pair, plus the same root sent without the vendor's required metadata header, which a v2-enforcing service must refuse. That is what makes the variant's answer the service rather than any host in that range.
payload_family: metadata ROOTS only. The whole credential half of the source's list stays unsent.
runtime_writer: none under this Playbook -- nothing is sent. The card permits reading the response shape and refuses retrieving the credentials, so the reading is not refused in general; it is refused HERE, by step 6, which forbids requesting a metadata service. supported_evidence: none under this Playbook.

preconditions: bb:triggers_all flow_step and state_changing_method; the subject is a route something else leads to. A run that has not walked the flow does not know which steps exist and cannot say a step was skipped -- it can only say a route answered. bb:baseline is pristine_surface, so a flow another Playbook advanced under this one turns the verdict into a statement about two runs.
baseline: Walk the flow in order as the interface does, storing every answer, all as whichever Identity the Task was opened under. Then read the authoritative outcome route: that is what the outcome reads as when the flow was earned.
variant: On a session that has completed no earlier step, send the subject step exactly as the walk sent it -- same method, same path, same body, only the earlier calls missing -- and then read the authoritative outcome route again.
control: Two legs. The pristine read: the outcome route on a session that has taken no steps at all, which is what 'nothing has happened' looks like. And the outcome route read twice on the completed flow with nothing sent between, because body_differs on an outcome page fires on a timestamp or a Date header as readily as on a state change.
payload_family: none. The step's own request, replayed with its predecessors missing.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay, src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016, which derives the Observation kind from the Test SPECIFICATION at :1060-1070 and writes the one hypothesis_transitions row a Finding needs -- from_status testing, to_status supported, actor_kind runtime -- at :1125, driven from src/redkraken/replay.py:106 for the outcome reads -- a Test whose actions are the three outcome reads with body_differs naming the post-variant read against the pristine read, deriving response_differential; the completed-flow pair carries no such assertion and derives response_invariant. promote_proposal, called from src/redkraken/execution.py:518, live definition src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with its INSERT INTO observations at :1116 (the kind the AGENT named, gated only by observation_kinds.allowed_provenance). The 20260814T070000Z:1631 definition this ledger cited before is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical for the kind bb:evidence actually declares: the agent files state_change ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:229) citing the Receipt of the outcome read that saw the effect, which is the writer the Playbook prose never names.
supported_evidence: state_change -- the authoritative outcome shows the step's effect with the earlier steps never taken, against a control that shows the same effect when they were. response_differential carries the pair that closes the Test.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the outcome after the lone step matches the pristine read; the step was refused and the state never moved.
stop_conditions: (1) halt trigger, observed: the outcome matches neither the completed-flow answer nor the pristine one (2) course of action: record it and stop; a half-applied flow is a state the application did not expect and is not evidence about ordering (3) scope of halt: route -- this flow; the reading does not continue into further spellings from a half-applied state (4) resume condition: the flow is cancelled or emptied through the target's own route and the outcome reads back as pristine (5) who is told: the engagement operator, with the half-applied state described, before anything else is sent (6) what is recorded: the ordered walk, the lone step sent, all three outcome reads, and the unwind request with its read-back
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable
notes: The Playbook as shipped. What the ledger adds is the writer for state_change, which bb:evidence declares for both the control and the supported variant and which the prose leaves unattributed: promote_proposal writes it from a Receipt, and the earlier reading of the card that called state_change writer-less was wrong. Only two mining rows named this Playbook and neither is this reading, so this row is built from the Playbook and the schema. mined_from is empty per D7: this row is the group's own reading, built from the Playbook plus the schema rather than from any of the 665 mined rows. ON THE FINDING PATH, CONDITIONALLY, and the condition has to be in the step text. The three outcome reads are GETs and their differential is the request line, so close_test_replay can settle them. What cannot be a Test request is a flow step that needs a body: _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) sends url and method only, on setup as well as on actions (replay.py:390-395), and rk2_test_request_problem (20260815T000000Z:194-227) names no body key at all. So the reading reaches a Finding where the flow's steps are expressible as method plus url -- a POST or PUT whose parameters ride the query string, or a bare state-changing POST -- and stops at an agent-filed state_change Observation where they are not. Where they are not, the walk is performed with mcp__rk2__http_request (routing is bb:effects mutates_object, so _body_allowed at src/redkraken/execution.py:3646 returns true and the door carries the body) and only the outcome reads enter the replay lane.

preconditions: bb:triggers_all flow_step and state_changing_method, AND the lone step of the previous row was refused -- the refusal is what makes this reading meaningful, because it may belong to the front of the stack rather than to the application. Every spelling stays at the recorded route on the recorded host: a spelling that leaves it is not this reading.
baseline: The completed-flow outcome and the pristine outcome from the previous row, both already stored.
variant: One request at a time, each on its own session that has taken no earlier step: the same path under a different method the route also serves, including HEAD; the same path with a trailing slash, a doubled separator, a dot segment or a mixed-case segment; the same request sent as GET carrying X-HTTP-Method-Override (also X-Method-Override, X-HTTP-Method) naming the step's verb. After each, read the authoritative outcome route.
control: Three legs. The pristine outcome read. The completed-flow outcome read twice, so a body_differs verdict is not a timestamp. And the decisive one the references insist on: the same decoration applied to a path that certainly does not exist, which must stay 404 -- otherwise a server that answers 200 to anything of that shape has produced every result.
payload_family: the same recorded step spelled differently: an alternate method, a path decoration that normalises to the same resource, and the method-override header. Not proxy or client-IP headers, not the origin IP, not a different port or scheme.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay, src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016, which derives the Observation kind from the Test SPECIFICATION at :1060-1070 and writes the one hypothesis_transitions row a Finding needs -- from_status testing, to_status supported, actor_kind runtime -- at :1125, driven from src/redkraken/replay.py:106 for the outcome reads (status_differs / body_differs naming the post-variant read against the pristine read, deriving response_differential), plus promote_proposal, called from src/redkraken/execution.py:518, live definition src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with its INSERT INTO observations at :1116 (the kind the AGENT named, gated only by observation_kinds.allowed_provenance). The 20260814T070000Z:1631 definition this ledger cited before is superseded by that CREATE OR REPLACE; the behaviour is identical filing state_change ({receipt}) from the outcome Receipt. The override header forwards: x-http-method-override is in neither proxy.HOP_BY_HOP (proxy.py:316) nor the internal x-redkraken- prefix, and its name matches the door's header NAME pattern.
supported_evidence: state_change -- a spelling produced the step's effect at the authoritative outcome route with the earlier steps never taken, and the nonexistent-path decoration control stayed 404.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every spelling leaves the outcome at the pristine read.

notes: PARTLY ON THE FINDING PATH, AND THIS IS THE ONE ROW IN THE FILE THAT SPLITS. The shipped step 4, with two additions from the mining. preconditions: bb:triggers_all flow_step and state_changing_method; TWO multi-step flows with per-phase endpoints, at least one reachable without a credential, sharing a plausible phase marker. The reading runs inside ONE Task holding ONE Identity, because the session state it depends on lives in that Identity's cookie jar: Session.capture (identity.py:363-371) extracts the target's Set-Cookie into self.jar and Session.inject (identity.py:330-340) puts it back on every later request. THE JAR CANNOT BE REWOUND, which is what fixes the arm ORDER below and what blocks the three-jar form of this reading entirely.
baseline: First, before anything has been walked: GET the guarded late step of the flow that challenges the caller. It refuses. Send it twice, unchanged.
variant: Third, and only third: walk step 1 of the guarded flow, then steps 1 and 2 of the UNGUARDED flow, then request the guarded late step again. A guard that is now satisfied says one session slot was serving both flows.
control: Two legs, and the first has to be sent SECOND, before the variant, because the jar only accumulates. Leg one: an equal number of unrelated requests on the same session -- a search, a product page -- then the guarded late step again. It must still refuse, which rules out 'any warm session passes' and 'the guard only checks that a session exists'. Leg two: the two identical baseline refusals, without which body_differs on the guarded step is the Date header.
payload_family: none. The application's own two flows, interleaved in an order it did not anticipate: guarded_1 -> unguarded_1 -> unguarded_2 -> guarded_late.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay, src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1016, which derives the Observation kind from the Test SPECIFICATION at :1060-1070 and writes the one hypothesis_transitions row a Finding needs -- from_status testing, to_status supported, actor_kind runtime -- at :1125, driven from src/redkraken/replay.py:106: the three requests of the guarded late step are the actions, with status_differs naming the post-variant read against the control read, deriving response_differential. promote_proposal, called from src/redkraken/execution.py:518, live definition src/redkraken/migrations/20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with its INSERT INTO observations at :1116, files state_change ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:229) from the Receipt of the satisfied guard -- the kind routing's own bb:evidence declares for both the control and the supported variant role.

refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the guarded late step refuses identically in all three positions, so the two flows do not share a slot.
stop_conditions: (1) halt trigger, observed: the guarded phase is entered -- the late step answers rather than refusing (2) course of action: stop there and send nothing further in either flow; actually completing a reset or a registration on the far side of the guard is an account takeover and not a reading (3) scope of halt: route -- the guarded flow; the unguarded flow needs no unwind because only its early steps were walked (4) resume condition: the operator confirms the designated account and agrees a bounded re-run for the report (5) who is told: the engagement operator, immediately, because a guard that was satisfied without its own predecessor is an authentication-adjacent result (6) what is recorded: the exact interleaving sent, all three reads of the guarded step, and the account named in every arm

Two shards carry it and both filed it under a NEW target nobody owns: owasp.json:14 (NEW:session-puzzling, WSTG-SESS-08) and wiki-delta.json:9 (NEW:session-state-puzzling). It is business_logic.workflow_order by its own terms -- a step's guard satisfied without the step before it -- so routing is the emitter and no new class is needed. ON THE FINDING PATH where the walked steps are expressible as method plus url, and only there: _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) hands proxy.spend a url and a method and nothing else, on setup as well as actions (replay.py:390-395), and rk2_test_spec_problem closes the key set of a setup request to exactly 'method' and 'url' (20260815T000000Z:345-350). The agent never sees a Set-Cookie -- WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS (proxy.py:376-385) strips it on every path including the unbound one (proxy.py:3083) -- and the only jar is the leased Identity's, which accumulates and cannot be reset (Session.capture mutates self.jar, identity.py:363-371; a Task names one Identity, 20261101T000000Z__a_task_names_the_one_identity_it_acts_as.sql). preconditions: spa_surface, path_parameter, read_method, web_surface. The recon pass recorded a route whose page issues at least one same-origin sub-request after load; without a second Receipt there is no sink. The mission runs under whichever Identity the Task was opened with -- there is no identity_slot argument (ticket 97) and the Playbook must not name one.
baseline: One browse mission: navigate to the recorded route with the segment carrying the ordinary value the page's own links use, wait_for the settled state, capture_dom. Read the mission's Receipt list and record the SECOND Receipt's request line: the route the page built and the byte position of the segment inside it.
variant: The identical mission with only the segment replaced by one encoded traversal spelling (%2e%2e%2f and its case/double-encoded variants), one spelling per mission. Read the Receipt list again: a Receipt whose request line names a route different from the baseline's is the differential.
control: A third mission byte-identical to the baseline, run separately, whose Receipt list must name the same route as the baseline's. Two identical missions are what rule out a page whose sub-request route varies on its own -- a cache-busting segment, a rotating shard host, a route chosen from a feature flag. Without that pair a differing request line is noise. The comparison is over Receipt REQUEST LINES, never over the loaded document: body_differs on the document fires on the Date header alone.
payload_family: an encoded relative-path traversal inside one path segment, one spelling per mission
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, which inserts the observations row with the kind the AGENT named (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:1116) against a Receipt the browse mission produced; every browser mission request is receipted (20260814T040000Z__a_browser_mission_runs_behind_the_door.sql:1362-1381). NOT src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -- see notes.
supported_evidence: response_differential, AGENT-FILED through promote_proposal from the variant mission's Receipt ({receipt} provenance, 0018_vocabularies.sql:219-220), cited as role=variant polarity=supports; the same kind from the control mission cited as role=control polarity=supports. That is the pair the Playbook's bb:evidence bar asks for and rk2_promote_hypotheses writes both edges with no filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530). It is NOT close_test_replay evidence: a browse run is never a Test action, TEST_ACTION_KINDS = ('request',) (src/redkraken/roster.py:415).
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, agent-filed from the variant mission's Receipt: the page requested the same route with the traversal still encoded inside the segment. That is the Playbook's declared refutation and it is the same provenance ({receipt}).
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a mission Receipt shows the page requesting a route whose host is not the recorded origin, or the proxy refuses a mission request as out of scope, or the mission hits its step ceiling before the sub-request fires. COURSE OF ACTION: send no further traversal spelling; do not widen the segment; record the mission as inconclusive. SCOPE OF HALT: the route -- other recorded routes on the same Application stay open. RESUME: an operator confirms the moved route is inside the compiled scope, or a different route is chosen. WHO IS TOLD: the Task's operator, through the inconclusive verdict on the Task. WHAT IS RECORDED: the mission label, both Receipt lists verbatim, the traversal spelling sent, and the refusal reason the proxy returned.
owner_ticket: NEW: let a Test action open a browser mission, so an injection.client_path claim can reach a Finding. Until then this row is capped at an Observation by design, not by oversight.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the ceiling is mission, which ticket 211 does not touch. The ceiling paragraph below still holds. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING: the differential lives in a request mission rather than an http_request at all -- a browse run, and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so it is not expressible as a Test action. close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), the Observation kind it writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1072), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:643-649; findings.opened_by_test_run_id at :85). An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. TEST_ACTION_KINDS = ('request',) (src/redkraken/roster.py:415), so the mission that carries the whole reading can be neither an action nor a setup request. The Hypothesis is supportable and the Playbook's bar is satisfiable, but the FINDING is not reachable from the mission alone: findings.opened_by_test_run_id (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:85) needs a closed Test, and rk2_test_spec_problem refuses any action that is not a request -- 'is not a request, which is the only kind of action this runtime performs' (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:389-391). So close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) can never write this Playbook's declared kinds for a browser reading. That is the concrete corpus defect in this Playbook: it names response_differential in bb:evidence and its only producer is a lane the Test spec cannot enter. Ticket 99 is resolved, so the mission itself is reachable by a model; the gap is the Test lane, not the browser lane.

(a) An unauthenticated GET of a sibling static-looking path the mission never steered onto (/v1/token.zzz) -- it must stay 401/404, otherwise the path was simply public and the traversal proved nothing. (b) The same unauthenticated GET sent twice back to back before the mission runs, which must be invariant: without that pair a body difference after the mission is indistinguishable from an origin that varies its own error page.

COURSE OF ACTION: stop the reading immediately, send no further cache-priming mission, and do not read the document's fields. SCOPE OF HALT: the whole run, because a shared cache now holds somebody else's data under a key we minted. RESUME: only after an operator has confirmed the cache entry has aged out or been purged. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, immediately, with the cache key. WHAT IS RECORDED: the cache key, the timestamp, the fact that a foreign document was served, and no field values from it.

An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. The two unauthenticated GETs on their own ARE Test-expressible, but a Test that sends them back to back with no mission between them measures nothing. The plain web-cache-deception variant -- our own authenticated GET of the static-looking path, then an unauthenticated GET of it -- IS entirely request-line and does close a Test, but that is web-cache's row (group g09) and not this Playbook's: what makes this row CSPT is that the PAGE issues the authenticated fetch. baseline: Retrieve the served bundles through mcp__rk2__http_request and run run_tool js_routes over them. That run enumerates the request paths the code composes. Record, for each, whether the path is a constant or is built by concatenation, and from which source the concatenated segment comes.
variant: Run run_tool js_map over the same bundles to resolve the composed paths back to their authoring positions, and keep only the routes whose composed segment traces to a caller-reachable source (a route parameter, location.search, location.hash). Those, and only those, are the routes the traversal mission is worth planning against.
control: Run the same two tool runs against a bundle the application serves that has no route composition in it at all -- a vendor chunk, a polyfill bundle. It must produce no composed route. Without that pair, a js_routes result that lists every string literal that looks like a path reads as a finding when it is the tool's ordinary output. Second control: the same bundle fetched twice and the two tool runs compared, invariant, so a hashed chunk name that rotates per deploy is not read as a changed route set.
payload_family: no payload: the served JavaScript bundles, read as source
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the INSERT INTO observations at :1116, filing content_match against the js_routes tool run. content_match's provenance is {tool_run} alone (0018_vocabularies.sql:233-234) and js_routes is one of exactly four binaries the run_tool enum admits, so the kind fits this reading natively.

This row supports the PRECONDITION of the traversal claim -- that a composition sink exists -- and not the claim itself.

That is a clean refutation of this Playbook's whole premise on this subject, at the cost of two tool runs and no request to a target beyond fetching the bundles.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a bundle url resolves outside the compiled Program scope, or js_parse or js_routes returns a parse failure on a bundle rather than a route list, or the bundle exceeds what one tool run will read. COURSE OF ACTION: stop enumerating; do not fall back to reading the bundle by hand into the Task's context; record the bundle url and the tool's failure verbatim. SCOPE OF HALT: the bundle -- other bundles of the same application stay open. RESUME: an operator confirms the bundle is in scope, or a source-mapped build of it is served. WHO IS TOLD: the Task's operator, through the inconclusive verdict on the Task. preconditions: file_parameter, state_changing_method, embedded_document, xml_request. An upload route that accepts image/svg+xml and a downstream step that rasterises or thumbnails it. A correlator minted on the Program's declared out-of-band channel. Approval on the Task, and the retrieval URL of every stored object recorded before the next one is stored.
baseline: Store a byte-identical SVG whose external reference is a data: literal. No arrival is expected, and its absence over the same window is what the variant is measured against.
variant: Store the same SVG with the reference pointing at the minted correlator on the declared channel. An arrival means the rasteriser resolved a reference the uploader chose.
control: The channel's own control arrival, which proves the channel is live and the correlator resolves. Plus the negative control that both arms were ACCEPTED at store time -- an arm rejected at upload proves nothing about the parser, and without that pair a silent variant is indistinguishable from a refused upload.
payload_family: an external reference inside a stored XML vector document, pointed at a minted correlator
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/callback.py:85 -> record_callback_interaction, which writes an observations row of kind callback_interaction, registered is_evidential = true with allowed_provenance {callback} (20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:344-350; ticket 98's 20260928T040000Z__the_out_of_band_refusal_was_reversed.sql:19 calls it evidential in as many words).
supported_evidence: callback_interaction, written by record_callback_interaction (src/redkraken/callback.py:85), cited role=variant polarity=supports. rk2_promote_hypotheses writes hypothesis_evidence from an agent-supplied observation_id with NO filter on the cited kind (20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530), so an out-of-band arrival does carry a bar. The store-time acceptance pair is filed alongside as an agent-filed response_invariant.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant on the two upload responses plus SILENCE on the channel over the declared window: both arms stored and nothing resolved. Note the limit -- a CONTROL arrival writes no Observation at all, because is_control and a null subject are one state tied by a CHECK (20261001T000000Z__a_control_arrival_is_what_makes_silence_a_finding.sql:45-52), so the control arrival is read for channel freshness and is not itself the refutation.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): an arrival whose correlator is not the one minted for this subject, or an arrival carrying content from the target's filesystem. COURSE OF ACTION: stop the reading, store no further document, and do not point a second reference anywhere. SCOPE OF HALT: the whole run. RESUME: an operator decision only. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, immediately. WHAT IS RECORDED: the correlator, the arrival time, and the fact that content arrived -- never the content.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING: the differential lives in a request body -- the external reference rides inside the uploaded SVG -- and the proof is an arrival rather than a response, and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so it is not expressible as a Test action. close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), the Observation kind it writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1072), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:643-649; findings.opened_by_test_run_id at :85). An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. record_callback_interaction is a runtime writer and its Observation is evidential (20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:348-350), but it is not close_test_replay, so it cannot write the testing -> supported transition either. The reference points at our own publisher. Not at file:///etc/hostname, which is a file read and a different class, and never at expect://, which is a shell and belongs to injection.command under approval. Second real limit worth carrying into the Playbook prose: the provenance is {callback} alone, so an agent may not file a Receipt under this kind and inherit the weight of an out-of-band confirmation. The neighbouring row that other shards filed under structured-injection (an uploaded OOXML document repacked with an external entity) is BLOCKED by the binary-body ceiling -- see the archive row -- while this one is not, because an SVG is ASCII.

baseline: Would be: an SVG with no onload, stored and served, rendering identically.
variant: Would be: the same SVG whose onload fetches the minted correlator.
control: Would be: the same bytes served from a route known to send Content-Disposition: attachment, which must produce no arrival, so the arrival is about the serving context and not about the file. The control is sound; the reading is still not taken.

runtime_writer: src/redkraken/callback.py:85 would write it; the refusal is not about the writer.

preconditions: path_valued_parameter, state_changing_method, web_surface. A path served from disk -- an assets or uploads directory -- inside the compiled Program scope. No Identity slot is needed or expressible (ticket 97). Approval on the Task, because a landed write is a stored object.
baseline: OPTIONS on the directory, reading the Allow and DAV response headers (headers come back to the caller, ticket 94, and neither is stripped by WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS at proxy.py:376). Then GET /uploads/<32-hex>.txt -- a 404, which fixes that the name is free.
variant: PUT /uploads/<32-hex>.txt, then GET the same URL. The 404 turning into a 200 is the write landing. In the TEST-LANE spelling the PUT carries NO body at all -- a Test action carries only ordinal, role, kind, method and url (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377) and _Door.send passes no body= to proxy.spend (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351) -- so what lands is a zero-length object and the read-back GET's STATUS is the whole signal. A marker body may be sent in the ordinary lane first to make the object findable by an operator; it is not what the Test measures.
control: PUT / with the identical body, which must be a 405. If the server 2xx's that too its status says nothing and only the read-back GET counts. Plus the pre-write GET sent twice, both 404, which is the invariant the post-write GET is measured against -- a directory that answers a soft-404 body with a varying request id would otherwise make body_differs fire on the id.
payload_family: an alternate write verb against a served directory path
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay: the pre-write GET, the post-write GET and the control PUT are all request actions, and a status_differs assertion naming the post-write GET makes it a response_differential.
supported_evidence: response_differential (role=variant) from close_test_replay between the pre-write and post-write GETs, closed by a status_differs assertion naming the post-write GET, against response_invariant (role=control) on the two pre-write GETs. Both kinds come straight out of close_test_replay with no agent-filed edge required.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant between the pre-write and post-write GETs: the PUT was accepted at the status line and nothing landed, which is exactly the acceptance-is-not-storage trap references/file-upload.md names.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a write lands outside the directory it was aimed at, or the removal (DELETE, or the route's own removal) fails. COURSE OF ACTION: stop, attempt no second write and no traversal spelling. SCOPE OF HALT: the origin, not just the route -- a write that escaped its directory has an unknown blast radius. RESUME: operator confirmation that the file is gone. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, immediately, with the landed path. WHAT IS RECORDED: the path written, the marker, the read-back answers and every removal attempt.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: REACHES A FINDING: the whole differential is in the request line (method and url only -- OPTIONS on the directory, PUT on the target path, GET on the same path), which is exactly what a Test action carries -- a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224) -- so close_test_replay settles the Test, writes the testing -> supported transition and rk2_finding_refusal's precondition exists. The ORDER is guaranteed rather than hoped for, which this row depends on: _walk runs 'Setup, then the actions, then the cleanup -- in that order, always' (src/redkraken/replay.py:381) and walks plan['actions'] in list order (:395), while rk2_test_spec_problem forces each action's stated ordinal to equal its position (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:381-383). So the pre-write GET, the PUT and the post-write GET are sent in that sequence by construction. This is the only file-upload row in the group that is a Test end to end with nothing outside it: every step is method plus url and nothing rides in a header or a body. The shipped Playbook is written entirely around forms and its bb:triggers_all requires file_parameter, so this reading never fires today -- that is a corpus gap the rewrite should close by adding path_valued_parameter + state_changing_method as an alternative trigger set, or by saying plainly that the method is the distinct reading. One correction to the source: it also carries a traversal PUT (PUT /uploads/../<name>) as a second variant. The request target is sent unnormalised, so it is expressible, but a write outside the declared directory has no bounded blast radius and no clean undo; the Playbook's step 8 ceiling refuses it, and the CoreFTP form in the source writes to C: by traversal, which is a system write and not a proof. One small inert text file, a random name, never an executable extension, never an existing path.

preconditions: file_parameter, state_changing_method, embedded_document, and an archive-accepting upload that both validates entries and extracts them. NOT SATISFIABLE: the archive must arrive byte-exact.
baseline: Would be: upload an archive containing only b.txt, then GET the extracted b.txt.
variant: Would be: upload an archive whose local header and central directory name the entry differently, or two concatenated archives with two EOCD records, and read whether the extracted set differs from the enumerated set.
control: Would be: upload an archive containing the disallowed name plainly, which must be rejected, confirming an enumeration check exists to disagree with; plus two identical uploads to fix the invariant. None of this is sendable.

supported_evidence: none available.
refuted_evidence: none available.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): the model composes a body containing any byte at or above 0x80 and the request is sent. COURSE OF ACTION: do not send it -- the bytes on the wire will not be the bytes intended and any verdict from them is fabricated. SCOPE OF HALT: every archive-shaped reading, on every route, for the whole run. RESUME: when an encoding argument (base64) or a binary body ships on mcp__rk2__http_request. WHO IS TOLD: nobody at run time; this is a corpus fact and belongs in the Playbook's prose. WHAT IS RECORDED: that the reading was not attempted, and why.
owner_ticket: NEW: give mcp__rk2__http_request a body encoding argument, so a binary document is expressible
notes: The missing capability is precise and is named in the source's own words: _body() re-encodes the model's JSON string as UTF-8 and its docstring says 'What that forbids is a body no UTF-8 string can hold -- a binary upload, a filename with a null byte in it -- and the honest place for those is an encoding field this contract does not have' (src/redkraken/_launch.py:1792-1807). A ZIP carries arbitrary CRC and compressed bytes, so it cannot survive. The mined row hedged this as a precondition; it is a block. The SAME block kills every OOXML/DOCX/XLSX repack reading and the zip:// and phar:// upload arms other shards filed under structured-injection and deserialization, so one capability ticket unblocks a whole family.

preconditions: file_parameter, path_valued_parameter, state_changing_method, and a served upload directory whose stored path is predictable from the submitted name. Approval on the Task. The uploads are a target_state precondition of the Test, not steps inside it.
baseline: Upload inert bytes as rkprobe.<expected extension>; GET the expected served path -- it answers. That fixes the naming scheme the writer uses.
variant: Upload the identical bytes under a name whose validated component and whose stored component differ: rkprobe.php. (trailing dot), 'rkprobe.php ' (trailing space), rkprobe.php.<expected> and rkprobe.<expected>.php (doubled, both orders), rkprobe.php:x (NTFS alternate data stream colon), rkprobe.pHp (case). Then GET BOTH the name as submitted and the name as truncated. The truncated path answering is the disagreement.
control: Upload rkprobe.php plainly -- it must be REJECTED. If it is accepted there is no extension check for the two parsers to disagree about and the reading is unnecessary. Second control: the same separator inserted where it cannot truncate (rkpr.obe.<expected>), which must be stored and served under the submitted name -- that is what shows the divergence follows the POSITION of the separator and not its mere presence.
payload_family: filename separators that one parser consumes and another does not -- trailing dot, trailing space, doubled extension in both orders, ADS colon, case
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay for the retrieval pair (a status_differs assertion naming the truncated-path GET). src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal for an agent-filed error_detail from the rejection Receipt where the refusal names the parsed component ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:227).
supported_evidence: response_differential (role=variant) between the GET of the truncated path and the GET of the submitted path, against response_invariant (role=control) on the repeated baseline retrieval.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant: only the submitted name is served and the truncated path 404s, so validator and writer read the same component.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a truncated name lands with an executable extension in a served directory. COURSE OF ACTION: remove it by the route's own removal request before sending any further spelling; do not GET it a second time. SCOPE OF HALT: the route. RESUME: after a retrieval of the truncated path 404s. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, immediately -- an executable name in a served directory is the one outcome of this row that is a live risk. WHAT IS RECORDED: both names, both served paths, the removal request and its answer.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: REACHES A FINDING: the whole differential is in the request line (the GET of the truncated path against the GET of the submitted path -- two different paths), which is exactly what a Test action carries -- a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224) -- so close_test_replay settles the Test, writes the testing -> supported transition and rk2_finding_refusal's precondition exists. The upload that creates the disagreement is a body and is therefore a target_state precondition performed in the ordinary lane before the Test opens (TEST_PRECONDITION_KINDS, src/redkraken/roster.py:396-402), not a setup request: a setup request carries only method and url (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:332-346). One further spelling constraint the Test lane adds: neither retrieval url may carry a '.' or '..' path segment or a '%2e' anywhere, because rk2_test_request_problem refuses both (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:222-226) -- the truncated-name spellings here (trailing dot, doubled extension, ADS colon) are fine, a traversal spelling would not be. HIGH VALUE: this emits injection.parser_differential, one of the nine property classes that exist in the vocabulary and that no Playbook emits. Three shards filed it under three slugs (file-upload, NEW:parameter-parser-differential, and a name-census row); it is one reading. One correction to every source that names %00: a literal NUL is NOT reliably expressible -- _body() encodes the model's string as UTF-8 and its own docstring names 'a filename with a null byte in it' as the class the contract forbids (src/redkraken/_launch.py:1792-1807). technique: The name a caller chose, not the bytes, decides how the server later describes the stored object -- identical bytes stored under two names that differ only in extension come back with different content types, dispositions or handlers.

preconditions: file_parameter, path_valued_parameter, state_changing_method. A retrieval route exists for stored objects -- an upload route with no retrieval is not readable by this Playbook. The Task carries an approval, because bb:risk is approval_required and bb:effects is mutates_object. The two stored objects are a target_state precondition of the Test, not steps inside it.
baseline: Store one object: ASCII bytes rk-probe-<task> under a name ending in the extension the route is for. Retrieve it, then retrieve it again. Record status, content type, disposition and length on both.
variant: Store the SAME bytes under a name ending in an extension a browser treats as a document (.html, .svg, .xhtml) and retrieve it; store the same bytes again under an extension a browser treats as inert (.txt) and retrieve that. compare_responses over the two retrievals -- it differences exactly two Artifacts (ticket 109), so this is one pairwise call and never a three-way.
control: The two control retrievals of step 3 differenced against each other, which must be invariant. That is the two-identical-sends control the differential needs: a store that returns a signed URL, a fresh id or a varying cache header is not byte-stable, and body_differs would fire on the Date header alone. Second control, in the upload responses: both arms must have been ACCEPTED and each retrieval must return the stored bytes -- an arm refused at store time is a control working, not this Hypothesis.
payload_family: one filename extension, varied while the bytes are held byte-identical
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay. The two arm retrievals are Test actions and a body_differs or status_differs assertion naming the variant retrieval makes its Observation a response_differential; the control retrieval that no such assertion names becomes a response_invariant. Both kinds take {receipt} provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:219-222) and every retrieval is a Receipt.
supported_evidence: response_differential (role=variant) over the two arm retrievals, plus response_invariant (role=control) over the two control retrievals -- which is exactly the Playbook's declared bb:evidence bar and the one row in this group where the shipped bar and close_test_replay agree without an agent-filed edge. Optionally a header_policy_observed filed by the agent from the same Receipt ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:235) naming the served Content-Type, since WIRE_RESPONSE_HEADERS strips only set-cookie and www-authenticate (proxy.py:376) and Content-Type does come back (ticket 94).
refuted_evidence: response_invariant over the two arm retrievals: same status, same content type, same disposition -- a route that stores under its own name and serves everything opaquely.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a removal request for any of the three stored objects returns a non-2xx, or a retrieval after removal still returns the bytes. COURSE OF ACTION: store nothing further -- explicitly do not store a fourth object to work around the third -- and stop the reading. SCOPE OF HALT: the route. RESUME: an operator confirms the objects are gone or accepts them as left behind. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, by name, with the three storage names carrying the rk-probe marker. WHAT IS RECORDED: the three names, the three retrieval URLs, the removal requests sent and each removal response.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: REACHES A FINDING: the whole differential is in the request line (two retrieval GETs at two different paths), which is exactly what a Test action carries -- a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224) -- so close_test_replay settles the Test, writes the testing -> supported transition and rk2_finding_refusal's precondition exists. The two stores are NOT Test actions -- a multipart upload is a request body and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224). They are performed in the ordinary egress lane before the Test opens and stated as a target_state precondition (TEST_PRECONDITION_KINDS, src/redkraken/roster.py:396-402); the Task is body-bearing because file-upload declares bb:effects: mutates_object, so _body_allowed returns any(one.effects != 'read_only' for one in selected) (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646-3667), the answer is written into tool_runs.args when the Tool run opens, and authorize_egress_request then refuses a body the run was not opened for, the door filing a blocked Receipt (src/redkraken/migrations/20260924T000000Z__a_request_may_carry_a_body.sql:19-28). This is the Playbook's own reading and the mandatory floor row. It is also the one file-upload row that needs no agent-filed Observation: the declared bar asks for response_invariant and response_differential and close_test_replay writes both. Every other file-upload row below needs promote_proposal for at least one edge.

baseline: Upload a document whose ASCII signature sits at byte 0 -- accepted.
variant: Upload the identical document with the signature at byte 1000, then at byte 2000, then at byte 8000, padding with ASCII spaces. The offset at which acceptance flips names the sniffing window and is a quotable fact about the stack.
control: A document of the same length with no signature anywhere, which must be rejected -- that rules out 'the route accepts everything of this size'. Plus the baseline sent twice and differenced, invariant, so the acceptance answer is not carrying a per-upload id.
payload_family: an ASCII file signature placed at a chosen byte offset inside otherwise inert padding

An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. HIGH VALUE: injection.parser_differential, one of the nine unemitted classes, and it produces a measured number without ever uploading anything executable. Two honest bounds the mined row got half right. (1) 65536 bytes brackets libmagic's common 1024-byte window; file(1)'s 1048576-byte window is beyond the body ceiling and must be recorded as out of reach, not asserted. preconditions: file_parameter, state_changing_method. An upload route the Task's Identity may call. Approval on the Task, since each arm stores an object; the arms here are refused ones on a working guard, so the count of objects that survive is usually zero.
baseline: Upload inert ASCII bytes under rkprobe.<the extension the route is for> -- must be accepted, which is what says the route works at all.
variant: Upload the identical bytes under rkprobe.rkxyz, an extension that is neither on any dangerous list nor one the route expects. An allow-list REFUSES it; a deny-list ACCEPTS it. One request answers whether walking an extension wordlist is worth a single further request.
control: Send the baseline upload twice and difference the two upload responses -- they must be invariant. An upload endpoint that returns a fresh object id, a signed URL or a timestamp per call has no invariant to measure the variant against, and status_differs alone would then be reading the id. Second control: the variant upload repeated once, so a one-off 500 is not read as an allow-list refusal.
payload_family: one neutral, non-dangerous, non-expected filename extension
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487, INSERT INTO observations at :1116), filing response_differential from the neutral-extension upload's Receipt and response_invariant from the repeated baseline's, both {receipt} provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:219-222). NOT close_test_replay: the arms differ only in a multipart body and a Test action carries no body.
supported_evidence: response_differential (role=variant), AGENT-FILED, between the neutral-extension upload and the expected-extension upload, against an agent-filed response_invariant (role=control) on the repeated baseline. Plus error_detail from the refusing Receipt where the message names the list ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:227-228).
refuted_evidence: response_invariant between the neutral-extension upload and the expected-extension upload: the guard accepted both, so it is a deny-list and the finding is which names are on it, not that a list exists.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): any arm is accepted and the object cannot be removed by the route's own removal request. COURSE OF ACTION: stop uploading; do not try a second removal path. SCOPE OF HALT: the route. RESUME: operator confirms removal. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, with the stored names. WHAT IS RECORDED: names, retrieval URLs, removal attempts and their answers.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING: the differential lives in a request body: both arms are multipart uploads and the only thing that varies is the filename inside the part header., and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so it is not expressible as a Test action. close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), the Observation kind it writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1072), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:643-649; findings.opened_by_test_run_id at :85). An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. The source walks an eleven-name wordlist (php, php5, phtml, phar, pHp, asp, aspx, cer, shtml ...) where one request answers the question. The control -- an extension that is neither dangerous nor expected -- is the entire value of the row and it is what the wordlist pages leave out. The shipped Playbook does not ask this question at all; it asks what the retrieval says, which is a later question that only matters once the guard's shape is known.
finding_path_note: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states

technique: Which of three signals the store-time guard actually reads -- the filename extension, the declared part Content-Type, or the leading bytes -- separated by holding two of the three constant across pairwise arms.

preconditions: file_parameter, multipart_request, state_changing_method. An upload route that rejects at least one shape, so there is something for a signal to flip. The multipart document including its own boundary is spelled by the model inside the body string (roster.py:1820, a string 0..65536 deliberately, so the model spells its own encoding); there is no Content-Length argument and the door re-measures (src/redkraken/proxy.py:2898).
baseline: Multipart POST: inert ASCII bytes beginning GIF89a, part filename rkprobe.gif, part Content-Type image/gif. The accepted shape.
variant: Two arms, sent and differenced pairwise because compare_responses differences exactly two Artifacts (ticket 109). Arm 1: identical bytes, identical filename, part Content-Type changed to application/x-php. Arm 2: identical bytes, part Content-Type left image/gif, filename changed to rkprobe.php. Whichever arm flips the store answer names the signal the guard reads.
control: The baseline upload sent twice and differenced -- must be invariant, or the upload response carries an id or a timestamp and no arm difference is attributable. Second control: bytes, filename and declared type all plainly disallowed at once, which must be refused; without it an acceptance in either arm could just be a route that accepts everything.
payload_family: the three store-time signals -- extension, declared part Content-Type, leading ASCII magic -- varied one at a time
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal (live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487, INSERT at :1116), filing response_differential from whichever arm flipped and response_invariant from the repeated baseline, both {receipt}. NOT close_test_replay.
supported_evidence: response_differential (role=variant), AGENT-FILED, on the arm that flipped, against an agent-filed response_invariant (role=control) on the repeated baseline.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant on both arms against the baseline: the guard reads none of the three at store time and the reading moves to what the retrieval says (the core row above).
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): an arm carrying an executable-family extension is ACCEPTED and stored. COURSE OF ACTION: send the removal request for that object immediately and send no further arm. SCOPE OF HALT: the route. RESUME: after removal is confirmed by a retrieval that 404s. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, at once, because an accepted .php name in a served directory is a standing risk even with inert bytes. WHAT IS RECORDED: the accepted name, the retrieval URL, the removal request and its answer, and the bytes sent (which carry no code).
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING: the differential lives in a request body: all three signals -- the filename in the part header, the declared part Content-Type and the leading bytes -- live inside the multipart document., and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so it is not expressible as a Test action. close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), the Observation kind it writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1072), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:643-649; findings.opened_by_test_run_id at :85). An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. Four mining shards filed this as four rows; it is one reading with two pairwise arms. Every source version puts a live web shell in the bytes and the reading survives without one: what is asked is which of three signals the validator believes, and inert ASCII answers it. The polyglot half (a document that is a valid image and a valid script at once) stays refused by the Playbook's own step 8 and by references/file-upload.md, and it is also not expressible -- see the archive row for why.

preconditions: tech_sql, state_changing_method, and a sink that stacks statements plus pg_write_server_files or superuser. The stacking question is itself a reachable probe and belongs to sql-injection.
baseline: Would be: the served path absent.
variant: Would be: the served path present after the write.
control: Would be: the same write aimed at a path the server cannot reach, which must fail. Not taken.
payload_family: a stacked statement that exports table or large-object content to a filesystem path
runtime_writer: not applicable -- the reading is not taken.
supported_evidence: none filed.
refuted_evidence: none filed.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a run proposes any payload that writes to the target's filesystem. COURSE OF ACTION: refuse it, and refuse it separately from the file-READ primitive that shares its permission model, so a later reading cannot inherit the read's disposition for a write. SCOPE OF HALT: the class, every run. RESUME: never under a read_only Playbook. WHO IS TOLD: nobody at run time. WHAT IS RECORDED: the refusal, its reason, and the fact that it is filed apart from the read.
owner_ticket: none -- refused by standing decision, so no ticket unblocks it; re-opening it is an operator and Program decision, not a capability gap
notes: Carried here only because a miner filed it under file-upload; the primitive is sql-injection's (group g03) and the class is not injection.stored_file. Kept rather than dropped so the refusal is not lost between two groups. The reason is the sharper form the source itself invites: a file written into a served directory is a backdoor on somebody's production host, and even removed immediately it existed, and for that window anybody who found it had the access it granted. The 'proof.txt' framing in the source is the tell -- the harmlessness is entirely a property of what the payload chose to write.

technique: A genuine, unmodified token is honoured somewhere it never claimed to be valid -- a second audience, a second application sharing the issuer, or a route whose recorded surface requires a scope the token does not carry.
