preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, tech_jwt. TWO SPELLINGS, and they do not reach the same place. (a) FINDING SPELLING: the token is the static Authorization header of an Identity the Task leased, so identity.Session.inject puts it on every request in the run (src/redkraken/identity.py:329-339, called at src/redkraken/proxy.py:2954) and the only thing that varies between actions is the URL. (b) OBSERVATION SPELLING: the token was issued to a route this run drove from a Task with NO leased Identity and is presented as a caller-written Authorization header. That spelling is needed for any row that EDITS the token, and it can never be a Test action, because a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224). Session.inject also drops every caller-set header the Identity owns, so the two spellings cannot be mixed on one Task.
baseline: One authenticated read at the endpoint the token WAS issued for, token as issued. Store the answer. Then send it again unchanged and store that too -- two identical sends, because a resource response carrying a request id or a rate-limit counter has no invariant for the variant to be measured against.
variant: The identical token, byte for byte, sent to a second endpoint of the same application whose recorded surface says it needs a different scope; and separately to a second application in the Program's scope that shares the issuer where aud names only the first. One endpoint per request. Under spelling (a) this is a bare change of url.
control: Under spelling (a): a third URL on the same application that this Identity is known to be refused at -- an administrative route, or a route belonging to another tenant. It must answer as refused. That is what rules out 'this Identity is answered everywhere', which is the boring explanation for the variant. Under spelling (b) the sharper control is available -- the same token with the last character of the signature changed, which must be refused, saying the endpoint verifies the signature at all -- but it is a crafted header and so is not a Test action.
payload_family: one unmodified issued token, presented at an audience or scope it does not name
runtime_writer: TWO writers, and the Playbook's bar needs both. src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay closes the Test and writes response_differential / response_invariant, which is what a Finding needs (findings.opened_by_test_run_id, 20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:85). src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal writes the credential_effect the bb:evidence bar actually asks for, with {receipt} provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:231), inserting the observations row with the kind the agent named (20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:1116).
supported_evidence: Under spelling (a): response_differential (role=variant) from close_test_replay between the second-audience GET and the issued-for GET, with response_invariant (role=control) on the refused route; PLUS an agent-filed credential_effect from each of those Receipts ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:231-232), which is the kind the Playbook's own bb:evidence bar names on both supporting roles. Under spelling (b) only the agent-filed credential_effect pair is available.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, which is what bb:evidence declares for the refuted arm and which close_test_replay writes directly: every variant is answered the way the broken signature is.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): a variant is accepted and the response body carries a principal that is not this run's own -- another tenant's records, another subject's profile. COURSE OF ACTION: stop at the acceptance, send no further variant to that endpoint, and quote no claim value or record field into the Hypothesis. SCOPE OF HALT: the endpoint. RESUME: an operator decision -- the reading has crossed into authorization.tenant_isolation, which is a different Playbook and a different ceiling. WHO IS TOLD: the operator, immediately. WHAT IS RECORDED: the endpoint, the status, the fact that foreign data was returned and its size; never the claim values and never the data.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. REACHES A FINDING: the whole differential is in the request line (which URL the same held credential is presented at, plus which Identity the Task holds), which is exactly what a Test action carries -- a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224) -- so close_test_replay settles the Test, writes the testing -> supported transition and rk2_finding_refusal's precondition exists. That holds ONLY for the unmodified-token spelling (a) above. Every jwt-jose row below edits the token, which means a caller-written Authorization header, which means STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING: the differential lives in a request header, and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so it is not expressible as a Test action. close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), the Observation kind it writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1072), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:643-649; findings.opened_by_test_run_id at :85). An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding.  This is the Playbook's own reading and the mandatory floor row, and it is where this Playbook's corpus defect lives. bb:evidence asks for credential_effect on BOTH the control and the variant role to reach supported. close_test_replay writes only response_invariant and response_differential (ticket 166), so the supported bar CANNOT be met from the Test lane at all -- it needs an agent-filed credential_effect from promote_proposal. The shipped prose never says that, which is exactly the 'names a kind without saying which step produces it' defect. The rewrite must say: the Test closes on status_differs and the agent files credential_effect from the same Receipts as the two supporting edges. MINED_FROM is empty (D7): this row is the group's own reading, taken from the shipped playbook.md rather than from any of the 665 mined rows.
finding_path_note: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states

technique: A token past its own exp is still honoured, read opportunistically on a token that aged naturally rather than by waiting for one to.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, tech_jwt, and -- the load-bearing one -- a token this run has held long enough to pass its own exp. This is opportunistic: the reading is taken when a run has aged a token, never manufactured by waiting, and a run that has not aged one records the reading as not applicable rather than as refuted.
baseline: The same token used successfully earlier in the run, with its recorded successful answer as the stored comparison point. Two sends of the current answer, invariant, before anything is concluded.
variant: The identical token replayed after its stated exp has passed. An authenticated answer means the lifetime claim is not read.
control: The same token with its signature corrupted, replayed at the same moment. It must be refused -- otherwise the endpoint is answering everything and the acceptance is not about exp. Second control: a freshly issued token sent at the same moment, which must be accepted, so a rejection of the aged token is about age and not about an endpoint that has started refusing everyone.
payload_family: an unmodified issued token replayed past its stated lifetime
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 -> promote_proposal, live definition 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the INSERT INTO observations at :1116, filing the credential_effect the Playbook's bar names ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:231-232) and, where the messages differ, error_detail ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:227-228). NOT close_test_replay: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 cannot be reached by this reading at all, because a crafted Authorization header is not expressible as a Test action.
supported_evidence: credential_effect (role=variant) from the expired-token Receipt and credential_effect (role=control) from the corrupted-signature Receipt, both agent-filed.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant: the expired token is answered the way the corrupted one is, which is the system working and is not a finding.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): the run is about to sleep or to loop in order to age a token. COURSE OF ACTION: do not -- record the reading as not applicable for this run. SCOPE OF HALT: this reading. RESUME: a later run that happens to hold an aged token. WHO IS TOLD: nobody. WHAT IS RECORDED: that the reading was not applicable and why, so it is not read as a refutation.
owner_ticket: n/a -- reachable, and nothing is owed
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the ceiling is timing, which ticket 211 does not touch. The ceiling paragraph below still holds. STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING: the differential lives in a request header: the aged token rides in the Authorization value, and the variable is elapsed TIME, which a single Test run cannot span in any case., and a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224), so it is not expressible as a Test action. close_test_replay is the ONLY writer of a testing -> supported hypothesis_transitions row (src/redkraken/migrations/20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), the Observation kind it writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and from nothing else (:1063-1072), and rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without exactly that row joined through test_run_receipts to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:643-649; findings.opened_by_test_run_id at :85). An agent-filed Observation lands in hypothesis_evidence as a real edge and is never filtered out (rk2_promote_hypotheses, 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. The reading is still performable through the ordinary mcp__rk2__http_request lane and its Observation is real evidence on the Hypothesis; it stops one step short of a Finding. Overlaps identity-lifecycle (group g03), whose class is session_handling.lifetime and whose reading is 'is this token single-use and is exp enforced'. The difference that keeps this row here: this Playbook's step 3 lists exp among the things a token was issued FOR, so an expired token honoured is a token honoured beyond its issuance -- authorization.token_scope. The replay-twice arm from the same source is identity-lifecycle's, not this one's, and should not be folded in.
finding_path_note: the ceiling is timing, which ticket 211 does not touch

technique: An unsigned token is accepted -- alg set to none with an empty signature -- against a control that shows a corrupted signature being refused.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, tech_jwt, no leased Identity owning Authorization for this origin, and a token belonging to this run's own subject. Costs nothing to compute: base64url only, no key material.
baseline: The valid token unmodified -- the authenticated answer, sent twice and invariant.
variant: The same claims with alg set to none and an empty signature segment. An authenticated answer means unsigned tokens are accepted.
control: The ORIGINAL token with its signature corrupted, which must be rejected. If a corrupted signature is also accepted then nothing is verified and 'alg none works' is the weaker of two findings. This control is what stops the row from reporting a verification failure as an algorithm failure.
payload_family: alg none with an emptied signature segment

That is the whole design -- a route returning 400 for any nested object is validating its schema and returns 400 for both arms; a route answering one way for the operator and another for the plain nested key has interpreted the operator. Comparing an object against the original STRING would compare two shapes, and every serialiser, validator and logger in the path treats those differently. The route must not be an authentication route.
baseline: GET the route with the field as a plain scalar carrying a value that must not match -- for example a reset-token endpoint with a wrong token. Record the invalid answer. Send it twice; invariant.
variant: The same request with the field spelled in the parser's bracket syntax so it arrives as an object: field[not]=<the same wrong value>. A valid-token answer where an equality could never have matched means the parser built an operator object and nothing type-checked it.
control: The same bracket syntax on a field name the handler does not use -- fieldX[not]=<value> -- which must return the invalid answer. That rules out 'any bracketed parameter is accepted' and 'the parser rejects brackets outright', which are the two boring explanations for the same difference.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, query_parameter, tech_orm, tech_sql, and -- load-bearing -- a MySQL or MariaDB backend where regexp_time_limit is enforced (about 32ms by default) and the timeout surfaces as a 500. Without an enforced limit the pattern runs unbounded and the reading is refused, not merely inconclusive.
baseline: GET with the regex lookup carrying an anchored lookahead on a character the value cannot start with, followed by the nested wildcards -> 200 with an empty list. Sent twice, invariant.
variant: The identical pattern with the lookahead anchored on the guessed character -> 500, because the prefix matched and the backtracking ran into the limit.
control: GET with a plain anchored prefix and no wildcards at all -> 200 non-empty. That proves the field and the lookup exist and that the 500 came from backtracking rather than from a rejected filter name. Without it a 500 reads as 'the ORM refused the parameter'.
payload_family: an anchored lookahead followed by nested wildcards, in a regex lookup on a filter parameter
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 -> close_test_replay: the observation is a STATUS CODE, so a status_differs assertion naming the matching-character action makes it a response_differential.
supported_evidence: response_differential (role=variant, status_differs) between the matching and non-matching lookahead, against response_invariant (role=control) on the repeated baseline.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant: both patterns answer 200, so either the regex never reaches the database or no time limit is enforced -- and the second of those is a halt, not a refutation.
stop_conditions: HALT TRIGGER (observed): two probe characters and the control have been sent, OR a 500 arrives without the control having returned 200 non-empty. COURSE OF ACTION: stop. A catastrophic pattern is real load on the target and the second condition means the load is unbounded because no time limit is enforced. SCOPE OF HALT: the endpoint on the first condition; the whole run on the second. RESUME: never sweep an alphabet. WHO IS TOLD: the operator on the second condition, immediately, because unbounded backtracking on a shared database is a DoS with better manners. WHAT IS RECORDED: the two patterns, the two statuses, the control's answer, and the backend's regex limit if the banner names it.

notes: REACHES A FINDING: the whole differential is in the request line (the query string -- one regex pattern in a filter parameter, settled on the STATUS code), which is exactly what a Test action carries -- a Test action carries exactly the keys ordinal, role, kind, method and url (rk2_test_spec_problem, src/redkraken/migrations/20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:377), a setup or cleanup request carries only method and url (:332-346), and _Door.send hands proxy.spend the url and the method and nothing else -- no headers=, no body= -- although proxy.spend accepts both (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351, src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4224) -- so close_test_replay settles the Test, writes the testing -> supported transition and rk2_finding_refusal's precondition exists. The cleanest example in the whole group of re-casting a timing mechanism into a status observation, and it is worth stating as a general Playbook-writing rule rather than as one row's trick. Two corrections to the mining note. (1) It justifies itself with 'this does NOT need the writer-less timing_differential kind' -- timing_differential is not writer-less: promote_proposal writes it with {receipt} provenance and Receipts carry ts_arrival, ts_egress and waited_ms (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:56-58). The status framing is still the better one, but for evidence STRENGTH, not for availability. (2) The enforced regex time limit is a hard precondition, not colour: without it this is the XPath nested-count reading another shard correctly refused, and it must be refused here too.

preconditions: bb:triggers_all api_surface + multiple_test_identities, plus a working lease on one Identity label (Test precondition kind `identity_leased`, roster.py:396-401). The count is written down before the first request; twelve is the Playbook's default. bb:risk is approval_required, so the Program grant is a precondition and not a step. If the route only answers a POST, the Tool run must be opened body-bearing, and today it cannot be: `_body_allowed` (execution.py:3667) is `any(one.effects != "read_only" ...)`, this Playbook ships `bb:effects: read_only`, and authorize_egress_request (20260924T000000Z__a_request_may_carry_a_body.sql:256-262) raises 'egress body does not match authorized tool run'.
baseline: Request #1 through mcp__rk2__http_request, read to confirm the answer is the authenticated one and not a login redirect or an anonymous view of the same route. This is the Playbook's step 2 and the Receipt every later comparison is held against.
variant: Requests #2..#N, byte-identical, same Task, same Identity. One variable moves: how many have been sent. Stop early on the first answer that differs.
control: Two legs, and neither is optional. (a) Send the baseline request TWICE back to back before the sequence opens and compare the two stored Artifacts: the response Artifact is the whole message/http exchange (proxy.transcript, proxy.py:878-887), so a Date, a request-id or an ETag makes body_differs true between two identical sends. Whatever differs between those two is the noise floor and no later body_differs below it is a reading. (b) Read the layer the application answers at, not the status line: a SOAP Fault and a GraphQL errors array both arrive as 200, so a run of Faults is invariant while every request failed (api-soap.md section 3). On a credential-verification route add the third leg pkb-checklist names: one malformed value that must produce a DIFFERENT answer, proving the endpoint discriminates inputs at all and the sameness is not a blanket response.
payload_family: repetition count. Nothing in the request varies; the only value that changes across the sequence is the ordinal.
runtime_writer: close_test_replay -- 20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1072, kind derived :1063-1070 from the specification: an action a status_differs/body_differs assertion names as `action` or `against` becomes response_differential, every other action becomes response_invariant. The control's credential_effect leg is agent-filed: promote_proposal -- 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:1116 (definition :487) inserts an observations row with the kind the AGENT named, gated only by enforce_kind_provenance over 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236 with provenance `receipt` from the step-2 Receipt, attached by rk2_promote_hypotheses -- 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530, which writes hypothesis_evidence from an agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind.

notes: FINDING PATH -- the two arms differ only in the request line, so a Test specification can carry both as actions ({ordinal, role, kind, method, url}, roster.py:1186-1198), `close_test_replay` derives the transition from the Test's own assertions (20260816T000000Z...:1064-1074 for the kind, :1125 for the transition) and a Finding can open. One constraint travels with it: `rk2_test_request_problem` (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:216-226) refuses any `.` or `..` segment in the PATH and any `%2e` anywhere in the url, so neither arm may be spelled with one; the door itself would forward them verbatim (origin_form, proxy.py:818-828), so this is the Test lane's rule and not the wire's. One more constraint the query carrier has to carry: `record_test_action` compares a Receipt to the action it is recorded as over the method, the scheme, the host, the port and the PATH, and deliberately not the query (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1382-1391, 'The query is not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns'). The query IS sent -- `_Door.send` hands `proxy.spend` the specification's url whole -- so the differential is real; but two actions differing ONLY in their query are indistinguishable to that anti-swap guard, so a specification should differ in a path segment too wherever the route allows one. Here the two arms are BYTE-IDENTICAL requests and the only thing that moves is how many have been sent, so the whole differential is an ordinal in the specification's `actions` array and the Test lane carries it natively. This is the one api reading that reaches a Finding with nothing conditional about it. The Playbook's own claim, and the one row here whose evidence the replay lane can write end to end. It is also one of the few readings in the corpus whose finding is an INVARIANCE, which is the direction ticket 166's wall happens to favour. The api-soap.md control leg is load-bearing and easy to lose: without it a run of SOAP Faults or GraphQL error bodies grades as 'nothing is counting' when every request failed.

technique: Ask whether the counter is keyed on the route AS THE CALLER SPELLED IT rather than on the identity, by driving the same sequence twice where the only thing that moves between runs is a request-line spelling of the same resource -- a trailing slash, an added junk query parameter, a case change in a path segment -- and reading whether the limit engages at the same ordinal.

baseline: N identical requests to one exact spelling of the route under one leased Identity, driven until the limit engages. Record the ordinal it engaged at; that ordinal is the reading's whole measurement.
variant: The same N under the SAME Identity where each request restates the route differently and equivalently: `/x`, `/x/`, `/x?cb=1`, `/x?cb=2`. technique: The failed-authentication counter is keyed to the account rather than to the caller, so the same budget spread across accounts is never counted.
preconditions: api_surface AND unauthenticated_endpoint AND email_valued_parameter; at least three identifiers the Program NAMES as existing, and a declared count K+2 taken from the application's own stated policy or found by stepping the first series. The Task's Identity is fixed for the whole run (tickets 97 and 131), which is exactly what makes 'the caller' one origin and the question answerable.
baseline: K+2 failed attempts against ONE named account. Record the ordinal at which the answer changes -- 429, captcha, 'account locked'. Two identical sends open the sequence.
variant: The same K+2 failed attempts, one each across K+2 different named accounts. Does the answer stay the ordinary refusal at the last attempt?
control: Two identical sends of the baseline, first and last, whose stored Artifacts must hash alike. body_differs compares response_agent_sha (20260815T000000Z...:1503-1506) and that sha covers the whole message -- status line, headers and body (proxy.py:878 transcript, proxy.py:3088) -- so a Date header alone makes any two sends differ. A route that is not byte-stable across the pair is not a route this reading can difference, and the verdict is inconclusive. Then K+2 requests from the same caller that carry a VALID credential, or K+2 GETs of a cheap authenticated page. If those throttle too, the limiter is a generic per-origin rate limit and says nothing about the auth counter; if they do not, the counter is keyed to the account and the spread series walked past it.
payload_family: one common wrong credential against many identifiers, against many wrong credentials against one identifier

SO THE PLAYBOOK PROSE MUST NOT BE WRITTEN TWICE: 00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:31-33 records the ordering this repo already chose -- 'This is why the order is harness first. Adding state-of-the-art techniques to steps that cannot be executed would multiply the unrunnable part of the catalogue' -- and 211 says in as many words that writing 'this step stops at an Observation' into a third of the corpus would be 'a catalogue that describes attacks it cannot grade'. preconditions: api_surface AND state_changing_method; the same hard precondition as the row above -- the baseline must reach a refusal -- plus an account the operator owns, because the sequence is spent against it.
baseline: N attempts with a byte-identical request line until one is refused. Record the ordinal k. Two identical sends open the sequence.
variant: k attempts where ONLY the decoration changes: a trailing slash, one fresh junk query parameter per attempt, a case change in the path. No refusal at k means the counter key includes bytes the application throws away.
control: Two identical sends of the baseline, first and last, whose stored Artifacts must hash alike. body_differs compares response_agent_sha (20260815T000000Z...:1503-1506) and that sha covers the whole message -- status line, headers and body (proxy.py:878 transcript, proxy.py:3088) -- so a Date header alone makes any two sends differ. A route that is not byte-stable across the pair is not a route this reading can difference, and the verdict is inconclusive. Then k attempts with the decoration held CONSTANT -- the same trailing slash every time. It must still refuse at k. Without it the variant cannot be told from a window that expired, or from a decorated path that is unlimited for an unrelated reason.
payload_family: the same request under spellings the application resolves to one route: trailing slash, case, one throwaway query parameter
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 calls close_test_replay, which derives the Observation kind from the Test SPECIFICATION: an action any status_differs/body_differs assertion names becomes response_differential, any other action becomes response_invariant. The variant is named by a status_differs assertion against the constant-decoration control, so its Observation is response_differential.
supported_evidence: response_differential, role variant: spec asserts status_differs(kth decorated, against=kth constant-decoration control).
refuted_evidence: response_invariant, role variant: the decorated run refuses at k as the constant one does -- the key is the caller and the claim is refuted.
stop_conditions: halt trigger (observed condition): the decorated spelling answers a different route, or a 404 | course of action: stop; the two arms are no longer the same request and the sequence is not comparable | scope of halt: the route | resume condition: a later run with a decoration the route demonstrably resolves to the same handler | who is told: the operator, through mcp__rk2__park_for_human, with the halt trigger quoted verbatim | what is recorded: the Receipt label of every arm sent before the halt, which arm triggered it, and the verdict inconclusive carrying the trigger as its stated reason

stop_conditions: 1 HALT TRIGGER (observed condition): the inventory is empty, or the DOM after the dispatch is identical to the DOM before it | 2 COURSE OF ACTION: stop and report; on an empty inventory the reading ends before send_message is even admissible, and on an identical DOM the report is 'dispatched, and here is the DOM before and after' and nothing more | 3 SCOPE OF HALT: this document for this run | 4 RESUME CONDITION: a different document that the same Surface says registers a listener | 5 WHO IS TOLD: the Task result via mcp__rk2__submit_mission_result; the operator via mcp__rk2__park_for_human when the halt is wider than this route | 6 WHAT IS RECORDED: the client_state Artifact hash, the listener count and script positions, the two DOM Artifact hashes, the js_parse output, and the dispatch outcome as `dispatched` -- never as `matched`

The browse-run Observation is a real evidence edge -- `rk2_promote_hypotheses` (20261025T000000Z...:530) filters on nothing -- but an edge is not a transition. It is stated here because a reader comparing this row to a request-lane row would otherwise expect the same ceiling. What the step got RIGHT and must keep is the boundary -- send_message reports `dispatched`, not `matched`, deliberately, because postMessage has no handler result, so a step may never claim a listener accepted the body. baseline: The route with an ordinary value, stored as the Artifact everything else is compared against.
variant: The same value followed by a separator and a harmless command that prints something stable. Many converters echo the command line or its error into the response body, and a route that does answers the question in one request.
control: The same characters in a position where they cannot separate -- inside a quoted region, or with the separator replaced by an inert byte of equal length -- which distinguishes a shell from an echo. FINDING PATH -- the two arms differ only in the request line, so a Test specification can carry both as actions ({ordinal, role, kind, method, url}, roster.py:1186-1198), `close_test_replay` derives the transition from the Test's own assertions (20260816T000000Z...:1064-1074 for the kind, :1125 for the transition) and a Finding can open. One constraint travels with it: `rk2_test_request_problem` (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:216-226) refuses any `.` or `..` segment in the PATH and any `%2e` anywhere in the url, so neither arm may be spelled with one; the door itself would forward them verbatim (origin_form, proxy.py:818-828), so this is the Test lane's rule and not the wire's. One more constraint the query carrier has to carry: `record_test_action` compares a Receipt to the action it is recorded as over the method, the scheme, the host, the port and the PATH, and deliberately not the query (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1382-1391, 'The query is not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt, over a normalisation the door owns'). The query IS sent -- `_Door.send` hands `proxy.spend` the specification's url whole -- so the differential is real; but two actions differing ONLY in their query are indistinguishable to that anti-swap guard, so a specification should differ in a path segment too wherever the route allows one. This differential cannot be spelled as a Test: `_Door.send` (src/redkraken/replay.py:341-351) hands `proxy.spend` a url and a method and nothing else -- no `headers=`, no `body=`, though `proxy.spend` (proxy.py:4216-4227) accepts both -- and a Test action element is exactly {ordinal, role, kind, method, url} (roster.py:1186-1198). But an edge is not a transition, so the claim stops at an Observation. -- which is the state of the multipart-filename carrier of the same question. The Playbook's step 3 and the cheapest evidence in the class: one request, one comparison, no distribution to reason about. Worth a note for the rewrite: the shipped bb:evidence block has no response_differential row at all, so the Playbook's cheapest and most decisive outcome has no declared bar. That is a gap in the frontmatter, not in the harness.

preconditions: a declared and bound out-of-band http channel with placement=path (src/redkraken/oob.py:667-671, 791-801: a publisher serves one hostname, so the correlator rides the path), a correlator minted through mcp__rk2__mint_callback (roster.py:937), and the approval_required grant, since this still runs a process on somebody else's host. Carrier-specific precondition, and it is the one most likely to be missed: where the carrier is a JWT `kid` or any other Identity-owned header, the Task must have NO leased Identity, because identity.Session.inject (identity.py:334) replaces the caller-set cookie and every static Identity header and the crafted header never reaches the wire. the Tool run must be opened body-bearing, and today it cannot be: `_body_allowed` (execution.py:3667) is `any(one.effects != "read_only" ...)`, this Playbook ships `bb:effects: read_only`, and authorize_egress_request (20260924T000000Z__a_request_may_carry_a_body.sql:256-262) raises 'egress body does not match authorized tool run' for a multipart or JSON carrier.
baseline: The same request with the separator replaced by an inert character of the same length, and the same correlator hostname present with no shell metacharacter at all. No arrival in the freshness window. This second form matters: an arrival here means the value was FETCHED as a URL rather than executed, which is a different finding (a key-URL or fetcher SSRF) and leaves the command claim unproved.
variant: The same request with the separator and one fetch of https://<endpoint>/<correlator>/x.txt. One arrival at the publisher, attributed to this subject, is the claim.
control: The channel's own control arrival inside the freshness window, cited beside any negative reading so that silence means the target rather than a dead tunnel. Read the correction that goes with it: a CONTROL arrival writes NO Observation -- is_control and a null subject are one state tied by a CHECK (20261001T000000Z__a_control_arrival_is_what_makes_silence_a_finding.sql:40-52) -- so the control is read for freshness and is not itself evidence, and the evidential negative is the inert-twin request producing no arrival.
payload_family: out-of-band confirmation: one separator, one fetch, no output carried. Named carriers seen in the corpus: an uploaded filename, a URL-valued parameter handed to a fetcher, a JWT kid resolved before verification, and a tool argument a model passes on verbatim.
runtime_writer: record_callback_interaction -- 20261001T000000Z__a_control_arrival_is_what_makes_silence_a_finding.sql:543, which writes an observations row of kind callback_interaction with provenance 'callback'. The kind is registered is_evidential = true with allowed_provenance {callback} (20260812T040000Z__a_callback_arrives_on_a_declared_channel.sql:349) and ticket 98's migration 20260928T040000Z__the_out_of_band_refusal_was_reversed.sql:19 calls it evidential in as many words. The edge onto the Hypothesis is written by rk2_promote_hypotheses -- 20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530, which writes hypothesis_evidence from an agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind.
supported_evidence: Neither of the two -- and that is admissible rather than a gap. The bar is callback_interaction, which is evidential and carries a supporting edge; the response_invariant that close_test_replay would write for the two http actions is the SECONDARY bar showing the responses themselves did not move, so the arrival is the only thing that changed.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant on both arms with no arrival in the window and a fresh control arrival proving the channel was alive: the value did not reach a shell that can reach the network. Note the residual ambiguity honestly -- a target with no egress produces the same silence, and that is inconclusive rather than refuted.
stop_conditions: 1 HALT TRIGGER (observed condition): one arrival correlated to this subject, or the declared freshness window closes with none | 2 COURSE OF ACTION: stop. One fetch, and no second command once the first has answered -- os-command-injection.md's own refusal, in those words | 3 SCOPE OF HALT: this endpoint for this run; a Program whose rules of engagement do not admit an out-of-band channel halts the technique Program-wide | 4 RESUME CONDITION: a fresh correlator for a different subject, under the same grant | 5 WHO IS TOLD: the operator via mcp__rk2__park_for_human (roster.py:1008); the Program via a program_halts row when the halt is Program-wide | 6 WHAT IS RECORDED: the correlator, the arrival's interaction label, channel name and byte size, the inert-twin Receipt showing no arrival, and the control arrival cited for freshness
notes: FINDING PATH, and by an unobvious route worth stating once. Where the payload rides the query or the path, BOTH arms are Test actions, and the Test that closes this claim asserts INVARIANCE: `status_equals`/`body_equals` between the arm carrying the separator-plus-fetch and the inert arm. `rk2_settle_replay` returns 'holds', `rk2_test_outcome` maps 'holds' to settles='supported' (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:108-121), `close_test_replay` writes the runtime `testing -> supported` transition (20260816T000000Z...:1125) and `rk2_finding_refusal` (20260815T120000Z...:642-649) is satisfied. The Observation that Test writes is `response_invariant` -- exactly the secondary bar this row wants -- and the arrival's own `callback_interaction` rides alongside as an evidence edge. So a blind reading whose responses do NOT move is not shut out of the Finding path; what shuts a row out is a differential the Test cannot SPELL. Where the payload rides a multipart filename instead, this row is Observation-ceilinged like its neighbour above. HIGH VALUE and structural: it converts this class's blind reading from a kind no Test can close to one that carries a bar on its own. The corpus reference ranks an out-of-band hit THIRD, behind an echo and a delay, partly because it 'puts a record of the engagement on somebody else's resolver'. That was true of a public DNS canary and is not true of an http tunnel this harness owns end to end, so the rewrite should re-derive the ranking rather than inherit it. Two limits stay: a control arrival is not evidence, and the provenance is {callback} alone, so no Receipt may be filed under this kind and the arrival cannot inherit a Receipt's weight.

technique: Ask whether an uploaded file's name is concatenated into a command line, by sending a name carrying a bounded delay beside a name carrying the same separator characters inert, interleaved, and reporting the separation between two sampled distributions rather than the duration of one request.

preconditions: bb:triggers_all file_parameter + multipart_request + state_changing_method, and the Program grant that bb:risk approval_required means: every observation this row makes runs a process on somebody else's host. BODY PERMISSION -- the Task's Playbook selection must contain at least one Playbook whose `bb:effects` is not `read_only`. `_body_allowed` (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646, return at :3667) is `any(one.effects != "read_only" for one in selected)`, and `authorize_egress_request` (20260924T000000Z__a_request_may_carry_a_body.sql:22, :256-262) files a blocked Receipt for a body otherwise. `command-directory-injection` itself ships `bb:effects: read_only`, so a Task selecting it alone can send nothing here. Thirteen of the fifty shipped Playbooks are not read_only (api-authorization, authentication, file-upload, identity-lifecycle, identity-parsing, oauth, payment-workflows, race-conditions, request-parsing, routing, spreadsheet-injection, webauthn, webhooks), so the precondition is satisfiable today and is stated here as a precondition rather than softened away. In practice the co-selection is the ordinary case rather than a contrivance: `file-upload` ships `bb:effects: mutates_object` and `bb:triggers_all: ["file_parameter", "path_valued_parameter", "state_changing_method"]`, so it triggers on the same surface facts this Playbook does and a Task that selects one usually selects both.
baseline: Several uploads of a small valid file with an ordinary name, sent through mcp__rk2__http_request as whichever Identity the Task was opened under. This measures two things: that the route works and what it answers, and how long it takes and how much that varies -- because a timing claim against an unmeasured distribution is one sample with an opinion attached.
variant: The ordinary name with a separator and a bounded delay appended, five rounds.
control: The same name, same length, same separator characters, with the delay replaced by a command that does nothing -- five rounds, INTERLEAVED with the variant rather than run as a block, because backend latency drifts, deployments roll and pools refill, and a block comparison measures the drift. Both arms carry the separator: that is what makes it a control, since a filter stripping the separator strips it from both and the remaining difference is about what the shell did rather than what the filter matched. If the two sets overlap after five rounds, run five more and stop -- a third five is a route being hammered until it agrees.
payload_family: a statement separator plus a bounded delay, against the same separator plus an inert command of equal length. Not a payload catalogue: one delay, sized as a signal and not an outage.
runtime_writer: promote_proposal -- 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 (definition), INSERT INTO observations at :1116-1123, called from src/redkraken/execution.py:518 (`PROMOTE = "SELECT promote_proposal($1::uuid)"`). It inserts the kind the AGENT named, gated only by `enforce_kind_provenance` (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364) which checks the provenance_kind STRING against the vocabulary row's allowed_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236) and nothing else. `timing_differential` and `response_invariant` are both {receipt}-provenance and the Receipts come from ordinary `mcp__rk2__http_request` runs. close_test_replay is NOT cited on this row.
supported_evidence: Agent-filed `timing_differential` (allowed_provenance {receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:226) over the ten interleaved Receipts' `waited_ms` (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:56-58), with agent-filed `response_invariant` ({receipt}) on the control arm as the second edge -- which is the pair the Playbook's own bb:evidence asks for. NOT close_test_replay's: a multipart filename is a request body and no Test action carries one.
refuted_evidence: Agent-filed `response_invariant` on the variant arm: the filename comes back byte for byte with every separator intact and the two arms do not separate in waited_ms. Something encoded the name at the sink, which is the strongest available answer.
stop_conditions: 1 HALT TRIGGER (observed condition): the two sample sets have separated, OR ten rounds have run and they still overlap, OR any response exceeds the route's measured ceiling | 2 COURSE OF ACTION: stop. If the arms did not separate the answer is more samples up to the ten-round cap and then `inconclusive` -- never a longer sleep, which is how a reading becomes an outage without anybody deciding to cause one | 3 SCOPE OF HALT: this endpoint for this run. A route whose connection pool is being asked to hold connections is a Program-wide halt, not a route-level one | 4 RESUME CONDITION: a fresh grant and a re-measured baseline, at a delay no longer than the one already declared | 5 WHO IS TOLD: the operator via mcp__rk2__park_for_human (roster.py:1008); the Program via a program_halts row when the halt is Program-wide | 6 WHAT IS RECORDED: every sample's waited_ms with its arm and round, the counts, the spread, the measured ceiling, and the compare-responses output for the echo leg
owner_ticket: 101 -- the reading is deliverable today only on a Task whose selection also holds a non-read_only Playbook (see preconditions). command-directory-injection declares `bb:triggers_all: ["file_parameter", "multipart_request", "state_changing_method"]` and `bb:effects: read_only` in the same front matter, which is the contradiction ticket 101's rewrite has to settle; `bb:effects` and `bb:risk` move together (playbook.py:95-112).
notes: CEILING -- this reading stops at an Observation and does NOT reach a Finding. `rk2_finding_refusal` (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:642-649) will not open a Finding without a `hypothesis_transitions` row carrying from_status='testing', to_status='supported', actor_kind='runtime', joined through `test_run_receipts` to the very Test run cited. `close_test_replay` (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125) is the only writer of that row, and its to_status comes from `rk2_test_outcome` over the Test's OWN assertions (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:108-121: 'holds' -> 'supported'). This differential cannot be spelled as a Test: `_Door.send` (src/redkraken/replay.py:341-351) hands `proxy.spend` a url and a method and nothing else -- no `headers=`, no `body=`, though `proxy.spend` (proxy.py:4216-4227) accepts both -- and a Test action element is exactly {ordinal, role, kind, method, url} (roster.py:1186-1198). The agent-filed Observation IS a real evidence edge: `rk2_promote_hypotheses` (20261025T000000Z__a_refusal_names_its_cause_and_the_words_it_would_have_taken.sql:530) writes `hypothesis_evidence` from an agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind. But an edge is not a transition, so the claim stops at an Observation. The differential here is a MULTIPART FILENAME, which is a request body end to end, so this row is Observation-ceilinged twice over -- once by the Test action shape and once by the body permission below. The query- and path-borne spellings of the same question are the neighbouring rows and those do reach a Finding. CORRECTION APPLIED. Two mining shards (pd-web-b2, pkb-completed-web) marked this blocked because 'timing_differential has no runtime writer'. It has one: promote_proposal inserts the kind the agent names, the vocabulary allows {receipt}, and a Receipt carries the duration. The Playbook's principal reading is filable as written. What is NOT available is a Test that closes it, because the arms differ in a multipart body and a Test action carries method and url only -- so this claim reaches `supported` and cannot open a Finding. That is the honest limit and it belongs in the rewrite.

Where the framework merges the query string into the same object (`?a[__proto__][x]=`), the write is request-line and the pair becomes Test-expressible; that spelling is worth trying first for exactly that reason.
baseline: POST the same value DIRECTLY as the named field, which route A's validator refuses. That refusal is the reading's whole premise and must be established first.
variant: POST the same value under the property path, then GET route B, which reads the property into the command line. One arrival at the correlator.
control: POST the same pollution carrying a value with NO shell metacharacter, then GET route B. No arrival -- so the arrival belongs to the metacharacter and not to the fetch. Plus the channel's control arrival for freshness, which is read and is not evidence.
payload_family: a property path carrying a read-only command that calls back. One command, and it must be one that reads nothing and changes nothing.

baseline: The ordinary value with no line terminator, submitted and answered.
variant: The same value carrying a raw CRLF at the same offset.
control: The same value with the newline replaced by a SPACE, so the length and shape hold and only the structural character differs. Plus the two-identical-sends noise floor: on this sink the informative outcome is an exception and the silent 200 is the ambiguous one, so a noise floor that is not measured turns a Date header into a finding.
payload_family: one line terminator, plus at most one rung of the encoding ladder (see the next row): raw CRLF, %0d%0a, %250d%250a, and the lone \n without its \r, which many parsers accept and many filters miss.

The assertion set is what decides the kind, so it is part of the row: name the VARIANT in a body_differs assertion against the ORDINARY request and the CONTROL only in a body_equals assertion against the ordinary request. Then close_test_replay writes response_differential for the variant and response_invariant for the control, which is exactly the Playbook's bb:evidence shape. Asserting body_differs(variant, control) instead would make BOTH actions differential, because an action named as `against` counts as named.
supported_evidence: response_differential where url-expressible, with error_detail as the mechanism edge: a mail library that validates its own headers RAISES when it finds a newline, so the route returns a 500 or a specific message and that exception is the primary evidence on this surface.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant between the CRLF arm and the space arm, with the value echoed back with the terminator escaped or stripped. Note what is NOT a refutation: a clean 200 on both arms. The success case is invisible from the response, because a route that accepted the injected header returns exactly what it returned before -- the mail was queued and the handler does not report on it. The honest verdict for a silent 200 is inconclusive, and a reading that treats 'no error' as 'no injection' has this surface exactly backwards.
stop_conditions: 1 HALT TRIGGER (observed condition): the variant errors, or both arms answer 200 identically | 2 COURSE OF ACTION: stop. baseline: The ordinary request: a value of the shape the route documents, carrying nothing structural at all. It comes first and it is what the control is later held invariant against -- without it 'the control answered normally' is an assertion rather than a comparison.
variant: The same field carrying one structural character for the named sink: an unbalanced quote or bracket for a predicate, a bare < for element content, a CRLF pair for a line-oriented sink.
control: The same value with that character replaced by an inert one of the SAME LENGTH -- a space for the newline, a letter for the bracket. Same length, same position, same everything else, because a control that omits the character shortens the value, changes the document's byte count and travels a different path through every validator between the caller and the parser. Repeat policy is two rounds of all three, six requests: a parser error that appears once is as likely to be a restart as a parse, and an offset that moves between two otherwise identical variants is not an offset this reading can cite. Plus the two-identical-sends noise floor.
payload_family: one structural character per sink, against its inert twin of equal length. Not a payload list.

baseline: the first arrival alone, which the external-entity row already produces: the parser fetched the DTD and stopped there.
variant: a second arrival whose recorded target carries a value the reading did not send. One arrival proves resolution; the second proves the parser executed a nested declaration our DTD wrote.
control: the first-arrival-only case as the negative -- a parser that fetches the DTD and never makes the second request has told you parameter entities resolve and nested dynamic declarations do not -- plus the channel control arrival for freshness, which is read and is not evidence.

preconditions: graphql_surface. A filter -- a WAF rule, a middleware regex or a gateway deny list -- refuses a named token. The ignored character is spelled percent-encoded in the query -- %0a, %09, %20 or %2c -- which rk2_test_request_problem accepts: its url pattern is '^https?://[a-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/[^\s]*)?$' and its only path refusals are a literal . or .. segment and the string %2e (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:217-226).
baseline: GET /graphql?query=%7B__schema%7B...%7D%7D -- the plain introspection document in the query string; artifact A, a 400 or 403.
variant: The identical url with the ignored character percent-encoded between the token and its brace -- ?query=%7B__schema%0A%7B... ; artifact V. The header value pattern forbids CR and LF in OUR headers, but %0A in a query string is three printable characters on the wire (origin_form takes urlsplit(url).path verbatim and appends the query, removing nothing, proxy.py:818-828) and the server decodes it into the newline the lexer ignores.
control: Two controls. (a) POST a trivially valid document that names no blocked token; it must succeed, otherwise the endpoint refuses everything and V proves nothing. (b) Two identical sends of the baseline, which must be body_equals -- an error page carrying a request id or a timestamp would otherwise make every arm differ.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, websocket_surface. The session must not travel as a per-connection ticket, or the answer is already no.
baseline: Would be: the handshake from the application's own page and origin under the leased session, recording status 101, the accept header and the negotiated subprotocol.
variant: Would be: the identical handshake with the session, from a page served on a different origin -- one variable, the Origin the browser attaches.
control: Would be: the identical handshake from the same origin with the session removed, which must fail. Without it a public endpoint reads exactly like the finding. Plus the two-identical-sends control, since a 101 exchange carries a per-connection accept value and body_differs would fire on it alone.
payload_family: an HTTP upgrade request whose Origin is the only varied field
runtime_writer: none reachable. The handshake never leaves the door in a form the target can upgrade, so no Receipt of a 101 exists and close_test_replay has nothing to derive a kind from.
supported_evidence: none. The Playbook declares response_invariant as its supporting variant kind and that kind is writable, but the action that would produce it cannot be performed.
refuted_evidence: none, same reason.
stop_conditions: (1) Halt trigger: the first step's response is not a 101 -- observed as a 200, a 400 or a 426 where the surface record says the route upgrades. (2) Course of action: stop the reading at step 2 and do not send the variant; a variant compared against a baseline that never upgraded measures the door, not the target. (3) Scope: the whole reading, on every websocket route, until the owner ticket lands -- this is not a property of one route. (4) Resume: an egress lane exists that carries Upgrade and Connection to the target and records the 101 exchange as a Receipt. (5) Told: the engagement operator, and the Playbook maintainer, because a Playbook whose first step cannot complete will otherwise be re-selected on every websocket surface the scheduler finds. (6) Recorded: this ledger row, the Receipt of the non-101 answer, and the three source lines below.

notes: THE LOAD-BEARING ROW OF THIS GROUP. D1 is the operator's decision on this row: realtime gets a truthful scope, bb:triggers_any grows form_request and state_changing_method, the five form-CSRF readings below become the Playbook's principal reading, and the websocket refusal is named in the prose with these three source lines so nobody re-proposes it.

The spellings '..%2f' and '..;/' match neither refusal -- after '..' comes '%' or ';', not '/' or end of string, and neither contains '%2e' -- so those two are the ones the closing Test uses.

variant: GET a path that keeps a cacheable prefix or a foreign first segment and reaches the private route through '..%2f' or '..;/', on its own invented key; then, from a Task holding no Identity, GET that same url. notes: REACHES A FINDING, on the two spellings named below and not on the other two. CRITIC BLOCKER g09#26 IS PARTLY RIGHT AND PARTLY WRONG, AND THE SOURCE SETTLES IT. Right: the card's 'the traversal family is reachable' was never checked against the Test-lane checker, and a closing Test whose url contains '%2e' or a literal '.'/'..' segment is refused before the Test opens, so the old body_differs claim was not producible for those spellings. Wrong: 'any row whose CLOSING Test needs %2e or a dot segment is blocked' does not reach this row, because this row does not need either. I ran the two refusal patterns from 20260815T000000Z:222-226 over the candidate spellings: '/public/../admin' is refused by the segment regex, '/%2e%2e/admin' is refused by the %2e test, and '/public/..%2fadmin' and '/public/..;/admin' are refused by NEITHER -- after '..' comes '%' or ';' rather than '/' or end of string, and no '%2e' appears. Those two spellings are also the ones that reach the wire unchanged, because origin_form removes nothing (proxy.py:818-828). So the row keeps a Finding path and the row now names the spelling that carries it, which is a stronger corpus instruction than either the old row or the critic's fix. Distinct from the delimiter row: one asks where the path ends, this one asks whether the path is resolved before routing, and a cache whose rule is a string prefix rather than a resolved path fails only the second. The mined nokline row proposed proving it by invariance across two Identities; writing it as a differential on the anonymous arm instead gets the same fact through the bb:evidence rows the Playbook has. This is the one family that can leak a real user's response into a shared cache, hence the immediate-notify stop condition.

variant: The same operation, same method, same body shape, as label A, on label A's object whose recorded state should forbid it. One variable against the owner control: the object's state.
control: Three. (1) The nonexistent control: the same operation, as label A, on an identifier that names no object, so a 404 for a forbidden transition and a 404 for a missing object can be told apart. (2) The foreign-owner control: the same operation as label B on label A's object, which must be refused. (3) The two-identical-sends control: the step-2 read of the untouched sibling object sent twice unchanged, because body_differs fires on the Date header alone and the after-state comparison in step 5 is worthless against a route nobody showed to be byte-stable.

preconditions: form_request or json_request, state_changing_method, unknown_auth_endpoint. A username that is known-valid or plausibly valid, and the backing store identified well enough to choose one spelling: an LDAP directory, an XML document, or a document store. Every character needed is printable ASCII inside body, which is a free 0..65536-byte string, so none of it touches the header value pattern.
baseline: The same login form posted with a well-formed, certainly-wrong credential of the right type: the ordinary refusal page, stored.
variant: One spelling per request: an LDAP wildcard alone in the password field against a known username; an XPath predicate that closes the quoted term and appends an always-true clause, and its neutralising form where a trailing hashed-password clause can never be satisfied; the field carrying a comparison-operator document where the store parses documents.
control: Two. (1) The same spelling against a username that certainly does not exist -- if that authenticates too, the endpoint accepts anything and the operator proved nothing about the filter. For the XPath arm the equivalent is the same quote-breaking shape with a FALSE tail, which must not authenticate. (2) The wrong-credential baseline sent twice unchanged, so a body_differs between refusal pages is not a per-request nonce.
payload_family: one metacharacter or operator of the query language behind the comparison, one spelling per request.

refuted_evidence: credential_effect ({receipt}), filed the same way: the operator arm is answered the way the wrong credential is. An Observation, not a settled refutation, for the reason in notes.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the first authenticated response arrives. course of action: stop; do not enumerate further accounts under a bypassed check. scope: this endpoint. resume: an operator decides whether the session that came back may be used at all. told: the operator who opened the Task, immediately, because a live session was created against the subject. recorded: the exact spelling, the nonexistent-username control, and the identity the authenticated page named.

No LDAP- or XPath-aware Playbook exists among the fifty and this is the right home for the authentication-boundary half. The blind oracle halves -- filter rebalancing to recover which characters are escaped, positional node walks, substring ladders -- are enumeration, are refused by this Playbook's step 3, and need a Playbook of their own. preconditions: unknown_auth_endpoint or unauthenticated_endpoint, email_valued_parameter, state_changing_method. One identifier known to exist -- the operator's own account is enough. On the reset endpoint the known identifier must be the operator's own, so nobody else receives mail.
baseline: The endpoint posted with an identifier that certainly does not exist and an arbitrary password: status and body recorded byte for byte.
variant: The identical request with an identifier known to exist. Any difference in status, in wording, or in redirect target is the oracle; the Academy records cases where the difference is a single invisible character, which a byte comparison catches and a reader does not.
control: A SECOND certainly-absent identifier against the first. The two must match exactly. If they already differ, the endpoint carries a nonce, a timestamp or a rotating message and the variant's difference proves nothing -- this is the two-identical-sends control in the only form that works here, because two literally identical sends would not separate 'stable page' from 'stable for this one identifier'.
payload_family: account identifiers: one known-real, two invented.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 (close_test_replay) writes the response_differential from the status_differs/body_differs pair over the known and invented arms.
supported_evidence: SPLIT BY CARRIER. Where the identifier rides the QUERY or the PATH -- a registration-availability check, a lookup route, a public profile route -- response_differential written by close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) from the status_differs/body_differs pair over three urls that differ only in the identifier: known-real, invented, invented-again. Where the identifier rides a login or reset BODY, reflected_input ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- the wording that names existence, cited from the Receipt of the known-identifier arm and absent from both invented arms. NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the known identifier is answered exactly as the invented ones are.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the first pair that differs. course of action: stop; the reading is 'is there an oracle', not 'harvest the users', and no password guessing follows the account that was confirmed. scope: this endpoint. resume: not needed -- the reading is complete at three requests. told: the operator who opened the Task. recorded: the three identifiers, the byte difference, and the count, which is three and is declared before starting.

notes: Filed under this slug because two miners filed it here and the subject is this Playbook's own route, but the class is information_disclosure.identifier_oracle -- one of the nine nothing emits -- and sign-up-login-register.md deliberately routes it out: the enumeration reading wants MANY accounts and the verification reading wants ONE sent five ways. The rewrite must keep the routing sentence and hand the reading to the new Playbook rather than folding it in. The reset-endpoint spelling is the same mechanism and costs no mail beyond the operator's own. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW REACHES A FINDING. Its differential lives in the QUERY or the PATH -- three urls differing only in the identifier -- wherever the pre-auth surface answers an identifier from the request line, which is the availability-check and lookup shape, which is what a Test action can state. A Test action states a method and a url and the checker accepts both (rk2_test_request_problem, 20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:199-226), and record_test_action compares method, scheme, host, port and path -- the query is deliberately not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt (same file, :1375-1391), so a query-borne differential rides through intact. The login-POST and reset-POST spellings of the same reading are body-borne and stop at an agent-filed reflected_input. The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226). CLASS NOTE, and the emitter verdict is not this row's: information_disclosure.identifier_oracle is one of the nine classes no Playbook emits, and the verdict for it lives in ledger/orphans.json rows 14, 15 and 24 under exceptional-conditions. baseline: Register or request recovery for an address the operator controls, and receive the link without opening it.
variant: Change the account's address, then redeem the link that was issued for the first one, and read which address it verified. Or read several issued tokens and ask whether they share a prefix, advance monotonically, or encode a timestamp or a user id.
control: A link issued for a third address redeemed against the same account, which must not verify the second; and tokens issued minutes apart, so a shared prefix is not an artefact of the same second.
payload_family: the flow's own issued credential, read out of band
runtime_writer: none. The reading never reaches a verb.
supported_evidence: would be response_differential on the redemption, once the link is in hand. Not producible.
refuted_evidence: would be response_invariant. Not producible.

preconditions: email_valued_parameter, state_changing_method, unauthenticated_endpoint, form_request or json_request. Every address on both sides is one the Program's test identity controls. The rate matters as much as the shape: a recovery endpoint is one of the few whose abuse is visible to end users rather than only to logs.
baseline: The recovery request with a single, valid, operator-owned address: the accepted answer, stored.
variant: One multiplicity spelling per request: the name repeated in the query and the body; a JSON array of two owned addresses; a comma list; the value carrying a folded cc line; a form body restated as JSON with a nested array.
control: Two. (1) A single value that is not a valid address, which must be a validation error -- that confirms the field IS validated, so acceptance of the multiplicity shape means something. (2) The baseline sent twice unchanged, so a body_differs between two confirmation pages is not a per-submission token.
payload_family: multiplicity spellings of one recipient field, every value an address the Program leased.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 (close_test_replay) writes the response_differential from the status_differs/body_differs pair over the multiplicity arm and the invalid-address control.
supported_evidence: SPLIT BY CARRIER. Where the recipient rides the QUERY -- `?email=a&email=b` on the recovery route -- response_differential written by close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) from the status_differs/body_differs pair over the multiplicity url and the single-valid-address url, with an invalid-address url as the control: three urls, one method, no body. Where the recipient rides the JSON body -- the array, the comma list, the folded cc line -- reflected_input ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- the multiplicity arm accepted where the invalid-address control was refused. NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every multiplicity spelling is answered the way the invalid address is.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: an address appears in an arm that the Program did not lease. course of action: do not send it; there is no version of this reading that touches a stranger's mailbox. scope: the whole run under this Playbook. resume: the operator confirms both addresses are leased. told: the operator who opened the Task, plus the Program contact through the operator once the endpoint has been exercised at all. recorded: every address used, every spelling sent, and the count.
owner_ticket: 101 -- ship the authentication.recovery_flow emitter line (D3). PLUS 211 for the body-borne arms.
notes: Two boundaries are worth carrying verbatim into the rewrite. The delivery half is blocked: no observation kind carries a received message, so the claim stops at acceptance. And the CR LF here sits inside a BODY value bound for a mail header -- body is a free 0..65536-byte string -- so the schema refusal that excludes CR and LF from OUR header values (VALUE pattern printable ASCII only) does not reach it. That distinction is the one the request-parsing CRLF refusal is repeatedly mistaken for. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW REACHES A FINDING. Its differential lives in the QUERY STRING for the repeated-name arm, which is the one arm of this row that is two urls and nothing else, which is what a Test action can state. A Test action states a method and a url and the checker accepts both (rk2_test_request_problem, 20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:199-226), and record_test_action compares method, scheme, host, port and path -- the query is deliberately not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt (same file, :1375-1391), so a query-borne differential rides through intact. The array, comma-list and folded-cc-header arms ride a JSON or form BODY and stop at an agent-filed reflected_input. The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226). THE CLAIM CEILING IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE POINT OF THE ROW: the claim is kept on whether the SHAPE was accepted, never on what arrived anywhere, because there is no mailbox -- callback_interactions carry arrival_kind dns or http and the declared channel is a correlator, not an MX. This row is the survivor for pd-web-a:45; ledger/orphans.json folded[] records that and disputes the critic finding that called it lost. The two mail-header-injection mined rows (pd-web-b5:18, wiki-delta:14) fold in here as the folded-cc arm and nowhere else.

technique: The secret is presented in a shape the comparator was not written for -- the field omitted, present and empty, carrying a different JSON type, or with the signature stripped or empty -- so the branch that compares is skipped rather than answered.

preconditions: email_valued_parameter, state_changing_method, unknown_auth_endpoint or authenticated_endpoint. An Identity slot that holds a working credential for this endpoint; the run acts as whichever Identity the Task was opened under and the step neither chooses nor prints it. Where no slot holds a working credential the reading does not start, because every arm below is a comparison against a request known to succeed.
baseline: Two readings that are the scale: the credential presented correctly with the slot attached, stored; and the same request with the secret replaced by a value of the same type that is certainly wrong, stored. An endpoint answering 200 to both does not authenticate here and every arm below would measure the wrong route.
variant: One malformation per request, each sent once: the field omitted; the field present and empty; the field carrying a boolean, a number, an empty array, an object; and where the credential is a signature or a MAC, the same body with the signature removed and with it present but empty.
control: Two. (1) The wrong-secret arm, which is what says the endpoint returns an authentication decision at all -- this is the Playbook's own control and its credential_effect edge. (2) The correct-credential arm sent twice unchanged, because body_differs fires on the Date header alone and a login answer usually carries a fresh token or timestamp; without it 'the variant matched the correct-secret answer' is a sentence about a route nobody showed to be stable.
payload_family: type and presence changes on one field. Never a second value of the same type: that is guessing, it is bounded by rate_limiting rather than by this class, and the Playbook refuses to iterate.

The Playbook's own bb:evidence already names credential_effect twice, so this is the kind the corpus asks for and not a substitute.

stop_conditions: halt trigger: an account lockout, a captcha, or a 429 appears mid-sequence. course of action: end the sequence at that request; the readings after one are about the defence rather than about the comparison. scope: this endpoint for the rest of the run. resume: the operator confirms the lockout has expired or the slot has been re-leased. told: the operator who opened the Task. recorded: the arm that met the defence, the stored scale, and the fact that the remaining shapes were not sent.
owner_ticket: 211 -- A Test action carries the header and the body it plans (ready-for-agent, Blocked by: nothing)
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the carrier is a request header or body, which a Test action now states. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. The Playbook's core. The mined claim that credential_effect has no runtime writer is wrong: promote_proposal inserts an observations row with the kind the agent named, and credential_effect's vocabulary row allows {receipt}, which a request through the door produces. A variant that answers a 500 or a third status is inconclusive here and is recorded as an error_detail question for somebody else. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. Its differential lives in a request BODY -- the login or token-exchange document, whose field is omitted, emptied or retyped. The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226). Only close_test_replay writes a testing->supported hypothesis_transitions row (20260816T000000Z__impact_is_authorized_before_it_is_proved.sql:1125-1129), rk2_finding_refusal will not open a Finding without one joined to the cited Test run (20260815T120000Z__a_supported_claim_becomes_a_candidate.sql:644-649), and the Observation kind that lane writes is derived from the Test's own assertions and nothing else (20260816T000000Z...:1063-1072). An agent-filed Observation is a real hypothesis_evidence edge -- rk2_promote_hypotheses filters on no kind (20261025T000000Z...:530) -- but it cannot carry a Hypothesis to supported. Unblocked by ticket 211 (docs/specs/production-harness-v2/issues/211-a-test-action-carries-the-header-and-the-body-it-plans.md, status ready-for-agent, Blocked by: nothing). The one spelling that WOULD reach a Finding is an endpoint that takes the credential in the query string; where the recon pass finds that, re-file the same reading with the two urls as the two actions.
