An account the Program's test identity created whose token column has never been populated, or one where the expiry is initialised at signup rather than at reset.
baseline: The validate-token step submitted with a token that is well-formed and wrong: rejected, stored. Then the same step with a correct token from the test identity's own live reset: accepted, stored. Those two are the scale.
variant: The token field omitted; then present and empty; then the JSON null; then the JSON string spelling of null; then an empty array. One per request.
control: Two. (1) The well-formed-wrong-token arm, which is what says the step rejects at all. (2) The wrong-token arm sent twice unchanged, so a body_differs between two rejections is not a rotating nonce in the page.
payload_family: absence and empty-type spellings of one token field.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 (close_test_replay) writes the response_differential from the status_differs pair; src/redkraken/execution.py:518 (PROMOTE = "SELECT promote_proposal($1::uuid)"), whose LIVE definition is 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123 -- the 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition is superseded, behaviour identical files the credential_effect edge from the accepted arm's Receipt.
supported_evidence: SPLIT BY CARRIER. Where the token rides the QUERY STRING -- the shape a mailed reset link actually has -- response_differential written by close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) from the status_differs pair over `?token=` absent, `?token=` empty and a well-formed-wrong-token control: three urls, one method, all three states of a Test action. Where the token rides a JSON body, credential_effect ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- the absent-token arm answered the way the correct token is. NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every absence spelling is answered the way the wrong token is.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the endpoint has no separate validate step, so acceptance and the credential change are one request. course of action: do not send the arm; a single-shot endpoint puts this reading above the Playbook's effects declaration. scope: this flow. resume: an operator opens a Playbook declaring mutates_account, which playbooks_risk_matches_effects (src/redkraken/migrations/0032_playbooks.sql:252-257) forces to approval_required or forbidden. told: the operator who opened the Task. recorded: the account the test identity created, the flow shape, and the reason the arm was not sent.
owner_ticket: 101 -- ship the authentication.recovery_flow emitter line (D3: a missing bb:outputs emitter is reachable with owner_ticket 101, because 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs). PLUS 211 for the body-borne spellings only. The emitter verdict itself is orphans' (ledger/orphans.json rows 9-13, 22, 23).
notes: This is authentication.credential_verification read at a reset step, which the Playbook's step 1 admits as a subject ('a login, a token exchange, a step in a reset'), and it is also the cheapest candidate emitter for authentication.recovery_flow -- a class with a bound fixture and no bb:outputs anywhere naming it. Bounded to the validate step on purpose: completing the change is mutates_account and this Playbook is constrained/mutates_session. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW REACHES A FINDING. Its differential lives in the QUERY STRING -- the token parameter omitted, then present and empty, against a well-formed-wrong-token control -- for the link-borne spelling, which is the spelling a recovery flow actually ships, which is what a Test action can state. A Test action states a method and a url and the checker accepts both (rk2_test_request_problem, 20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:199-226), and record_test_action compares method, scheme, host, port and path -- the query is deliberately not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt (same file, :1375-1391), so a query-borne differential rides through intact. The JSON-body spellings of the same reading (null, the string "null", an empty array) are body-borne and stop at an agent-filed credential_effect. The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226). ONE MECHANISM CHECK against orphans: this is NOT ledger/orphans.json row 10 ('the completion step does not require the credential the flow issued', from researchers:26 and portswigger:26). That row is about a completion step with no token check at all; this row is about a token check that runs and compares against a column the server left at its default.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, serialized_object_parameter, state_changing_method -- and two facts the recon pass must have established, not guessed: a JSON-accepting route whose handler MERGES the caller's document into an object, and a JavaScript-shaped stack. Plus the operator gate in stop_conditions: pollution is not undoable in process, so this reading may not start without an authorisation that names a process-wide side effect.
baseline: The route's own malformed request -- a deliberately broken JSON body -- sent once and recorded as answering a stable error status, typically 400 or 500. Then that identical malformed request sent a SECOND time, unchanged, so the error path is shown to be byte-stable before anything is written.
variant: One well-formed request whose body carries {"__proto__":{"status":555}}, and then the identical malformed request from the baseline, unchanged. 555 is chosen because no framework means it. One arm of the same row asks how far up the chain to write: one __proto__ step reaches the class prototype and two reach Object.prototype, and the SHALLOWEST step that works is the one to keep, because it is both the safer write and the more precise claim.
control: Three. (1) The sibling-route control: the same malformed request against a route on the same application that does not merge, which must still answer the baseline status -- that is what makes the change the prototype's and not the request's. (2) The chain-depth control: three __proto__ steps, which must have NO effect, because the chain ends at Object.prototype; an effect at three means the oracle is not measuring the chain at all. (3) The two-identical-sends control already in the baseline, because body_differs fires on the Date header alone.
payload_family: one inert property name the framework itself reads -- status -- carried under __proto__ at a stated chain depth. Never a property that changes routing, authentication or a template path; never a gadget.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 issues SELECT promote_proposal($1::uuid); the LIVE promote_proposal is 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with its observations INSERT at :1116-1123 (the 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition is superseded, behaviour identical). It inserts the kind the AGENT named out of the proposal's open element list (roster.py:1356-1370), gated only by enforce_kind_provenance (0018_vocabularies.sql:345-364), which checks the provenance_kind STRING alone. close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) does NOT write for this row: the pollution write is a request body and no Test action carries one.
supported_evidence: state_change ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- a side effect observable on a LATER request -- which is what this whole family is, and it is the one evidential kind whose own vocabulary description says so (0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236: 'a side effect was observable on a later request'). NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.
refuted_evidence: state_change ({receipt}) filed the same way and reading the other way: the re-sent read arm answers exactly as it did before the write, so nothing on this route merged into a prototype. An Observation, not a settled refutation -- close_test_replay is the only writer of BOTH terminal transitions and this reading cannot reach that lane.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the polluted status appears, OR any request to the application starts failing in a way it did not before the write. course of action: stop the family immediately, do not try the second or third oracle, and do not raise the chain depth. scope: this route AND every route the same worker process serves, which is the whole point of the halt -- pollution is not undoable in process. resume: an operator restarts the process or accepts the residue in writing. told: the operator who opened the Task, immediately and before the next arm, because the blast radius is the process and not the route. recorded: the exact polluted key and value, the depth of the chain that reached it, the three Artifacts, and the wall-clock instant of the write so a restart can be correlated.
owner_ticket: 101 -- three things this ticket owns at once: no Playbook of the fifty emits a prototype-pollution class at all (the nearest is authorization.object_property_write, one of the nine with no emitter, and it is narrower because it is about an object the caller DOES own); deserialization's bb:outputs is injection.object_graph and does not cover a merge that writes the prototype; and bb:effects: read_only forbids the body this reading needs. D3 makes a missing emitter reachable-with-owner-ticket rather than blocked. PLUS 211 for the Test-action body.
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: nothing is sent; the row files an Observation over stored material. The ceiling paragraph below still holds. WRITTEN IN THIS REPAIR PASS under D6 item 2 and repair/g10.json blocker 1: eight mined prototype-pollution rows had no ledger row, no fold and no drop anywhere in the ledger -- a mined_from census over all eleven files confirmed pd-web-b3:10-14 and portswigger:0-2 were UNCLAIMED. Three rows now carry them, and this is the first. HIGH VALUE. The chain-depth reading is folded in here rather than given its own row because it is not a separate question about the target -- it is the parameter that makes the other three safe enough to send, and a row nobody runs first is a row that gets skipped. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING, and the carrier is why. The pollution WRITE is a JSON request body and there is no other spelling of it: the whole mechanism is a merge of a caller's document. Two walls, both checked in source. (1) deserialization declares bb:effects: read_only, so a Task whose whole selection is read_only Playbooks opens with body_allowed: false -- _body_allowed returns any(one.effects != 'read_only') (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646) -- and the door refuses the body. The write is performable only on a Task whose selection carries a non-read_only Playbook, or after ticket 101 moves this Playbook's bb:effects, which drags bb:risk with it because risk may not sit below what effects imply (0032_playbooks.sql:252-257, playbook.py:95-112). (2) The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226). So the pollution can never be an action, a setup step or a cleanup step of a Test, which means the READ arms -- which are method-plus-url and would otherwise close a Test on their own -- have nothing to attribute their difference to inside the replay. preconditions: json_request or api_surface, plus an Artifact already stored whose BODY IS JSON and carries the token as a value. jq is registered with two arguments -- filter (text, the jq program) and input (artifact) -- at src/redkraken/migrations/20260814T030000Z__an_offline_tool_becomes_evidence.sql:205-207, and jqrun.py runs it as a bare two-argument jq call over the carrier-stripped body (src/redkraken/jqrun.py:105-118). No flags: the input must be valid JSON, so a token in a JSON body qualifies and a token in a response header does not -- and set-cookie is stripped from the agent view anyway (src/redkraken/proxy.py:376).
baseline: The token as issued, inside the stored Artifact, unmodified.
variant: One run_tool call, tool jq, whose filter tests the token against the format table: the base64 prefix of a Java stream or its raw magic bytes, the base64 prefix of a pickle or its raw opcode, the leading object or array marker of a PHP serialize string, a polymorphic type-handling key in a JSON document, a leading XML declaration with an object-class element. test(), capture(), splits() and base64 decoding are all ordinary jq and all available inside the one filter argument.
control: One run of the same filter over a token from an application known to issue random identifiers, so 'no signature matched' means something rather than being the filter's only possible answer.
payload_family: none. This is a read of bytes already held; nothing is sent.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/execution.py:518 (PROMOTE = "SELECT promote_proposal($1::uuid)"), whose LIVE definition is 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123 -- the 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition is superseded, behaviour identical inserts the observations row with the kind the agent named. The kind is content_match, whose vocabulary row allows {tool_run} ALONE (src/redkraken/migrations/0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), and the tool_run is the jq call above -- there are only four binaries and this is the one that matches text.
supported_evidence: none from the Test lane. content_match is an agent-filed supporting edge on the Hypothesis the type-name differential closes; rk2_promote_hypotheses writes hypothesis_evidence from agent-supplied observation_id with no filter on the cited kind.
refuted_evidence: none. A classification that matches nothing does not refute the Hypothesis; it says the type-name reading has no field to edit and the run stops before it starts.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the token is not inside a JSON body, so jq has no valid input. course of action: do not file a content_match; say the classification is ungrounded and stop before the type-name reading. scope: this token. resume: the token is captured inside a JSON response, or a matcher binary is registered. told: the operator who opened the Task. recorded: the jq filter, its exit code -- 1, 4 and 5 each mean something and jqrun.py passes them through untouched -- and the Artifact hash it read.
owner_ticket: 211 -- A Test action carries the header and the body it plans (ready-for-agent, Blocked by: nothing)
notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: nothing is sent; the row files an Observation over stored material. The ceiling paragraph below still holds. The mined row called this blocked on two grounds and both are wrong. jq's filter argument is a whole jq program, so matching a byte signature and base64-decoding are both expressible; and content_match is not writer-less -- promote_proposal inserts the kind the agent named. The real limit is narrower and is in the preconditions: jq is invoked with no flags, so the Artifact body has to be valid JSON. Everything else in the deserialization family is gated behind this classification, which is why the unlock is worth more than its size. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING, and it always did. CEILING RESTATED AND IT WAS ALREADY HONEST: this row files an Observation and never reaches a Finding, because nothing is sent -- it is one jq run over bytes already held. That is not the Finding-path wall, it is the row's purpose: it tells the type-name rows where the field is before they edit anything. D4 does not shorten it either, because the input here is a stored Artifact and not a browse run. jq is registered with exactly two arguments, filter (text) and input (ARTIFACT, singular) (20260814T030000Z__an_offline_tool_becomes_evidence.sql:205-207), so ONE run reads ONE Artifact -- which is the same limit that blocks the cross-artifact identifier reading orphans carries at its row 23.

preconditions: serialized_object_parameter, authenticated_endpoint. Established by the parse-versus-validation reading above: every edited blob is rejected identically regardless of what was edited.
baseline: The original blob, replayed twice unchanged: accepted.
variant: n/a -- the arm cannot be composed. Any edit to the type name invalidates the signature and the route rejects the envelope before it reaches a deserialiser.
control: n/a. The reading has already produced its own control: an edit to an inert FIELD is rejected the same way an edit to the type name is, which is what says the signature and not the content decided.
payload_family: none composable. Key material is not sought.
runtime_writer: none. The verdict is inconclusive and inconclusive writes no Observation.
supported_evidence: none.
refuted_evidence: none. A signed blob does not refute injection.object_graph; it says this reading cannot see it.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: two edits to different fields of the blob are rejected identically. course of action: record inconclusive, name which signature stopped it, and route to an operator; do not look for the key in a bundle, a config file or a repository. scope: this route. resume: an operator decides that the key question is in scope and opens it as its own work. told: the operator who opened the Task, with the decision in front of them. recorded: the signature scheme if the envelope names one, the two rejected edits, and the inconclusive verdict in those words.
owner_ticket: NEW: key-material work is an operator decision and needs its own scope grant, not a step in this Playbook
notes: The refusal has a reason that is about evidence rather than about safety: a reading that finds the key can no longer tell whether the route trusts the blob because it verified the signature or because it never checked. Where the envelope is ENCRYPTED rather than signed there is a distinct three-request reading -- the intact token, one byte of the final block flipped, and a length that is not a block multiple, asking whether a padding failure answers differently from a MAC failure. That is a ciphertext oracle, it is harness-reachable in three requests and closes as a status differential, and it is NOT injection.object_graph: it belongs with information_disclosure.identifier_oracle, which nothing emits. Recorded here so the next reader does not fold it into this class, and so the byte-by-byte recovery that follows it -- hundreds of requests against a live subject -- is refused on sight. REFUSAL UNCHANGED. Recorded here rather than as its own row: the padding-oracle and ciphertext-oracle readings (owasp:22, pd-web-a:52) fold in as the same ceiling -- the envelope is authenticated, editing it needs the key, and key-material work is an operator grant this Playbook does not have. Note that the WSTG scenario cited is the padding-oracle one, which is the fold's source and not this row's own mechanism.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, serialized_object_parameter, state_changing_method -- and two facts the recon pass must have established, not guessed: a JSON-accepting route whose handler MERGES the caller's document into an object, and a JavaScript-shaped stack. Plus the operator gate in stop_conditions: pollution is not undoable in process, so this reading may not start without an authorisation that names a process-wide side effect.
baseline: The read endpoint answered once and recorded byte for byte, then answered a second time unchanged, so the serialisation is shown to be stable. Where the charset arm is the one available, the baseline is a reflected test string that round-trips verbatim -- the source's own is HelloWorld+ACEAIQAh-, which is HelloWorld!!! encoded UTF-7 by iconv.
variant: One well-formed request whose body carries {"__proto__":{"json spaces":10}}, then the read endpoint again: the same data comes back indented. Or {"__proto__":{"content-type":"application/json; charset=utf-7"}}, then the reflection again: the test string comes back decoded as HelloWorld!!!. UTF-7 rather than a codepage the application cannot speak, precisely so the application keeps working. Second arm, run only after a __proto__ spelling produced nothing: {"constructor":{"prototype":{"json spaces":10}}} -- as nested objects, because dot notation is one property name -- which asks whether the sanitiser blocked a spelling or a capability.
control: Three. (1) The value-follows control, which is what makes indentation a reading rather than a server mood: send {"__proto__":{"json spaces":0}} and confirm the indentation returns to the baseline. A one-way change is anything; a change that FOLLOWS the value is pollution. (2) The pure-ASCII control for the charset arm: a string with no +-sequence in it, which must be identical on both legs, so the difference is the decoder and not the reflector. (3) The shape control for the constructor arm: {"harmless":{"prototype":{"json spaces":10}}}, a nested object of the same shape with no reachable prototype, which must do nothing -- so the effect is the constructor path and not any nesting. A third spelling that cannot work, "proto", rules out the endpoint reacting to any extra key.
payload_family: serialisation properties the response writer itself reads -- json spaces, content-type -- and the two PATHS to the prototype, __proto__ and constructor.prototype. The value is always inert: an indent width, a charset the application already speaks.

supported_evidence: state_change ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- a side effect observable on a LATER request -- which is what this whole family is, and it is the one evidential kind whose own vocabulary description says so (0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236: 'a side effect was observable on a later request'). NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.

preconditions: authenticated_endpoint, serialized_object_parameter, state_changing_method. The parameter is read from the state view rather than picked out of the request, because a route may carry a session cookie, a CSRF token and a saved-state blob and only the last is deserialised. The format is named from the first bytes of a blob the client itself produced, which is what says where the type name sits.
baseline: stable_session. The request sent twice, unchanged, carrying a blob the client itself produced. Two identical sends because everything after is a comparison and a route that returns a fresh token or a rotating panel is not byte-stable; a differential against a baseline nobody checked is noise with a verdict attached.
variant: The same state re-encoded by the same code path, naming a type the client never sends, chosen from the runtime's own standard library and chosen for being inert: a container, a collection, a primitive wrapper, a date. No constructor, no readObject, no setstate, no property setter and no finaliser that touches a file, a process, a socket or a class loader.
control: Three. (1) The control arm: the same state through the same encoder naming the type the client's own blob named, so the pair differs in one string and not in the encoding. (2) The nonexistent-type probe: a name of the right shape that resolves to nothing in any runtime -- if it reproduces the variant, what was measured is a validator. (3) The two-identical-sends baseline above, which is what makes body_differs mean something other than the Date header.
payload_family: type names from the runtime's own standard library, inert by construction; never a chain, never a generator's output.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 (close_test_replay) writes the response_differential from the body_differs/status_differs pair over the variant and control arms, and the response_invariant from the two baseline sends that no differing assertion names.
supported_evidence: SPLIT BY CARRIER. Where the blob rides the QUERY STRING or a PATH SEGMENT: response_differential written by close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) from the body_differs/status_differs pair over the type-name arm and the control arm, plus the response_invariant from the two baseline sends that no differing assertion names -- five urls, one method, no body. Where the blob rides a request BODY or the Cookie header: state_change ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- the type-name arm answered differently from a baseline that was invariant against itself. NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the two arms invariant against each other against a stable baseline: the blob was read as data into a shape the route had already chosen.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the two baseline sends differ and nothing holds still between them. course of action: run compare-responses over them, record what moved, and compare only the parts that held still; where nothing holds still, say the Playbook cannot read the route. scope: this route. resume: the route becomes byte-stable, or an operator names the fields to exclude. told: the operator who opened the Task. recorded: both baseline Artifacts and the fields that moved.
owner_ticket: 211 -- A Test action carries the header and the body it plans (ready-for-agent, Blocked by: nothing). PLUS 101 if the rewrite wants the body-borne spelling runnable at all, because that needs deserialization's bb:effects to move off read_only and bb:risk moves with it (playbook.py:95-112).
notes: The Playbook's core, and the repeat policy is part of the reading: two rounds of the pair, four requests, interleaved with the baseline rather than sent as a block. A difference that appears once and not again is a route that varies, not a type that was constructed. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW REACHES A FINDING. Its differential lives in the QUERY STRING or a PATH SEGMENT wherever the blob travels there, and the type name is one field inside a value the url carries, which is what a Test action can state. A Test action states a method and a url and the checker accepts both (rk2_test_request_problem, 20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:199-226), and record_test_action compares method, scheme, host, port and path -- the query is deliberately not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt (same file, :1375-1391), so a query-borne differential rides through intact. CARRIER IS THE WHOLE QUESTION FOR THIS PLAYBOOK, and the row now names it. deserialization declares bb:effects: read_only (src/redkraken/playbooks/deserialization/playbook.md), so a Task whose whole selection is read_only Playbooks opens with body_allowed: false -- _body_allowed returns any(one.effects != 'read_only') (src/redkraken/execution.py:3646). A body-borne blob therefore needs a Task selection that carries a non-read_only Playbook before it can be SENT at all, and it can never be a Test action. A cookie-borne blob is worse: identity.Session.inject sets owned = {static Identity header names} | {'cookie'} and removes the caller's Cookie before appending its own (src/redkraken/identity.py:334), and this Playbook's bb:triggers_all names authenticated_endpoint, so a leased Identity is the normal case. The QUERY-STRING and PATH-SEGMENT spellings of a serialised blob -- which is how ViewState, a signed state parameter and most base64 tokens actually travel -- are two urls and nothing else. The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226).

preconditions: reflected_parameter, redirect_target, web_surface. Refused on both halves. In OUR OWN headers it is excluded by construction: the egress header NAME pattern admits letters, digits and hyphens only, and the VALUE pattern admits printable ASCII from space to tilde, so CR, LF and every non-ASCII byte are unrepresentable. In a PARAMETER value the bytes are expressible and the arm is refused by decision.
baseline: The answers already collected. A route that builds a header from something the caller supplied is worth noticing, and that observation costs no request.
variant: n/a -- refused. The arm would carry a percent-encoded CR LF, or one of the overlong forms some decoders fold into control characters, or either doubly encoded for a hop that decodes twice.
control: n/a -- refused.
payload_family: control characters and their encodings.
runtime_writer: none. The observation goes in the Task note and is never promoted.
supported_evidence: none.
refuted_evidence: none.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: a split genuinely looks reachable from an answer already held. course of action: say so, quote the response header the value appeared in, and stop. scope: the whole run under this Playbook. resume: an operator decides whether a cache sits in front of that route, whether the Program's rules permit an arm that could poison it, and whether a maintenance window is needed. told: the operator who opened the Task, because that decision is theirs and not the run's. recorded: the header, the parameter, and the fact that nothing was sent.
owner_ticket: NEW: if response splitting is ever wanted it needs an operator-gated Playbook with a bounded blast radius, which this one cannot provide
notes: Four reasons and they are not interchangeable: the proof lands on the next caller and a poisoned cache entry has no undo; the non-cache arms still write a header into a person's browser; the encoding ladder is filter evasion, which establishes something about the filter rather than the application; and the interception proxy re-serialises every request, so where a control character survives our own egress is a property of the proxy and a positive result would be unattributable. One boundary the rewrite must NOT blur: a CR LF inside a body value bound for a MAIL header is a different question, is not excluded by the egress schema, and is filed in this ledger under authentication. REFUSAL UNCHANGED. Two independent reasons, and only one of them is policy: the Playbook's step 7 refuses response splitting, AND CR and LF cannot be spelled in our own header values at all -- the VALUE pattern is ^[\x20-\x7e]{0,1024}\Z, printable ASCII only. The refusal here is about a CR LF the APPLICATION writes into a header from a parameter we sent, which is expressible and is refused by decision.

preconditions: header_parameter, body_parameter, state_changing_method, api_surface or xml_request. A dispatcher that reads an operation name from somewhere other than the body it executes -- a SOAPAction header, a method-override form field, or one of the override header spellings. All the header names match the egress NAME pattern and their values are printable ASCII, so every spelling is expressible.
baseline: Both carriers naming the SAME permitted operation, and the answer recorded: which operation the response belongs to, and what it produced.
variant: The header naming the permitted operation and the body naming a different one. An answer that belongs to the body's operation while the header named the other is one component's check and another component's work.
control: Two. (1) BOTH carriers naming the restricted operation, which must be refused if the dispatcher checks anything at all; and, for the override spelling, the override set to a verb that does not exist, which must answer differently from a plain request -- if it answers identically the override is being ignored and the variant means nothing. (2) The baseline sent twice unchanged.
payload_family: operation and method names the application itself exposes, one per carrier.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 (close_test_replay) writes the response_differential from the body_differs/status_differs pair over the disagreeing arm and the both-restricted control.
supported_evidence: SPLIT BY CARRIER. The METHOD-OVERRIDE spelling in the QUERY -- `POST /x?_method=DELETE` against `DELETE /x` -- is response_differential written by close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) from the status_differs/body_differs pair: the method and the query are two of the things a Test action states. The DISPATCH-HEADER and BODY-ELEMENT spellings are reflected_input ({receipt,tool_run}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- the arm accepted and answered as one operation while producing the other's work, against a both-restricted control that was refused. NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- the arm is answered the way the both-restricted control is, so one component decided.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the arm is aimed at a verb a front end blocks, so the reading becomes 'did I get past the edge'. course of action: stop and hand it over -- one hop refusing what another serves is authorization.edge_rule and the Playbook is deployment. scope: this route. resume: an unfiltered route on the same application carries the same two carriers. told: the operator who opened the Task. recorded: both carriers verbatim, the operation each named, and anything the arm created.
owner_ticket: 211 -- A Test action carries the header and the body it plans (ready-for-agent, Blocked by: nothing). Needed only for the header and body spellings.
notes: New to the corpus: the shipped text is about parameter carriers and this is the same shape one layer up, on the name of the operation itself. The edge-bypass framing is deliberately excluded and routed to deployment, because 'a method the edge blocks arrives through an override' measures the edge; what stays here is a dispatcher and a handler reading one name differently with nothing in front of either. A second observation costing no request: the SameSite-Lax consequence -- an override turns a POST-only action into something a top-level GET navigation reaches -- belongs in the Task note for request-integrity. stop_conditions: halt trigger (observed condition): the inert re-spelling is accepted | course of action: stop; the guard is reacting to the encoding rather than to the declaration and the arm proves nothing | scope of halt: the route | resume condition: not resumed for this route | who is told: the operator, through mcp__rk2__park_for_human, with the halt trigger quoted verbatim | what is recorded: the Receipt label of every arm sent before the halt, which arm triggered it, and the verdict inconclusive carrying the trigger as its stated reason

notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: the parameter value is spelled in the query string or in the body, and both are now statable. The ceiling paragraph below is the pre-211 reading and is superseded. HIGH VALUE, unemitted class. This is the one place in the corpus where 'my payload got through' IS the finding rather than a precondition -- for injection.path getting through is the setup, for injection.parser_differential the disagreement is the property. Folds five mined rows (JSON comments, ....// single-pass strip, Matcher.matches()-vs-find() anchoring, email encoded-word, identifier-normalisation) into one reading. The identifier-normalisation arm -- a registration that treats two spellings as new and a lookup that treats them as one -- is the same disagreement over an identity table and is also the authentication.recovery_flow row below.  FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW STOPS AT AN OBSERVATION AND DOES NOT REACH A FINDING. Its differential lives in a request BODY document for the comment-truncation, encoded-word and punycode arms; the single-pass-strip arm can ride either the query string or the body. A Test action carries only {ordinal, role, kind, method, url} (roster.py:1184-1197), _Door.send passes only url and method to proxy.spend (replay.py:342-351) although proxy.spend accepts headers and body (proxy.py:4216-4224), and record_test_action compares a Receipt to an action over method, scheme, host, port and path alone (20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:1386-1391). THE CEILING IS PRICED AND OWED, NOT PERMANENT -- see owner_ticket. TICKET 211 ('A Test action carries the header and the body it plans', docs/specs/production-harness-v2/issues/211-a-test-action-carries-the-header-and-the-body-it-plans.md) removes exactly this rule, is Blocked by: nothing, is ready-for-agent, and ticket 101's own Blocked by line already names it. The price is small because the two expensive halves already exist: proxy.spend accepts a header mapping and a body today (proxy.py:4216-4224), and receipts.request_agent_sha already stores the agent-view request message (0005_artifacts_and_provenance.sql:59), so binding a plan to what was sent needs no new column. What is owed is rk2_test_spec_problem's action key set widening from five keys to seven (20260815T000000Z...:377), two keyword arguments in _Door.send (replay.py:342-351), two Arguments in the roster action element (roster.py:1184-1197), the header and body comparison in record_test_action (20260815T000000Z...:1383-1396), and the decision about what a read_only Playbook may put in a body (_body_allowed, execution.py:3646). SO THE PLAYBOOK PROSE MUST NOT BE WRITTEN TWICE: 00-todo-and-harness-gaps.md:31-33 records the ordering this repo already chose -- 'This is why the order is harness first. Adding state-of-the-art techniques to steps that cannot be executed would multiply the unrunnable part of the catalogue' -- and 211 says in as many words that writing 'this step stops at an Observation' into a third of the corpus would be 'a catalogue that describes attacks it cannot grade'. The '..%2f' and '..%252f' spellings of the same idea are NOT: '%2e' is refused case-insensitively anywhere in the url, and '..' is refused as a segment, even though origin_form() forwards both verbatim (proxy.py:818-828).  D3 (operator decision, rewrite/DECISIONS.md): a property class with no emitter is neither a missing execution path nor missing evidence, so capability_state stays 'reachable' and owner_ticket is 101 -- ticket 101 is the ticket that edits bb:outputs, so the gap closes inside it.

variant: The same name three times, each occurrence carrying a distinct value the application lists, sent in one order. preconditions: embedded_document, read_method, spa_surface. Each candidate must have a USE SITE inside the document -- which request it is attached to, in which header or parameter, against which host. A candidate whose use site is not in the document is one this reading cannot test and it stays a candidate. The route chosen is the safest the document offers: a GET, a listing, a profile, never one that writes, pays, sends or deletes.
baseline: The identical request with the credential omitted entirely. This is the control that makes the other half mean something: a route that answers the same to a bearer token and to no token at all was never checking.
variant: The same request with the candidate presented exactly as the document presents it. One pair per candidate, one pair only.
control: Two. (1) The omitted-credential half of every pair, including the pairs that produced no difference: a document with six matching strings of which one works is the ordinary case, and naming the five the target refused is what says the sixth was tested rather than recognised. (2) The omitted-credential request sent twice unchanged, because body_differs fires on the Date header alone and an anonymous listing is often a rotating page.
payload_family: candidate credential strings already present in the target's own document, presented once each, never varied.
runtime_writer: src/redkraken/replay.py:106 (close_test_replay) writes the response_differential from the status_differs/body_differs pair over the presented and omitted arms; src/redkraken/execution.py:518 (PROMOTE = "SELECT promote_proposal($1::uuid)"), whose LIVE definition is 20261008T000000Z__a_suggested_task_becomes_a_task_or_a_drop.sql:487 with the observations INSERT at :1116-1123 -- the 20260814T070000Z...:1631 definition is superseded, behaviour identical files the credential_effect Observations ({receipt}) this Playbook's bb:evidence requires on both the variant and the refutation.
supported_evidence: SPLIT BY CARRIER, and for this Playbook the split is decisive. Where the document presents the candidate as a QUERY PARAMETER -- `?api_key=`, `?token=`, the shape an SPA config actually ships for a keyed third-party route -- response_differential written by close_test_replay (src/redkraken/replay.py:106) from the status_differs/body_differs pair over the presented url and the omitted url: two urls, one method, no header and no body. Where the document presents it as an Authorization or x-api-key HEADER, credential_effect ({receipt}, 0018_vocabularies.sql:216-236), filed by the agent through promote_proposal -- the presented request succeeding where the omitted one did not -- a 200 against a 401, a document against an empty list, a named account against an anonymous one. NOT response_differential and NOT response_invariant: close_test_replay writes those two kinds only for actions of a Test it can replay, and this reading's arms are not Test actions. which is the kind this Playbook's own bb:evidence already requires on both the variant and the refutation.
refuted_evidence: response_invariant -- every candidate is answered exactly as no credential is, so the strings are samples, identifiers or public keys and the document discloses nothing.
stop_conditions: halt trigger: the only use site the document offers is a route that writes, pays, sends or deletes. course of action: stop and route to an operator -- the way to learn what a write credential is worth is to write with it, and that is their decision. scope: this candidate. resume: an operator names a read route the same credential reaches, or accepts the write. told: the operator who opened the Task, and where a candidate is live the Program contact early and plainly, because a key in a published bundle is fixed by rotating it and the target cannot start until they have been told. recorded: the stored document, both Artifacts of every pair, the candidate REDACTED to enough characters to identify it in the document, and the count of candidates that produced no difference.
owner_ticket: 211 -- A Test action carries the header and the body it plans (ready-for-agent, Blocked by: nothing). Needed for the header-borne presentation, which is most of them.
notes: The Playbook's core, and credential_effect is filable: promote_proposal inserts the kind the agent named and the vocabulary row allows {receipt}, which each half of the pair produces. The raw value lives only in the stored Artifact, which is what the evidence bundle redacts on export. FINDING PATH -- THIS ROW REACHES A FINDING. Its differential lives in the QUERY STRING, wherever the document itself puts the candidate there -- the presented url against the omitted url, which is what a Test action can state. A Test action states a method and a url and the checker accepts both (rk2_test_request_problem, 20260815T000000Z__a_test_runs_through_the_replay_lane.sql:199-226), and record_test_action compares method, scheme, host, port and path -- the query is deliberately not compared because only its digest is on the Receipt (same file, :1375-1391), so a query-borne differential rides through intact. The header-borne presentation, which is the commoner one, stops at an agent-filed credential_effect. The whole Test lane is bodiless and headerless: setup, actions and cleanup all route through _sent (src/redkraken/replay.py:456-466) to _Door.send (src/redkraken/replay.py:342-351), which calls proxy.spend with url and method and NOTHING ELSE, although proxy.spend accepts headers= and body= (src/redkraken/proxy.py:4216-4226). notes: TICKET 211 RE-PASS: nothing is sent; the row files a content_match over stored material. The ceiling paragraph below still holds. This row exists because secrets is one of the ten Playbooks that name only kinds an earlier card called writer-less, and the defect is the PROSE: the shipped step 2 says 'out of the stored document, list every string that could be a credential' and never says which of the four binaries produces the content_match its own bb:evidence requires.
